docs.title: Collaboration
docs.text:
Real-time multi-editor sessions over TCP with msgpack framing: several humans, one project, live cursors, cameras, selections and gizmo operations.

What syncs live: peer cursors and viewport cameras, entity selections, gizmo drag operations, scene snapshots on demand, asset changes via the file watcher, open tabs, script contents with per-peer cursors and operational-transform edits.

Entry points (core/network/collab/*, core/network/client.py, core/network/serverp/* — no single collaboration.py):

  • CollabServer (serverp/base.py + connection.py): hosts the room — set_password / set_room / set_max_clients, _auth_ok room+token check, peer registry with join/leave callbacks (set_peer_joined_callback, set_peer_left_callback in collab/presence.py), scene snapshot serving (set_scene_snapshot_callback), broadcast of remote scene/tab/script events.
  • CollabClient (core/network/client.py): joins — connect(host, port, name, password, room), set_on_auth_failed / set_on_connected / set_on_disconnected, send() + poll_messages(); script domain senders for open/change/cursor (send_script_open/change/cursor in collab/script_sync.py), receivers for remote scene open, tab switch/close, script ops.
  • Background _PollThread (collab/poll.py) drains the socket without blocking the editor; _AssetWatcher (collab/watcher.py) pushes file changes.
  • CollaborationManager (collab/manager.py, 449 lines, editor side) owns state sync (start_server(host, port, password, room), connect(...), host_relay / join_relay, create_invite / create_lan_invite / join_invite, stop), peer discovery and disconnect timeouts; the panel exposes host/join, peer list and kick.

Session flow: host starts CollabServer from the collaboration panel → peers join with the address → each peer's camera and cursor appear as RemoteCollaborator gizmos → edits broadcast as operations → conflicts resolve by operation order, snapshots heal divergence.

Etiquette that prevents pain: one peer owns a scene subtree at a time (selection broadcast shows who); heavy reimports pause for a countdown; script conflicts prefer the operation stream over copy-paste overwrites.

Troubleshooting: peer invisible → firewall or wrong address; edits lost → divergence beyond op-stream, request a fresh snapshot via set_on_scene_sync; high latency → asset watcher flooding on huge imports, exclude build/cache dirs.

Related: RemoteCollaborator (peer gizmos), Transport and Protocol (wire layer), VCS panel (commit the collaborated result).

docs.title: NetworkAnimator
docs.text:
Animation-state sync: which clip, at what time, speed and playing flag — plus gameplay parameters.

Inspector group / field Meaning Sync: Sync Clip / Time / Speed / Playing Channel toggles — idle loops need clip only Network Animator: Authority AnimatorAuthority Send Rate Updates per second Sync Params Named parameter set (bools, floats, triggers by snapshot)

API: apply_snapshot(data) remote write; trigger(name), set_float(name, value), set_bool(name, value) — local calls that replicate to remotes.

Bandwidth wisdom: sync clip + playing at low rate for ambient characters; add time sync only where foot-sync matters (dance, marching); params carry gameplay truth (aim blends, hurt flags) while clip names carry visuals. Triggers are fire-and-forget — the snapshot carries them once, so trigger during a send tick or force a send.

Fighting-game note: time sync at full rate is expensive; prefer deterministic playback (same start event + same clock) and sync only triggers and params.

Troubleshooting: T-pose on remotes → clip name mismatch (different asset names per build); desynced dance → time channel off; stuck trigger → sent between ticks and never snapshot, force on trigger.

Related: NetworkIdentity, Animation Clips and Animator, NetworkVariables (params twin).

docs.title: NetworkIdentity
docs.text:
Network existence card for an entity: who it is on the wire, who owns it, which prefab to instantiate remotely, whether it survives scene changes.

Inspector group / field Meaning Network Identity: Net ID Session-unique id, assigned on spawn Owner ID Peer id with write authority Prefab ID Which prefab remotes instantiate Authority AuthorityMode — owner-driven or server-authoritative Is Local Player This peer's avatar flag Dont Destroy Survive scene loads (managers, session state)

API: transfer_ownership(peer_id), request_ownership(), apply_owner_change(...) — handoff protocol for pickups, vehicles and dropped items.

Authority model: owner-driven components (transform, variables) accept writes from the Owner ID peer; server-authoritative flows route through the host. AuthorityMode on the component selects the posture per entity — players owner-driven, doors and scores server-side.

Every networked prefab needs exactly one NetworkIdentity at its root; sync components (transform, rigidbody, animator, variables) attach alongside and key off the Net ID. Is Local Player gates input scripts — same prefab, only the owner reads keys.

Ownership handoff pattern: driver enters car → request_ownership() → host approves → transfer_ownership(driver) → car transform follows the driver until exit hands it back.

Troubleshooting: duplicates on remotes → prefab id mismatch or missing identity on root; input on all clones → Is Local Player gate missing; handoff ignored → request sent to non-authority, route via host.

Related: NetworkManager (spawns assign ids), NetworkTransform/Rigidbody/Animator/Variables (sync off this id), NetworkPlayer (peer data twin).

docs.title: NetworkManager
docs.text:
Session component: one per scene, owns hosting, joining, player spawns, despawns and RPC fan-out at entity level.

Inspector group / field Meaning Network Manager: Port Listen/connect port, default 7777 Max Players Room cap Server Name Lobby display name Host Address Last/preset join target Player Prefab Spawned per connection Auto Spawn Player Spawn on join without script Tick Rate Sync ticks per second Show Debug Overlay session state

Lifecycle API: host(), connect(), disconnect() (mirror the plugin, scoped to this scene via NetworkManagerTransportMixin); on_awake registers the instance and existing identities, on_update polls the shared Transport deque and dispatches by MessageType, on_destroy clears the singleton instance (does not disconnect — call disconnect() explicitly).

Gameplay API (verified in netmgr/transport.py + netmgr/sync.py):

  • spawn_prefab(prefab_path, pos=None, rot=None, owner_id=None) / spawn_entity(entity, owner_id=None) — authoritative spawn control; spawned entities carry NetworkIdentity with prefab ids so remotes instantiate the same prefab.
  • despawn(net_id: int) / despawn_entity(entity: Entity) — authoritative despawn by net id (server broadcasts NET_DESPAWN; client request goes to server).
  • send_rpc(net_id: int, method: str, args: dict | None = None, target: int | None = None) — component-level remote call (NET_RPC {"net_id", "method", "args", "target?"}); server may send_to(target) unicast, otherwise broadcast.

Setup: exactly one active manager per scene (two managers fight over the transport). Tick rate trades bandwidth for freshness — 10–20 Hz for lobbies and strategy, 30–60 for shooters; thresholds on sync components matter more than raw ticks.

Troubleshooting: double spawns → two managers or auto-spawn plus manual spawn; despawn mismatch → despawn by id, never by local reference; RPC silent → handler registered after poll started, or name typo.

Related: Network Plugin (transport wiring), NetworkIdentity (spawned ids), NetworkSpawn (prefab pools), NetworkPlayer (per-peer data).

docs.title: NetworkPlayer
docs.text:
Per-peer avatar data: name, id, team, ready flag and score — the lobby row as a component.

Inspector group / field Meaning Network Player: Player Name Display name Player ID Session peer id mirror Team Team index or name Is Ready Lobby ready flag Score Replicated score counter

API: set_ready(bool), add_score(n), set_team(t), set_name(s), apply_vars(data) snapshot path, on_awake registration.

Lobby flow: join → spawn avatar with NetworkPlayer → client sets name/team → set_ready(True) → host counts readies → match starts. Score flows through add_score so kills, captures and assists accumulate server-side without client trust.

Is Local Player on the sibling NetworkIdentity gates input; NetworkPlayer carries the social data. Keep them on the same prefab root — split roots desync name from body.

Troubleshooting: all names default → set_name never called or applied before spawn finished; ready ignored → host counts a different component, wire to this one; score resets → snapshot overwrites local adds, add only via API on authority.

Related: NetworkIdentity (Is Local Player gate), NetworkManager (join/spawn flow), NetworkVariables (score replication twin).

docs.title: Network Plugin
docs.text:
System plugin (SYSTEM = True) wiring gameplay code to the real transport: host, connect, message handlers and per-frame polling over core.network.transp get_transport() (GameServer / GameClient over TCP, msgpack MessageType framing).

plug = engine.plugins.get("NetworkPlugin")
plug.host(port=7777, max_players=16)
plug.connect("192.168.1.10", 7777)
plug.on_message("chat", handle_chat)
plug.broadcast("chat", {"text": "hello"})
plug.poll()

API, verified:

API Signature / meaning host host(port=7777, max_players=16) -> bool — get_transport().host("0.0.0.0", port, max_players), logs the result connect connect(host, port=7777) -> bool — get_transport().connect(host, port, "Player"), logs the result disconnect disconnect() — get_transport().disconnect(); also runs on plugin shutdown send send(msg_type, payload, target_id=-1) — send_to(target_id, NET_RPC, ...) when target_id >= 0 and server, else broadcast; payload wrapped as {"rpc": name, "payload": dict} broadcast broadcast(msg_type, payload) — broadcast(NET_RPC, {"rpc": name, "payload": dict}) to all peers on_message on_message(msg_type, handler) — subscribe; handler receives NetworkMessage(msg_type, payload, sender_id); "*" gets everything unhandled poll poll() — get_transport().poll(), dispatch NET_RPC {"rpc": ...} frames to handlers (handler exceptions logged, never raised), requeue the rest to the front State is_connected, is_server, local_id, peer_count — direct reads of get_transport()

Usage: one handler per message name, validate payload before use, "*" handler as the unknown-message logger. Call poll() once per frame from game code or a manager component — undrained queues read as dead peers. NetworkManager.on_update() already polls the same Transport deque and forwards NET_RPC {"rpc": ...} frames to this plugin, so do not run both pumps blindly.

def handle_chat(msg):
    line = str(msg.payload.get("text", ""))
    Logger.info("chat from " + str(msg.sender_id) + ": " + line)

plug.on_message("chat", handle_chat)
plug.on_message("*", log_unknown)

Limits: TCP-only transport (no UDP/WebRTC/ENet); client send always goes to the server, targeted delivery is server-side send_to; no gameplay password/room/auth; 4 MiB per-frame cap (MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE).

Related: Transport and Protocol, NetworkManager (component-level sessions), NetworkVariables (state sync twin of RPC events).

Verified against: plugins/network_plugin.py:13-17,33-62,64-84,94-116,118-180,182-188; core/network/transp/transport.py:82-144; core/network/protocol.py:80-91,97-110.

docs.title: NetworkRigidbody
docs.text:
Physics-state sync: velocities travel alongside transforms so remotes extrapolate rather than chase.

Inspector group / field Meaning Sync: Sync Velocity / Sync Angular Velocity channel toggles Network Rigidbody: Authority RigidbodyAuthority — usually the simulating peer or host Send Rate Updates per second Vel Threshold Minimum velocity change worth sending Interpolate / Interp Delay Remote smoothing twin of the transform settings

Reads in on_fixed_update (physics clock) and writes visually in on_update — sync follows the same split as simulation, so no half-step tearing.

Pairing rule: always attach alongside NetworkTransform on dynamic bodies. Transform alone makes remotes chase with position-only correction (swimming look); velocities let remotes coast ballistically between snapshots — the difference between playable and drunk driving.

Authority posture: owner-simulated (driver owns the car, host trusts) for responsiveness; host-simulated for competitive integrity (host integrates, all render). Thresholds hide idle jitter; teleport on the transform handles respawns.

Troubleshooting: orbiting remotes → velocity without position sync, pair both; explosions of energy on catch-up → interp delay too low, raise; host/client disagree on stacks → single authority only, never two writers.

Related: NetworkTransform (position twin), Rigidbody (local API), NetworkIdentity (authority source), Solver and Threading (fixed-step source).

docs.title: NetworkSpawn
docs.text:
Prefab pools and spawn points: what may spawn, where, and who triggers it.

Inspector group / field Meaning Network Spawn: Spawnable Prefabs Whitelist of prefab ids this spawner may instantiate Spawn On Start Populate on scene start Spawn Radius Random disc around the spawner Randomize Rotation Yaw variety per spawn

API: spawn(prefab_id) at the spawner, spawn_by_path(path) for dynamic content, spawn_player(peer) wiring a connection to its avatar; on_start handles the initial population.

Whitelists are security: remotes can only request listed prefabs, so a hacked client cannot spawn admin objects. Spawn Radius decorrelates clustered spawns (mob packs, loot bursts); randomize rotation breaks visual repetition.

Patterns: player spawner (one per team base, spawn_player on join), wave spawner (timer script calling spawn per interval), loot spawner (spawn on enemy death event), vehicle pad (spawn on interact, despawn on abandon).

Authoritative flow: request → host validates prefab + cooldown + cap → spawn_prefab → NetworkIdentity assigns Net ID → remotes instantiate by prefab id. Never trust client-side spawn calls directly.

Troubleshooting: spawns nothing → prefab missing from whitelist; wrong prefab on remotes → prefab id mismatch across builds; spawn storms → no cooldown or cap, add both.

Related: NetworkManager (spawn_prefab/despawn), NetworkIdentity (ids + prefab ids), Prefabs (authoring), NetworkPlayer (player wiring).

docs.title: NetworkTransform
docs.text:
Bandwidth-thrifty transform sync: which axes travel, how often, how remotes smooth, when to snap.

Inspector group / field Meaning Sync: Sync Position / Rotation / Scale Per-channel toggles — static props sync nothing Network Transform: Authority TransformAuthority — who may write Send Rate Updates per second for this entity Pos / Rot Threshold Minimum change worth sending (dead reckoning cutoff) Interpolate Smooth remote motion between snapshots Interp Delay Buffer delay hiding jitter (higher = smoother + later) Teleport Threshold Distance snap: beyond it, snap instead of gliding

API: apply_snapshot(data) — remote write path; teleport(position) — snap locally and remotely; motion itself is read in on_update from the Transform.

Tuning per archetype: players — position+rotation at 20–30 Hz, small thresholds, interpolate on with ~100 ms delay; crates — position only at 5–10 Hz, coarse thresholds; static doors — nothing until moved, then a teleport; camera-followed racers — higher rate, lower delay.

Thresholds beat raw rates: a 10 Hz stream with tight thresholds often moves less data than 30 Hz with zero thresholds on idle-heavy scenes. Teleport threshold prevents cross-map gliding on respawn — set it near the level's room size.

Troubleshooting: rubber-banding → delay too low for the jitter, raise interp delay; moonwalking (rotation lag) → rotation threshold too coarse; snap on stairs → teleport threshold below step distances, raise; frozen remotes → authority mismatch, writes rejected.

Related: NetworkIdentity (id + authority), NetworkRigidbody (physics twin), NetworkManager (tick rate ceiling).

docs.title: NetworkVariables
docs.text:
Replicated key-value state for gameplay truth: health, scores, door flags, match phase, inventory counts.

Inspector group / field Meaning Network Variables: Authority VariableAuthority — who may write Send Rate Cap on update frequency Reliable Ordered guaranteed delivery vs latest-only Sync On Change Send only deltas, never full state per tick

API: set_var(key, value), set_vars(dict), remove_var(key), apply_snapshot(data); dirty keys flush in on_update.

Reliable vs fast: health and scores use reliable (every change must land); crosshair-aim-style rapid values use unreliable latest-only (stale data is worse than lost data). Sync-on-change turns idle entities silent — a hundred quiet doors cost nothing.

vars = self._entity.get_component_by_name("NetworkVariables")
if vars:
    vars.set_var("hp", 75)
    vars.set_vars({"ammo": 12, "shield": True})

Design rule: variables carry truth, RPCs carry events. Door opened (state) → variable; door slammed with a bang (moment) → RPC + variable. Reading truth from events replays history wrong on late joiners; snapshots fix them instantly.

Troubleshooting: late joiner sees defaults → variable never snapshotted, force full sync on join; oscillating values → two writers, fix authority; flood → sync-on-change off with per-tick sets.

Related: NetworkManager.send_rpc (events twin), NetworkPlayer (score patterns), NetworkIdentity (authority).

docs.title: Networking Overview
docs.text:
Two independent subsystems share core/network (TCP + msgpack framing):

  • Gameplay netcode (components + NetworkManager + NetworkPlugin) — implemented, real transport calls. host() / connect() / send() / broadcast() / poll() / on_message() in plugins/network_plugin.py delegate to the core.network.transp get_transport() singleton (GameServer / GameClient over TCP, MessageType framing). Syncs entities across a session: transforms, rigidbodies, animator state, variables, spawns, RPCs; authority per component (server / owner).
  • Editor collaboration (CollabServer / CollabClient in core/network/serverp/* and core/network/client.py, CollaborationManager in core/network/collab/*): live cursors, cameras, selections, gizmo ops, scene snapshots, asset watch, co-edited scripts. Password rooms, relay and UPnP helpers belong to this path, not to gameplay.

Limits (gameplay path): TCP only, no UDP/WebRTC/ENet (asyncio.start_server / asyncio.open_connection with TCP_NODELAY); no password/room/auth on GameServer (JOIN handshake + max_players check only); MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE 4 MiB per frame; the server relays only NET_TRANSFORM / NET_RIGIDBODY / NET_ANIMATOR / NET_VARIABLES / NET_RPC / NET_SNAPSHOT to other peers; poll() must run every frame — one pump (plugin or manager), they share a single Transport deque.

Pages: Transport and Protocol, Network Plugin, NetworkManager, NetworkIdentity, NetworkTransform, NetworkRigidbody, NetworkAnimator, NetworkVariables, NetworkSpawn, NetworkPlayer, Collaboration, RemoteCollaborator.

First session recipe: empty scene → NetworkManager entity (port 7777, player prefab assigned, auto spawn on) → player prefab with NetworkIdentity + NetworkTransform + NetworkPlayer → host on one machine, connect from another → both spawns appear and move.

Related: Transport and Protocol (wire details), Network Plugin (RPC events), NetworkManager (session dispatch).

Verified against: plugins/network_plugin.py:64-180 (host/connect/send/broadcast/on_message/poll); core/network/transp/transport.py:82-144; core/network/transp/server.py:62-66,108-116,140-160,248; core/network/transp/client.py:58-64,91-129; core/network/protocol.py:80-110; core/config/constants.py:20-21; core/network/serverp/base.py:80-87,174-189 (password/room/auth are collab-only). No open markers in core/network/transp/*, plugins/network_plugin.py, core/components/network/* (grep).

docs.title: RemoteCollaborator
docs.text:
In-editor visual stand-in for a remote peer: where they look, what they hold selected, what they drag.

A 46-line component (core/components/network/remote_collaborator.py) with no custom _inspector_fields — presence is the data (identity lives in peer_id / peer_name / color, persisted via serialize/deserialize). It renders gizmo_lines / gizmo_meshes every frame: a square marker plus stem at the peer transform in the peer's color (gizmo_meshes returns []).

Peers appear when collaboration connects and vanish on disconnect timeout; the CollaborationManager owns the mapping from peer id to entity. Colors stay stable per peer within a session so teams learn who is who.

Use while co-editing: follow the frustum to see what your partner stages, avoid grabbing their selected subtree, watch their gizmo drag before it lands to catch mistakes early.

Troubleshooting: peer missing → not connected or timed out; stale pose → op-stream stalled, check latency; wrong color → session rejoined, colors reassign.

Related: Collaboration (sessions), NetworkPlayer (gameplay twin of peer data), Gizmos and Icons (rendering passes).

docs.title: Transport and Protocol
docs.text: Wire layer under gameplay netcode and collaboration: TCP sockets, 4-byte big-endian length prefix + msgpack frames, typed messages, per-frame drain.

docs.title: Gameplay transport (core/network/transp/, singleton via get_transport())
docs.text: API Signature / meaning host host(host="0.0.0.0", port=7777, max_players=16) -> bool — starts GameServer in a thread, resets role to server, local_id = 0 connect connect(host="127.0.0.1", port=7777, name="Player") -> bool — starts GameClient, sends JOIN {"name"}, waits up to 5 s, returns False on NET_KICK disconnect disconnect() — stops client/server, clears the queue, role back to "none" send send(msg_type, data) — client → server; on server role acts as broadcast send_to send_to(peer_id, msg_type, data) — server → one peer; on client role falls back to send to server broadcast broadcast(msg_type, data) — alias of send (server fans out to all peers) poll poll() -> list[(msg_type, data)] — drain incoming without blocking; call every frame peek / get_peers peek() non-destructive read; get_peers() -> [{id, name}] on server State is_connected, is_server, is_client, local_id (server 0, client = assigned peer id), peer_count, bytes_sent, bytes_received Caps / callbacks set_max_players(n) lives on GameServer, not on Transport; set_on_connected / set_on_disconnected live on GameClient, not on Transport

docs.title: Protocol (core/network/protocol.py, core/config/constants.py)
docs.text:
• Framing: make_msg(msg_type, data) packs msgpack {"t": int, "d": dict} with a ">I" length prefix; FRAME_HEADER_SIZE = 4; payloads over MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (4 MiB) raise instead of sending; parse_msg is the inverse.
  • MessageType IntEnum: gameplay range NET_SPAWN = 100, NET_DESPAWN = 101, NET_SPAWN_REQUEST = 102, NET_RPC = 103, NET_TRANSFORM = 104, NET_RIGIDBODY = 105, NET_ANIMATOR = 106, NET_OWNER_CHANGE = 107, NET_VARIABLES = 108, NET_READY = 109, NET_KICK = 110, NET_SNAPSHOT = 111 (collaboration types occupy 1–55, 210–212).
  • RPC shapes: plugin events travel as NET_RPC {"rpc": name, "payload": {...}} with the server stamping _sender before dispatch; component calls travel as NET_RPC {"net_id", "method", "args", "rpc_type", "target?"} via rpc.send_server_rpc / send_client_rpc / send_target_rpc.

docs.title: Collaboration transport (separate path, do not confuse)
docs.text: CollabServer (core/network/serverp/base.py, connection.py): set_password / set_room / set_max_clients, _auth_ok (room + token check), update_scene_data. CollabClient (core/network/client.py): connect(host, port, name, password, room), set_on_auth_failed. Relay (core/network/relayp/) and UPnP (core/network/upnpp/) helpers serve this path. Gameplay GameServer has none of that: first frame must be JOIN, over-capacity peers get NET_KICK {"reason": "server_full"} and the socket closes.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
TCP only — asyncio.start_server / asyncio.open_connection with TCP_NODELAY, so high-rate state pays head-of-line blocking; no UDP channel, no encryption, no gameplay-side auth. The server relays only transform/rigidbody/animator/variables/RPC/snapshot to other peers; spawn requests, ownership changes and despawns are consumed by NetworkManager. Transport.send on a server broadcasts — targeted delivery needs send_to; a client cannot unicast, it always sends to the server. NetworkPlugin.poll() and NetworkManager.on_update() drain the same singleton deque, so run one pump per frame (the manager forwards NET_RPC {"rpc": ...} frames to the plugin).

Usage: host() once on the host machine, connect() on joiners, then poll() every frame and dispatch by MessageType. Keep payloads flat and tiny (ids, positions, enums); large transfers go through split_chunks (CHUNK) or snapshots, never per-frame whole scenes.

Troubleshooting: connect refused → server not started or port blocked/firewalled; kicked at join → server_full; silent peers → poll() not called each frame or two pumps fighting over one queue; oversize send → ValueError, split the payload.

Related: Network Plugin (gameplay wiring), NetworkManager (session component), Collaboration (editor sessions), RPC usage in NetworkManager.send_rpc.

Verified against: core/network/transp/transport.py:39-80,82-157; core/network/transp/server.py:59-66,108-124,140-160,223-263,269-317; core/network/transp/client.py:52-64,91-129,148-186; core/network/protocol.py:26-111,147-163; core/network/rpc.py:72-105; core/config/constants.py:20-21; core/network/serverp/base.py:80-87,174-189,233-234; core/components/network/netmgr/manager.py:124-172.

docs.title: Collaboration Protocol
docs.text: Editor co-editing sessions: a host plus guests share cursors, cameras, selections, gizmos, scene edits, scripts and assets. Separate path from gameplay netcode — string peer ids (peer_<12hex>), rooms, password auth. Implemented by CollaborationManager (core/network/collab/manager.py + presence.py / poll.py / watcher.py / scene_sync.py / script_sync.py / asset_sync.py / upnp.py).

docs.title: Server, client, auth
docs.text:
CollabServer(host="0.0.0.0", port=9876, password="", room="", max_clients=32, heartbeat_timeout=20.0) (serverp/base.py:47-62, default direct port DEFAULT_DIRECT_PORT = 9876). First frame must be JOIN; over capacity answers NET_KICK {"reason": "server_full"}; then _auth_ok checks the room (must match when the server sets one) and the password — token = sha256(room + "\x00" + password) or the plain password — replying AUTH_FAIL {"reason": "auth"} on mismatch; clients newer than PROTOCOL_VERSION + 2 get AUTH_FAIL {"reason": "version"} (serverp/base.py:174-189, serverp/connection.py:36-96). Each peer gets a rotating color; joins fan out as PEER_JOINED, the newcomer receives JOINED {your_id, your_color, peers, scene, version, room}; leaves fan out as LEAVE. Guards: 400 msgs/s per-peer rate limit, 5 s stale sweeper vs heartbeat_timeout, PING→PONG, TCP_NODELAY everywhere.

CollabClient.connect(host, port, name, password="", room="", timeout=8.0) sends _make_join = {name, version, room, token} with TCP_NODELAY + SO_KEEPALIVE; wait_connected(timeout) resolves id vs auth error (client.py:77-104,182-189). set_password / set_room / set_max_clients reconfigure the server live; update_scene_data(scene) stores the snapshot served to newcomers (serverp/base.py:80-87,233-234).

docs.title: Presence, scenes, scripts, assets
docs.text:
PresenceMixin (collab/presence.py): send_cursor(x, y, hit?), send_camera(pos, fwd, up), send_gizmo_state(mode, hover_axis, dragging); oversize payloads auto-split into CHUNK frames (_send_link / _send_chunked). Remote state lands on RemotePeer fields: cursor_screen / cursor_hit, camera_pos/_fwd/_up, selected_entity_ids, gizmo_mode/_hover_axis/_dragging, current_tab (collab/models.py:9-34). Default cadences in CollabSettings: cursor 1/30 s, camera 1/15 s, transform 1/20 s, gizmo 1/10 s, ping 3 s, poll 8 ms, scene sync 2 s (collab/models.py:35-52).

Scene edits (scene_sync.py + server _route_message): send_entity_create/delete/transform/selection/component_update/component_sync/component_add/component_remove/play_mode, each rebroadcast under its *_UPDATE/*_CREATED/… pair with the sender id stamped, plus SCENE_OPEN / SCENE_TAB_SWITCH / SCENE_TAB_CLOSE tab tracking, request_scene_snapshot() → server answers SCENE_SNAPSHOT to the requester only, and _send_full_scene_sync(target) replays entities + transforms to a new peer. Script co-editing (script_sync.py): send_script_open/change/cursor(pos, sel_anchor, sel_end)/ops with set_on_remote_script_* callbacks. Assets (asset_sync.py + watcher.py): request_asset_list / send_asset_list(target) (paths + sha256 checksums) / send_asset_file / send_asset_request; _AssetWatcher polls mtimes (interval ≥ 0.5 s) and fires change/delete callbacks.

Polling (poll.py): _PollThread(callback, interval_ms, stop_event) daemon loops drive _poll_messages, _send_ping and _sweep_peers from the manager.

docs.title: Example session
docs.text:
mgr.start_server(host="0.0.0.0", port=9876, password="s3cret", room="LEVEL1")
invite = mgr.create_invite(public=True)          # "ZARIN1:..." (external IP when UPnP mapped)
mgr.join_invite(invite, name="Guest", password="s3cret")  # guest side: direct or relay by mode
mgr.send_cursor(x, y, hit_pos)                   # presence, ~30 Hz
mgr.send_script_change("scripts/player.py", text)
mgr.request_scene_snapshot()                     # full scene pull
mgr.stop()                                       # clears peers, watchers, UPnP mappings

Related: Relay and UPnP (rooms/invites/NAT), Message Types (frame format), RemoteCollaborator (in-scene avatars).

docs.title: Gameplay Message Types (NET_*)
docs.text: Wire IDs for gameplay netcode: MessageType IntEnum in core/network/protocol.py:80-91. Values 100–111; collaboration types occupy 1–55 and 210–212.

docs.title: Frame format
docs.text: make_msg(msg_type, data) packs msgpack {"t": int(msg_type), "d": dict} and prepends a ">I" (big-endian uint32) length prefix; parse_msg is the inverse, pack_frame / unpack_frame are aliases. FRAME_HEADER_SIZE = 4, MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE = 4 MiB — oversize payloads raise ValueError instead of sending. Large transfers go through split_chunks (CHUNK) instead of one frame.

docs.title: Server intake vs relay
docs.text: Every client frame first passes GameServer._client_loop: only the allowlisted types are queued locally with a _sender stamp (server.py:232-247). Of those, only transform/rigidbody/animator/variables/RPC/snapshot are fanned out to other peers (server.py:248-263). Spawn requests, ownership changes, despawns and ready flags are consumed by NetworkManager, never relayed. Related handshake types: first frame must be JOIN, answered with JOINED; disconnects fan out as LEAVE; PING is answered with PONG inline and never queued.

docs.title: Type table
docs.text:
Type Value Purpose (one line) Who sends / relay NET_SPAWN 100 Server announces a new entity {net_id, owner_id, prefab_id, entity} Server broadcast (or send_to for a late joiner via _sync_new_peer); clients apply via _handle_spawn NET_DESPAWN 101 Remove entity {net_id} Server broadcasts, client sends as a request to server; accepted by server but not relayed NET_SPAWN_REQUEST 102 Client asks server to spawn {prefab_id, entity, requester, pos?, rot?} Client → server only; server-only _handle_spawn_request, never relayed NET_RPC 103 Remote call, two shapes: plugin {"rpc", "payload"} or component {"net_id", "method", "args", "rpc_type", "target?"} Both directions; relayed to other peers; see RPC Reference NET_TRANSFORM 104 Transform state {net_id, t, seq, p?, r?, s?} Authority side broadcasts; relayed; applied via NetworkTransform.apply_snapshot NET_RIGIDBODY 105 Physics state {net_id, t, seq, v?, w?} Authority side broadcasts (from on_fixed_update); relayed; applied via NetworkRigidbody.apply_snapshot NET_ANIMATOR 106 Animator state {net_id, t, seq, clip?, time?, speed?, playing?, params?, trigger?} Authority side broadcasts; relayed; applied via NetworkAnimator.apply_snapshot NET_OWNER_CHANGE 107 Ownership transfer; client sends {requester}, server rebroadcasts {net_id, owner_id} Client → server → broadcast; accepted by server but not auto-relayed NET_VARIABLES 108 Synced vars {net_id, vars, t, seq} (legacy data key also read) Authority side broadcasts; relayed; applied via NetworkVariables.apply_snapshot or generic setattr fallback NET_READY 109 Reserved ready flag Accepted and queued by the server, not relayed, no built-in NetworkManager branch NET_KICK 110 Force-disconnect {reason}, e.g. server_full on over-capacity join Server → one peer, then closes the socket; Transport.connect returns False when it sees one NET_SNAPSHOT 111 Reserved whole-world snapshot channel Accepted and relayed like state channels; no built-in emitter or consumer — user payloads

Related: Transport Internals (framing on the wire), RPC Reference (NET_RPC shapes), Snapshots and Interpolation (state channels).

docs.title: Relay and UPnP (NAT Traversal)
docs.text: Two ways to connect peers that cannot reach each other directly: a WebSocket relay room, or a UPnP port mapping on the local gateway. Both serve the collaboration path (CollaborationManager); gameplay GameServer has neither.

docs.title: Relay (core/network/relayp/)
docs.text:
RelayServer(host="0.0.0.0", port=8765, max_rooms=256, max_peers_per_room=32) speaks WebSocket + msgpack (max_size 8 MiB, ping 20 s): start_sync(timeout) / stop_sync() run it on a daemon thread (relayp/server.py:19-105). Default port constant is DEFAULT_RELAY_PORT = 8765. The server routes typed payloads with _route_pair (e.g. CURSOR → CURSOR_UPDATE, ENTITY_CREATE → ENTITY_CREATED) and speaks ops join / welcomed / fail / data {"op","to","t","d"} / peer_joined / peer_left / ping / pong.

RelayClient.connect(relay_url, room, name="User", password="", timeout=10.0) normalizes the URL (ws:// prepended when missing) and the room code, derives token = sha256(room + "\x00" + password) when a password is set, and sends a join hello (relayp/client.py:78-99,175-212). welcomed stores the string peer_id and queues JOINED {your_id, your_color, peers, room, version}; fail queues AUTH_FAIL and fires on_auth_failed; remote traffic arrives as data frames queued by type, joins/leaves as PEER_JOINED / LEAVE. send(msg_type, data) wraps into the data envelope (optional target key selects a peer) and refuses payloads over 7 MiB; poll_messages() drains; wait_connected(timeout) blocks until id + auth state resolve.

Manager wiring (collab/manager.py:194-294): host_relay(relay_url, room="", ...) generates a 6-char room code when empty and returns it; join_relay(relay_url, room, ...) joins as guest; create_invite(public=True) builds a ZARIN1: invite — relay mode when connected via relay, otherwise a direct invite (public + UPnP-mapped prefers the external IP); join_invite(code, name, password="") parses the invite (v, mode, host/port or relay, room, locked) and connects accordingly. Invite helpers: make_invite / parse_invite, build_direct_invite / build_relay_invite, PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2 (protocol.py:18-23,180-215).

mgr.host_relay("ws://relay.example.com:8765", room="", password="s3cret", name="Host")
code = mgr.create_invite()          # "ZARIN1:..." -> share it
mgr.join_invite(code, name="Guest", password="s3cret")  # other side

docs.title: UPnP (core/network/upnpp/, collab/upnp.py)
docs.text:
UpnpMapper(lease=3600) discovers gateways over SSDP and maps ports: map_port(external, internal=None, protocol="TCP", description="ZarinEngine", try_alternatives=True, timeout=10.0) tries external … external+16, skips in-use mappings (fault 718), and returns {ok, external, internal, protocol, external_ip, error}; unmap_port(external, protocol) / unmap_all() remove mappings; a background thread renews leases at lease/2 (upnpp/mapper.py:175-339).

The collaboration mixin automates this: start_server maps the port when bound to 0.0.0.0 and settings.upnp_enabled (default True, lease 3600); status is a dict with state in idle / discovering / mapped / failed / disabled plus external_ip / external_port / gateway / error (collab/upnp.py:108-145). Extras: refresh_upnp(), map_extra_port(port), unmap_extra_port(port); stopping clears mappings.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
Direct connect works on LAN or with a reachable public IP (connect(host, port, ...)). Behind NAT without router access, use the relay (host_relay / join_relay) — no inbound ports needed, at the cost of routing all traffic through the relay host. When you control the router but lack a static IP, enable UPnP and share create_invite(public=True) so guests get the mapped external endpoint.

Related: Collaboration Protocol (sessions), Message Types (invite/auth types), Transport Internals (direct path).

docs.title: RPC Reference
docs.text: Remote calls travel as NET_RPC = 103 in two different shapes. Do not mix them: plugin events use {"rpc", "payload"}, component calls use {"net_id", "method", "args", ...}. The server stamps _sender on relayed frames before dispatch.

docs.title: Shape A — plugin events (NetworkPlugin)
docs.text:
send(msg_type, payload, target_id=-1) wraps the call as {"rpc": name, "payload": {...}} and uses send_to when target_id >= 0 on a server, otherwise broadcast; broadcast(msg_type, payload) always broadcasts (plugins/network_plugin.py:94-113).

plug = engine.plugin_manager.get_plugin("NetworkPlugin")
plug.on_message("chat", lambda msg: print(msg.sender_id, msg.payload))
plug.broadcast("chat", {"text": "hello"})          # everyone
plug.send("ping1", {"t": 1.0}, target_id=peer_id)  # server -> one peer
plug.poll()  # every frame: dispatches plugin RPCs, re-queues the rest

Subscribe with on_message(msg_type, handler); handlers receive a NetworkMessage(msg_type, payload, sender_id). _dispatch_rpc looks up handlers by rpc name and falls back to "*" handlers (network_plugin.py:115-142). handle_transport_messages splits NET_RPC {"rpc": ...} frames off for the plugin and returns the remainder; poll() drains the transport and pushes leftovers back to the front of the queue (network_plugin.py:144-180).

docs.title: Shape B — component calls (NetworkManager + core/network/rpc.py)
docs.text:
NetworkManager.send_rpc(net_id, method, args=None, target=None) builds {"net_id", "method", "args", "t", "target?"} and routes: send_to when target is set on a server, broadcast when on a server or target is None, otherwise send to the server (netmgr/transport.py:147-161).

mgr = NetworkManager.get()
mgr.send_rpc(net_id, "take_damage", {"amount": 10})            # server fans out / client asks server
mgr.send_rpc(net_id, "heal", {"amount": 5}, target=peer_id)    # server -> one peer

from core.ecs import Component
class Health(Component):
    @server_rpc
    def take_damage(self, args): ...

Helpers in core/network/rpc.py:72-105: send_server_rpc (client sends, server broadcasts), send_client_rpc (server broadcasts only), send_target_rpc (server send_to, client plain send). Decorators server_rpc / client_rpc / target_rpc tag a method with _rpc_type and register it by name. invoke_rpc(entity, method, args, sender) tries the tagged method first (fn(args), falling back to fn()), then handle_rpc(method, args, sender), then rpc_<method>(**args).

docs.title: Dispatch order
docs.text:
NetworkManager.on_update checks NET_RPC frames first: frames containing "rpc" go to the plugin's _dispatch_rpc, everything else goes to _handle_rpc (netmgr/manager.py:160-172). _handle_rpc drops frames whose target is not the local id, skips client-type RPCs on the server, and invokes the rest on the entity found by net_id (netmgr/sync.py:323-353).

Related: Message Types (NET_RPC row), Snapshots and Interpolation (apply_snapshot dispatch), NetworkManager session component.

Verified against: plugins/network_plugin.py:94-180; core/components/network/netmgr/transport.py:147-161; core/components/network/netmgr/manager.py:124-131,160-172; core/components/network/netmgr/sync.py:323-353; core/network/rpc.py:12-106; core/network/transp/server.py:232-263.

docs.title: Snapshots and Interpolation (Gameplay)
docs.text: How per-entity state flows: authority sides emit at capped rates, the server relays, receivers buffer timestamped frames and interpolate. NET_SNAPSHOT = 111 is accepted and relayed by the transport but has no built-in emitter or consumer — it is a reserved channel for custom whole-world snapshots; the four component channels below are the working snapshot system.

docs.title: Send rates and gating
docs.text:
Each component accumulates dt and sends at most every 1.0 / max(1.0, send_rate) seconds — and only when the value actually changed:

Component Default send_rate Inspector range Gate Tick source NetworkTransform 20.0 1–60 pos_threshold 0.001, rot_threshold 0.5°, first send always on_update NetworkRigidbody 20.0 1–60 velocity_threshold 0.01 on vel + angular on_fixed_update NetworkAnimator 10.0 1–30 clip/time/speed/playing/params/trigger diff on_update NetworkVariables 10.0 1–30 dirty flag + sync_on_change immediate send on_update

(network_transform.py:227-234, network_rigidbody.py:160-168, network_animator.py:131-165, network_variables.py:156-168.) Payloads carry {net_id, t, seq} plus channel keys (p/r/s, v/w, animator state, vars). NetworkManager.tick_rate (default 20.0, range 1–60) is an inspector field on the session component; per-component send_rate is what actually paces traffic.

docs.title: Owner-driven vs authoritative
docs.text: Every channel has a SERVER / OWNER authority enum defaulting to SERVER (TransformAuthority, RigidbodyAuthority, VariableAuthority, animator equivalent). _can_send returns is_server under SERVER and ident.is_owner under OWNER; apply_snapshot ignores echoes — owner's own frames under OWNER authority, and anything received on the server under SERVER authority — and drops stale seq frames. Ownership itself moves via NET_OWNER_CHANGE: a client sends {requester}, the server applies and broadcasts {net_id, owner_id} (netmgr/sync.py:355-379).

docs.title: Manager dispatch
docs.text: NetworkManager.on_update drains the transport once per frame (poll()) and routes by type (netmgr/manager.py:124-181): NET_SPAWN → _handle_spawn, NET_SPAWN_REQUEST → _handle_spawn_request (server only), NET_DESPAWN → _handle_despawn, NET_RPC {"rpc":...} → plugin _dispatch_rpc else _handle_rpc, NET_OWNER_CHANGE → _handle_owner_change, NET_KICK → disconnect(), PEER_JOINED → _sync_new_peer + optional auto-spawn of player_prefab at a random ±2 m offset, LEAVE → despawn that peer's owned entities. State channels resolve the entity by net_id and call comp.apply_snapshot(data); NET_VARIABLES without a NetworkVariables component falls back to generic setattr per component_key prop map.

docs.title: Interpolation
docs.text:
Receivers append {t, seq, ...} to a bounded deque (transform 32, rigidbody 20) and render at now - interp_delay (transform 0.1 s, rigidbody 0.08 s), lerping between bracketing frames; with interpolate = False the latest frame applies directly. teleport_threshold (default 5.0 m) clears the buffer and snaps on jumps. Variables/animator apply latest-wins with seq guards instead of buffering.

tr.send_rate = 30.0        # NetworkTransform: 30 Hz cap
tr.pos_threshold = 0.01   # ...but only when moved > 1 cm
tr.interpolate = True
tr.interp_delay = 0.1
rb.send_rate = 20.0        # NetworkRigidbody, paced in on_fixed_update
vars_comp.sync_on_change = True  # NetworkVariables: send immediately on set_var

Related: Message Types (channel ids + relay rules), RPC Reference, NetworkTransform / NetworkRigidbody / NetworkAnimator / NetworkVariables.

docs.title: Transport Internals
docs.text: How GameServer / GameClient move bytes: one TCP connection per peer, each in its own asyncio loop on a daemon thread, frames drained per write. Singleton access via get_transport().

docs.title: GameServer (core/network/transp/server.py)
docs.text:
start() spawns the loop thread and waits up to 5 s for the ready flag; set_max_players(n) clamps to >= 1 at any time. The listener is asyncio.start_server with TCP_NODELAY set on both the listen sockets and every accepted socket (server.py:108-116,126-133). _read_frame reads exactly FRAME_HEADER_SIZE bytes, unpacks ">I", rejects 0 or > MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE, then reads the payload (server.py:118-124).

Join handshake, first frame decides everything:

  1. First frame must be JOIN, otherwise the socket is closed without a reply (server.py:140-147).
  2. At capacity (len(clients) >= max_players) the server writes NET_KICK {"reason": "server_full"}, drains, and closes (server.py:148-160).
  3. Otherwise it assigns peer_id from _next_id (starts at 1), truncates the name to 32 chars, queues PEER_JOINED {"id", "name"} locally, fans it out to existing peers, and answers the newcomer with JOINED {"your_id", "peers"} (server.py:161-188).
  4. On disconnect it queues LEAVE {"id"} locally and fans it out, then closes (server.py:194-221).

_client_loop answers PING with PONG {"t"} inline; every other accepted type gets _sender stamped, is appended to the shared incoming deque, and — only for transform/rigidbody/animator/variables/RPC/snapshot — is re-packed and written to all other peers (server.py:223-267). broadcast writes one packed message to every client; send_to(peer_id, ...) writes to a single client; both schedule the drain on the loop via run_coroutine_threadsafe (server.py:269-317).

docs.title: GameClient (core/network/transp/client.py)
docs.text: connect(host, port, name) spawns the loop thread (no-op if already connected). _connect uses asyncio.open_connection, sets TCP_NODELAY, marks connected, then sends JOIN {"name"} as its first frame and waits for the reply (client.py:91-104). JOINED stores peer_id and queues the frame; NET_KICK is queued and the session ends; anything else unparseable aborts the connect. _read_loop answers PING with PONG, queues NET_KICK and breaks, and queues everything else (client.py:148-177). send(msg_type, data) packs and schedules _async_send only while connected with a live loop; bytes_sent / bytes_received count framed bytes. set_on_connected / set_on_disconnected are the only callbacks — they live on GameClient, not on Transport.

docs.title: Transport facade (core/network/transp/transport.py:82-144)
docs.text:
Method Semantics host(host="0.0.0.0", port=7777, max_players=16) Disconnects first, starts GameServer; on success role = server, local_id = 0 connect(host="127.0.0.1", port=7777, name="Player") Disconnects first, starts GameClient; polls up to 5 s for connected, returns False immediately on NET_KICK disconnect() Stops client and server, role back to "none", clears the incoming queue send(msg_type, data) Client → server; on a server acts as broadcast send_to(peer_id, msg_type, data) Server → one peer; on a client falls back to plain send to the server broadcast(msg_type, data) Alias of send poll() Drain the shared deque under lock, non-blocking — call once per frame peek() / get_peers() Non-destructive read; get_peers() -> [{id, name}] on server only

State: is_server / is_client / is_connected, local_id (server 0, client = assigned id), peer_count, bytes_sent / bytes_received (client side only). TCP only — no UDP, no encryption, no gameplay-side auth; high-rate state pays head-of-line blocking. NetworkPlugin.poll() and NetworkManager.on_update() drain the same deque, so run exactly one pump per frame.

Related: Message Types (relay table), Transport and Protocol (overview), NetworkManager.

docs.title: 2D Guide
docs.text: Top-down / side-view planar physics. 2D bodies use Rigidbody2D + one 2D collider and are simulated by the shared solver, then locked to the plane every step.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Field Default Notes Rigidbody2D.mass 1.0 add_impulse divides by mass unless kinematic drag 0.0 Inspector 0–1000 angular_drag 0.05 Inspector 0–1000 gravity_scale 1.0 Inspector 0–100 is_kinematic False freeze_rotation False Turn on for top-down characters velocity / angular_velocity Vec2.zero() / 0.0 Setters mark _velocity_dirty; consume_velocity_dirty() clears it

Shape mapping (shapep/shapes.py:83-91): BoxCollider2D → box size [sx, sy, 1.0], center [ox, oy, 0.0]; CircleCollider2D → sphere radius scaled_radius, center [ox, oy, 0.0]. Never mix 2D and 3D components on one entity.

Plane lock (scene.py:212-227, _constrain_2d_bodies): after step_simulation(dt) every 2D body is clamped — pos.z → 0, rotation (0, 0, rz), velocity (vx, vy, 0), angular velocity (0, 0, az).

rb.mass = 1.0
rb.gravity_scale = 0.0      # top-down: no gravity pull
rb.freeze_rotation = True   # no spin from hits
player.add_component(rb)
player.add_component(BoxCollider2D())

ground = scene.create_entity("Ground2D")

docs.title: Collision Callbacks
docs.text: Three phases derived from frame-to-frame contact sets: on_collision_enter (new pairs), on_collision_stay (kept pairs), on_collision_exit (lost pairs). Both bodies are notified with the other entity id.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Item Value Phases enter / stay / exit, computed as entered = current − prev, exited = prev − current, stayed = current ∩ prev (events.py:305-307) Script signature other_id OR (other_id, force) — arity from inspect.signature at load Component signature Always (other_id, force) force float(ev.get("force", 0.0)), max over duplicate events for the pair Gating _has_collision_listeners() skips the whole pass when nobody listens

docs.title: Arity rule (scripts)
docs.text:
At script load (hotreload.py:240-248):

nargs = len(inspect.signature(meth).parameters)  # fallback 1 on error
self._py_collision_arity[cb] = 2 if nargs >= 2 else 1

Dispatch (events.py:317-336): arity >= 2 → callback(other_id, force), else callback(other_id). Components (_invoke_component_collision, events.py:356-367) always get (other_id, force) and ScriptComponent instances are skipped there (they are handled by the script path).

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:

def on_collision_enter(self, other_id):
    print("hit:", other_id)

def on_collision_stay(self, other_id, force=0.0):
    print("stay:", other_id, force)

def on_collision_exit(self, other_id):
    print("left:", other_id)

# plain components must accept both args:
class DamageOnHit(Component):
    def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force):
        ...

docs.text: 3D rigid-body simulation in ZarinEngine: entities with a Rigidbody plus one or more colliders are stepped by a pluggable solver (IPhysicsSolver), everything else is static scenery.

docs.text:
entity = scene.create_entity("Crate")
from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody
from core.components.physics.box_collider import BoxCollider

rb = Rigidbody()
rb.mass = 1.0

def on_fixed_update(self, dt):
    rb = self._entity.get_component(Rigidbody)
    if rb is not None:
        rb.add_force(Vec3(0.0, 10.0, 0.0))
        rb.add_torque(Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0))

def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0):
    pass  # (other_entity_id, impact_force), also on_collision_stay/exit

docs.title: Fixed update notes
docs.text:
• Engine.tick_fixed_step (core/engine/eng/loop.py) accumulates real time against _fixed_dt (0.02), caps the backlog at 5 * _fixed_dt, runs at most 5 steps per tick (MAX_FIXED_STEPS), then runs scene.fixed_update(fd) (component on_fixed_update: Buoyancy/Motor/CharacterController forces and drives) and finally system-plugin step(fd).
  • PhysicsScene.step order: register new entities → shape-change check (every 60 steps) → ECS→physics sync → soft-body AABB separation (only when ≥2 soft bodies) → solver.step_simulation(dt) → 2D constrain → physics→ECS sync → soft sync → collision events.
  • Solver-param scoping: num_sub_steps (2), solver_iterations (10), erp (0.2) are project-config defaults consumed by the PyBullet solver (whose standalone defaults are 1 / 50 / 0.4); the default Culverin/Jolt solver ignores them and uses the culverin_* world caps instead.
  • Collision callbacks: script methods accept (other_id) or (other_id, force) — arity auto-detected via inspect.signature (ScriptComponent._py_collision_arity); engine-component handlers always receive (other_id, force).
  • Threading: multi_threaded runs the solver in a daemon multiprocessing.Process (PhysicsProcess) over SharedPhysicsBuffer / SoftSharedBuffer; single runs PhysicsScene in-process (required by CharacterController / Motor); per_layer_process spawns processes on demand per layer.

docs.title: Rigidbody
docs.text: Makes an entity simulated: mass, gravity response, accumulated forces, readable velocities. Without it a collider is static scenery; with it the entity joins the dynamics world.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Field Default Notes mass 1.0 Inspector 0.001–100000; forced to 0.0 at body creation when is_kinematic drag 0.0 Inspector 0–1000 angular_drag 0.05 Inspector 0–1000 use_gravity True Gravity applies is_kinematic False Transform-driven: pushes dynamics, never pushed freeze_pos_x/y/z False Serialized as freeze_pos triple freeze_rot_x/y/z False Serialized as freeze_rot triple velocity / angular_velocity Vec3.zero() Readable every frame; setter marks body dirty for next sync

docs.title: Usage in Editor
docs.text: Add Rigidbody + one collider (Box/Sphere/Capsule/Mesh). Mass 70–90 player-scale, 1–10 crates; keep interacting mass ratios within ~100:1. Tick is_kinematic for movers, freeze rotation axes for non-tipping crates.

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
entity = scene.create_entity("Ball")
from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody
from core.components.physics.sphere_collider import SphereCollider

rb = Rigidbody()
rb.mass = 2.0
rb.drag = 0.1
rb.freeze_rot_x = True
rb.freeze_rot_z = True
entity.add_component(rb)
col = SphereCollider()
col.radius = 0.5
entity.add_component(col)

def on_fixed_update(self, dt):
    rb = self._entity.get_component(Rigidbody)
    if rb is None or rb.is_kinematic:
        return
    rb.add_force(Vec3(0.0, 20.0, 0.0))   # accumulated, cleared after push
    rb.add_torque(Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0))
    rb.add_impulse(Vec3(0.0, 5.0, 0.0))  # instant velocity change impulse/mass

def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0):
    pass
def on_collision_stay(self, other_id, force=0.0):
    pass
def on_collision_exit(self, other_id, force=0.0):
    pass
  • add_force(force, world_space=True) / add_torque(torque) accumulate until the next ECS→physics push, then auto-clear — call every fixed step for continuous thrust.
  • add_impulse is ignored for kinematic bodies and non-positive mass.
  • velocity setter flips _velocity_dirty so the value pushes into the solver on the next sync.
  • Collision callbacks: script on_collision_enter/stay/exit accept (other_id) or (other_id, force) (arity auto-detected via inspect.signature); engine-component handlers always take (other_id, force).

  • In multi_threaded mode this crosses the SharedPhysicsBuffer (flags 1 active, 2 dirty, 4 kinematic/teleport, 8 2D).

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
# Gravity at runtime (IPhysicsSolver API):
solver.set_gravity((0.0, -9.81, 0.0))
solver.step_simulation(0.02)
solver.apply_force(body_id, (0.0, 10.0, 0.0))
solver.apply_torque(body_id, (0.0, 1.0, 0.0))
solver.apply_impulse(body_id, (0.0, 5.0, 0.0))
hit = solver.ray_cast((0.0, 5.0, 0.0), (0.0, -1.0, 0.0), 100.0)

Background step order (verified): coalesce pending step commands into one dt → apply teleports/forces from shared memory → step_simulation(dt) → zero 2D out-of-plane velocity → write back with version bump (+ soft buffers) → map body ids to entity ids for collision events. In-process path mirrors it without serialization: register → shape-check (every 60 steps) → ECS→physics → soft separation (only when ≥2 soft bodies) → step → constrain 2D → physics→ECS → soft sync → events.

  • ECS→physics pushes only on dirty Transform or accumulated force; physics→ECS skips kinematic/dirty bodies; force accumulators clear after every push — call add_force each fixed step.

docs.text: Key Default Notes culverin_num_threads 0 0 forces max_physics_jobs = 0 and max_physics_barriers = 0 (solver.py:74-76) culverin_max_physics_jobs 0 Passed as max_physics_jobs to PhysicsWorld culverin_max_physics_barriers 0 Passed as max_physics_barriers to PhysicsWorld culverin_max_bodies 65536 Passed as max_bodies culverin_max_pairs 65536 Passed as max_pairs culverin_max_contact_constraints 65536 Passed as max_contact_constraints culverin_temp_allocator_size 16777216 Passed as temp_allocator_size (16 MiB) culverin_penetration_slop 0.02 Passed as penetration_slop culverin_enable_ccd False Stored flag; CCD off by default culverin_enable_sleeping True Stored flag; sleeping on by default gravity_x/y/z 0.0 / -9.81 / 0.0 Applied via PhysicsWorld.set_gravity

docs.title: Keys read vs ignored
docs.text:
Read in initialize (solver.py:52-90): gravity_x, gravity_y, gravity_z, culverin_num_threads, culverin_max_physics_jobs, culverin_max_physics_barriers, culverin_penetration_slop, culverin_max_bodies, culverin_max_pairs, culverin_max_contact_constraints, culverin_temp_allocator_size, culverin_enable_ccd, culverin_enable_sleeping.

NOT read: num_sub_steps, solver_iterations, erp. step_simulation(dt) forwards a single world.step(dt) (solver.py:133-135) — there is no sub-step loop.

docs.title: Usage in Editor
docs.text: Set physics solver to culverin in the project config. Tune only the culverin_* keys above; changing num_sub_steps / solver_iterations / erp has no effect on this backend.

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
from physics_solvers.culverin_solver.solverp.solver import CulverinSolver

solver = CulverinSolver()
ok = solver.initialize({
    "gravity_y": -9.81,
    "culverin_num_threads": 0,          # 0 => jobs/barriers forced to 0
    "culverin_max_bodies": 65536,
    "culverin_max_pairs": 65536,
    "culverin_max_contact_constraints": 65536,
    "culverin_temp_allocator_size": 16777216,
    "culverin_penetration_slop": 0.02,
    "culverin_enable_ccd": False,
    "culverin_enable_sleeping": True,
})
assert ok
solver.step_simulation(0.02)

docs.title: Fixed update notes
docs.text:
• dt is Engine._fixed_dt (0.02 default); solving runs inside solver.step_simulation(dt).
  • ray_cast returns body_id / position / normal=(0,0,0) / fraction; get_collision_events returns body_a / body_b pairs only (no force).

docs.title: PhysX Solver
docs.text: USD/Omni (ovphysx) backend. Tensor-driven: poses, velocities, and wrenches flow through bound tables; gravity is baked into the generated scene.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Key Default Notes physx_device / device "cpu" opts.get("physx_device", opts.get("device", "cpu")); PhysX(device=device) gravity_x/y/z 0.0 / -9.81 / 0.0 Stored; written into USD as physics:gravityDirection + physics:gravityMagnitude (scenes.py) debug_draw setter is a no-op (pass) Reading works, enabling does nothing on this backend

docs.title: What initialize reads
docs.text:
Only physx_device/device and gravity_x/y/z (solver.py:57-71). Honest limitation, verified by grep over the whole physx_solver/ package:

  • num_sub_steps — not read (no match in package).
  • solver_iterations — not read (no match in package).
  • erp — not read (no match in package).

set_gravity only stores the tuple and marks _bodies_dirty = True; it takes effect when the scene is (re)built. step_simulation(dt) accumulates _sim_time += dt, calls ov_physx.step(dt, sim_time) + wait_all(), then pulls transforms from the pose table.

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
from physics_solvers.physx_solver.solverp.solver import PhysXSolver

solver = PhysXSolver()
ok = solver.initialize({
    "physx_device": "cpu",   # or "cuda"/"gpu" depending on ovphysx build
    "gravity_x": 0.0,
    "gravity_y": -9.81,
    "gravity_z": 0.0,
})
assert ok
solver.step_simulation(0.02)

Raycast returns the closest body by distance to hit["position"] with body_id / position / normal / distance. get_collision_events adapts get_contact_report() headers/points into body_a / body_b / type / points[position, normal, impulse, separation].

docs.title: Usage in Editor
docs.text: Set physics solver to pybullet. Collision layers work via setCollisionFilterPair: a pair collides only if (groupA & maskB) != 0 and (groupB & maskA) != 0 (solver.py:281-294).

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
from physics_solvers.pybullet_solver.solverp.solver import PyBulletSolver

solver = PyBulletSolver()
solver.initialize({
    "headless": True,
    "gravity_y": -9.81,
    "fixed_time_step": 0.02,
    "num_sub_steps": 2,
    "solver_iterations": 10,
    "erp": 0.2,
    "contact_erp": 0.2,
    "enable_sleeping": True,
})
solver.step_simulation(0.02)

# Spring joints map stiffness to constraint ERP:
# changeConstraint(erp=min(1.0, stiffness * 0.01), maxForce=100)
jid = solver.create_joint("spring", body_a, body_b, anchor=(0, 1, 0))

Compound bodies: create_compound_rigid_body splits mass by part volume (shapep.part_volume) and links extras with JOINT_FIXED; mixed trigger/solid parts log a warning and share one body.

docs.title: Music, Plotter and QtQuick
docs.text:
Smaller bundled extensions for sound, data and UI hosting — same base class, same hooks, narrower jobs. Verified versions: TrackerMusicPlugin 1.0.0 SYSTEM = False, PlotterPlugin 1.2.0 SYSTEM = False, QtQuickWorldPlugin 1.0.0 SYSTEM = True.

Tracker Music (plugins/tracker_music_plugin/, rend/ engine: engine.py, engine_seq.py, engine_mix.py, engine_fx.py, defs.py):

  • ProTracker-style module playback (patterns, samples, BPM-relative tempo) for retro scores and demoscene vibes.
  • Drop a module file, drive play/stop from hooks or scripts, mix under positional AudioSources — music bed plus 3D effects is the intended stack.
  • Tempo math follows classic tracker conventions (ticks per row against BPM).

Plotter (plugins/plotter_plugin/):

  • Curve and data plotting panels: profiler traces, animation curves, telemetry — see numbers as pictures during tuning.
  • Feed it from step() hooks or log taps; pair with the profiler panel for frame-time forensics.

QtQuick (plugins/qt_quick_plugin/):

  • Hosts QtQuick/QML surfaces inside the editor: animated dashboards, custom tool UIs, web-style panels without fighting the widget toolkit.
  • Use for tooling chrome; gameplay UI stays in the GUI system (GuiCanvas widgets ship in builds, QtQuick does not guarantee that).

All three iterate like any user plugin (same lifecycle, same config persistence) and package into .zplugin for sharing.

Related: Audio System (music bed pairing), Profiler (plotter data source), GUI Overview (gameplay UI home), .zplugin Packaging.

docs.title: Example Plugin Walkthrough
docs.text:
plugins/example_plugin.py (43 lines) is the canonical minimal plugin — every convention in one place. Read it, copy it, rename it.

from core.foundation.plugins import PluginBase
from core.foundation.logger import Logger

class ExamplePlugin(PluginBase):
    NAME = "ExamplePlugin"
    VERSION = "1.0.0"
    DESCRIPTION = "Example user plugin demonstrating the plugin API."
    SYSTEM = False

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self._frame = 0

    def initialize(self, engine):
        super().initialize(engine)
        self.add_menu_item("ExamplePlugin", "Say Hello", lambda: Logger.info("Hello from ExamplePlugin!"), "Ctrl+Shift+H")
        self.add_toolbar_button("Hello", lambda: Logger.info("Hello from toolbar!"), tooltip="Say hello")
        Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Initialized! Counter: {self.get_config('counter', 0)}")

    def on_scene_loaded(self, scene):
        Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Scene loaded: {scene.name}")

    def on_play_start(self):
        Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Play started!")
        self._frame = 0

    def on_play_stop(self):
        Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Play stopped after {self._frame} frames.")
        counter = self.get_config("counter", 0) + 1
        self.set_config("counter", counter)
        Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Run counter saved: {counter}")

    def shutdown(self):
        Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Shutdown.")

def get_plugin():
    return ExamplePlugin()

Line-by-line lessons:

  • Metadata block (NAME/VERSION/DESCRIPTION/SYSTEM) — copy and rename; SYSTEM = False keeps it in the user tier.
  • super().__init__() then super().initialize(engine) — the second call loads the persisted config; without it get_config always returns defaults.
  • add_menu_item(section, label, callback, shortcut) — menu placement with a hotkey; add_toolbar_button(label, callback, tooltip) — one-click access. Callbacks can be lambdas for one-liners.
  • on_scene_loaded(scene) reads scene.name — scene hooks receive the live object, query it directly.
  • on_play_start resets per-run state (_frame = 0); on_play_stop increments and persists the counter — the canonical config round-trip in four lines.
  • shutdown logs; base shutdown (not overridden here beyond logging) saves config and unpatches.
  • Module-level get_plugin() returns a fresh instance — the manager imports the module and calls exactly this. Any name else and the file is invisible.

Exercises: change the shortcut and watch the menu update; add step() counting frames into _frame so the stop message reports real numbers; store a second key (last_scene) in on_scene_loaded and print it in initialize.

Related: PluginBase Lifecycle (all hooks), User Plugins guide (where to put the file), Plugin Manager (how it loads).

docs.title: MCP Bridge
docs.text:
Model-Context-Protocol server (NAME = "ZarinMCP", VERSION = "2.1.0", SYSTEM = False in plugins/zarin_mcp/__init__.py) exposing engine operations to AI agents: scene queries, object creation, property edits, screenshots, code execution — the same surface this documentation workflow drives.

Layout in plugins/zarin_mcp/:

  • mcp_server.py — protocol server: tool registration, request dispatch, response framing.
  • registry.py — tool catalog: every exposed operation registers with name, schema and handler.
  • handlers/ — one module per domain (scene, objects, viewport, execution), keeping the server file thin.
  • main_thread.py — GUI-thread dispatch: document and view mutations must run on the main thread, so background requests marshal through here.
  • mcp_dock.py — editor panel: server status, connected clients, request log, start/stop.

Repo roots: zarin_mcp_config.json and zarin_mcp_launcher.py at the project root configure and launch the bridge outside the editor; plugins/mcp_pack-2.1.1.zplugin ships it as a signed distributable (see Packaging).

Workflow: launch the bridge (dock or launcher) → connect an MCP-capable agent with the config → the agent lists tools from the registry → scene edits flow as validated operations with screenshots back. Every mutation is an explicit tool call — auditable in the dock log.

Safety posture: the bridge can rewrite scenes and run code — bind it to localhost, gate launches behind the dock switch, and review the request log like a sudo history.

Troubleshooting: agent cannot connect → server not started or config path wrong; tool missing → registry for that domain not loaded, check the dock; scene edits lag → main-thread queue saturated, lighten the request rate.

Related: .zplugin Packaging (the shippable pack), Plugin Manager (load tier), Gizmos (what agents see).

docs.title: Network Plugin (Plugin Page)
docs.text:
System plugin (network_plugin.py, NAME = "NetworkPlugin", VERSION = "1.0.0", SYSTEM = True, DESCRIPTION "Multiplayer transport using GameServer/GameClient over TCP") bridging gameplay code and the transport singleton.

Plugin-side facts:

  • Loads in the system tier during editor/engine startup; initialize logs readiness, shutdown disconnects cleanly so no session survives quit.
  • Exposes session state as properties: is_connected, is_server, local_id, peer_count — all exception-guarded, safe to poll from UI code.
  • host(port=7777, max_players=16) binds all interfaces; connect(host, port) joins as "Player"; both log and return bool.
  • Messaging rides MessageType.NET_RPC frames: send(type, payload, target_id) targets one peer from the server or broadcasts otherwise; broadcast(type, payload) always fans out.
  • on_message(type, handler) subscriptions feed NetworkMessage(msg_type, payload, sender_id); "*" wildcard catches unhandled traffic for logging. _dispatch_rpc isolates handler exceptions per handler.
  • poll() drains transport frames, dispatches RPC ones, and requeues the remainder back to the transport — non-RPC protocols coexist untouched.
  • handle_transport_messages(msgs) is the seam other systems hook: returns unhandled frames for upstream processing.

For the full messaging patterns, payload shapes and session recipes see the Networking section (Transport and Protocol, NetworkManager, Network Plugin usage page) — this page covers the plugin as an engine citizen: where it loads, what it owns, how it shuts down.

Troubleshooting (plugin scope): handlers never fire → poll() not pumped or subscribed after traffic started; double handling → same handler subscribed twice (subscriptions append); session survives editor quit → shutdown path bypassed, always disconnect explicitly in tooling.

Related: Networking section (protocol, manager, components), Plugin Manager (system tier), PluginBase Lifecycle (hooks used).

docs.title: Plugins Overview
docs.text:
Plugins extend the editor and the engine without touching core files: dock panels, toolbar buttons, menu items, new components, file openers, method patches, extra Inspector fields, native extensions.

Two flavors:

  • System plugins (SYSTEM = True, shipped in plugins/): physics, network transport, mesh editor, VR, MCP bridge — the engine relies on them, they load first and cannot be casually removed.
  • User plugins (SYSTEM = False, live in plugins/user/): team tools, importers, level utilities, experiment rigs — load after system plugins, enable/disable freely.

Three formats, one manager:

  • .py source plugins with a get_plugin() factory returning the instance.
  • Native .dll / .so shared libraries with a Python entry shim.
  • .zplugin signed packages: manifest + code + native modules + bundled libs, verified against config/trusted_keys, extracted once and cached by sha256 fingerprint.

PluginManager (core/foundation/plugins/manager.py ~203 lines, plus base.py / discovery.py / loader.py / lifecycle.py / ui_registry.py; re-exported by core/foundation/plugins/__init__.py) owns discovery, _load_order, activation, dependency checks from manifests, security verification, config persistence per plugin, and teardown in reverse order.

Pages: PluginBase Lifecycle, Plugin Manager, Example Plugin walkthrough, User Plugins guide, .zplugin Packaging, System Plugins catalog, Network Plugin, VR Plugin, MCP Bridge, Music/Plotter/QtQuick extensions.

Five-minute first plugin: copy plugins/example_plugin.py into plugins/user/my_plugin.py, rename the class and NAME, keep get_plugin() at the bottom, restart the editor — the menu item appears, the toolbar button appears, the run counter persists across sessions.

docs.title: Plugin Manager
docs.text:
Discovery, ordering, security and teardown for everything pluggable. One class, PluginManager, three plugin tiers: built-in .py, native binaries, signed .zplugin packages.

Discovery and order:

  • System plugins load from plugins/ first, user plugins from plugins/user/ after. Registration order appends to _load_order; teardown walks it in reverse so dependents release before their dependencies.
  • get_system_plugins() filters the tier; iteration helpers yield instances in load order for frames (step/pre_step) and event fan-out (scene, play, window hooks).
  • Replacing a plugin (same NAME, new path) swaps the entry in place instead of duplicating — hot iteration without restarts for pure-Python plugins in some flows.

Native binaries:

  • .dll / .so entries load through the native path with _native_plugin_path recorded on the instance; a sibling <name>_resources folder auto-resolves as resource_dir.
  • Bundled dependency directories activate per plugin (_activate_bundled_libs) so two plugins can ship conflicting library versions without poisoning each other.

.zplugin security chain, verified step by step:

  1. verify_zplugin_file checks the manifest (name, version, dependencies list with missing-dependency reports), indexes every entry, and rejects unindexed native modules (_native/ discipline for .pyd/.so/.dll).
  2. Signatures verify against trusted keys from config/trusted_keys (plus an optional configured dir); without keys configured, verification reports "no trusted keys configured" instead of silently passing.
  3. _zplugin_fingerprint (sha256 + size + mtime) gates the extraction cache: unchanged packages reuse the extracted tree, changed ones re-extract.
  4. Manifest dependencies resolve (including bundled Cython builds via cython_modules); missing ones log explicitly and block activation.

Configuration: per-plugin security knobs (check_updates_on_startup, trusted_keys_dir) feed from the plugin security config; per-plugin data persists through the base-class config load/save.

Failure posture: a broken plugin logs and skips — one bad apple never prevents editor startup. Check the console first; the plugin manager panel mirrors load state, order and errors.

Related: PluginBase Lifecycle, .zplugin Packaging, User Plugins guide, System Plugins catalog.

docs.title: PluginBase Lifecycle
docs.text:
Every plugin subclasses PluginBase (core/foundation/plugins/base.py, re-exported by core/foundation/plugins/__init__.py) and is constructed through the module-level get_plugin() factory. Metadata first, behavior second.

from core.foundation.plugins import PluginBase
from core.foundation.logger import Logger


class GreetingPlugin(PluginBase):
    NAME = "GreetingPlugin"
    VERSION = "1.0.0"
    DESCRIPTION = "Greets the user and counts Play sessions."
    SYSTEM = False

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self._frame = 0

    def initialize(self, engine):
        super().initialize(engine)
        self.add_menu_item("GreetingPlugin", "Say Hello", self.hello, "Ctrl+Shift+H")
        self.add_toolbar_button("Hello", self.hello, tooltip="Say hello")

    def hello(self):
        Logger.info("Hello from GreetingPlugin!")

    def on_play_start(self):
        self._frame = 0

    def on_play_stop(self):
        total = self.get_config("runs", 0) + 1
        self.set_config("runs", total)

    def shutdown(self):
        Logger.info("GreetingPlugin shutdown.")


def get_plugin():
    return GreetingPlugin()

Metadata: NAME (manager key and log tag), VERSION, DESCRIPTION, SYSTEM (load tier). The manager keys everything — logs, config files, load order — off NAME, so renames orphan old configs.

Lifecycle hooks, in engine order:

Hook Signature When initialize (engine) Once at load; always call super() first (loads persisted config) shutdown () At unload; base implementation saves config and restores all patches step (dt) Every frame (scaled time) pre_step (dt) Every fixed step, before scene update on_viewport_ready (viewport) Editor viewport created on_main_window_ready (main_window) Main window assembled — safe to add docks on_project_opened () Project root known on_scene_loaded / on_scene_unloaded (scene) Scene switch boundaries on_play_start / on_play_stop () Session boundaries — reset per-run state here

Capabilities (all verified on the base class):

  • UI: add_menu_item(section, label, callback, shortcut), add_toolbar_button(label, callback, tooltip); dock descriptors in self._docks; file openers in self._file_openers; new component types in self._components.
  • Patching without forks: patch_component(name, method_patches, extra_inspector_fields, filter_extensions, wraps), add_inspector_field(component, field), extend_file_filter(component, field, filter), patch_function(module, name, wrapper) — everything tracked by a PatchTracker and reverted by unpatch_all() (automatic in base shutdown).
  • Config: get_config(key, default) / set_config(key, value) persisted per plugin across restarts; engine access via self.engine; manager via self._manager; enabled flag for soft on/off.
  • Native side: _native_plugin_path locates the binary; resource_dir resolves the sibling _resources folder; bundled_library_dir exposes shipped dependencies.

Rules: never block initialize (defer heavy work to project/scene hooks); always super().initialize(engine) or config never loads; undo every patch you own even though shutdown covers you; gate per-frame work on self.enabled.

Related: Plugin Manager, Example Plugin walkthrough, User Plugins guide.
