System plugins register components, docks and panels exactly like user plugins (same base class, same hooks) — the only differences are load tier and the engine's reliance on them. Disabling the physics or network plugin degrades the matching subsystem; the manager panel warns before you do.

.pending/ holds staged plugins awaiting activation; mcp_pack-2.1.1.zplugin is the shippable MCP artifact (see Packaging).

Related: Plugin Manager (load tiers), Network Plugin, VR Plugin, MCP Bridge, Music/Plotter/QtQuick page.

docs.title: User Plugins Guide
docs.text:
Team tools live in plugins/user/ as .py files: importers, level utilities, batch renamers, experiment rigs, custom panels. System tier stays untouched; user tier iterates freely.

Scaffold, step by step:

  1. Copy plugins/example_plugin.py to plugins/user/my_tool.py.
  2. Rename the class and NAME (manager key — unique per plugin), bump VERSION, write a one-line DESCRIPTION, keep SYSTEM = False.
  3. Implement initialize(engine): menu items, toolbar buttons, docks, file openers. Defer project-dependent setup to on_project_opened — initialize runs before the project root is known.
  4. Add behavior hooks: step for per-frame tools, on_scene_loaded for scene scanners, on_play_start/stop for session rigs.
  5. Persist with get_config/set_config — window layouts, last paths, counters survive restarts with zero file code.
  6. Restart the editor (or trigger plugin rescan from the manager panel) and verify: menu entry, button, console lines.

Patching etiquette: extend components with add_inspector_field and patch_component instead of editing core files — your fields ride engine updates instead of conflicting with them. Everything unpatches on shutdown automatically.

Debugging: console first (import errors name the missing module and line), manager panel second (load state per plugin), Logger.debug breadcrumbs third. A plugin that raises in initialize is skipped with a log — the editor always starts.

Distribution inside a team: share the .py file directly for trusted colleagues; ship .zplugin for everyone else (signed, versioned, dependency-checked — see Packaging).

Anti-patterns: blocking network calls in initialize (defer to hooks or threads), duplicate NAMEs across files (second load swaps the first), absolute paths in configs (store project-relative), per-frame allocations in step (cache in initialize).

Related: Example Plugin walkthrough (conventions), PluginBase Lifecycle (hooks), .zplugin Packaging (distribution), Plugin Manager panel (Editor Manual).

docs.title: VR Plugin
docs.text:
Editor and runtime virtual-reality support in plugins/vr_plugin/ (NAME = "VRPlugin", VERSION = "1.0.0", SYSTEM = True in vr_plugin/plug/plugin.py, get_plugin() in vr_plugin/plug/__init__.py): a runtime core plus an editor dock.

  • plug/plugin.py (VRPluginBase) + components/ (xr_rig.py, xr_locomotion.py, xr_haptics.py, xr_ar.py, xrinter/) — session and device management: headset poses feed the scene cameras, controllers appear as tracked input alongside the standard Input API for scripts.
  • vr_dock.py — editor panel: start/stop VR sessions, mirror the headset view into a viewport, device status and per-eye settings.

Workflow: open the VR dock, connect the headset, start the session — the game view renders the stereo pair while the desktop viewport keeps the editor camera for staging. Scripts read controller poses through the same Transform/Input conventions as desktop (device-specific bindings surface as buttons and axes).

Performance stance: VR doubles the render load (two eyes) — halve render_scale first, then shadow resolution, then PostFX. The profiler's per-stage timings apply per eye; budget 11 ms total, not per eye.

Scope note: desktop-first engine with a VR annex, not a VR-native engine — room-scale tracking and guardian flows depend on the OpenVR/OpenXR runtimes installed on the machine.

Troubleshooting: headset not found → runtime (SteamVR/monado) not running; black one eye → resolution scale overflow, lower render_scale; drift → tracking loss in the runtime, recenter there.

Related: Cameras (stereo pair source), Input API (controller bindings), Profiler, Render Resolution modes.

docs.title: .zplugin Packaging
docs.text:
Signed distributable plugin format: one file carrying code, native modules, bundled libraries and a manifest — install by dropping it in, verified before it ever executes.

Package anatomy:

  • Manifest: name, version, entry description, dependencies list (other plugins or libraries with versions), optional cython_modules for bundled native builds.
  • Code entries: .py modules loaded through the standard factory convention.
  • Native entries: .pyd / .so / .dll under the _native/ discipline — the verifier rejects unindexed native modules outright.
  • libs/ bundled dependencies activated per plugin, isolated from other plugins' versions.

Build tools: tools/build_plugin.py assembles a plain plugin directory; tools/build_zplugin.py compiles native parts (Cython via cythonize when configured), packs the manifest, code, natives and libs into the .zplugin archive.

Install and verification flow:

  1. Drop the file where the manager scans (or install from the plugin package panel).
  2. verify_zplugin_file (core/foundation/plugins/discovery.py:80) validates the manifest, reports missing dependencies by name, and checks the entry index; payload files re-checked by _verify_payload_files (hash mismatch → modified file, unindexed .pyd/.so/.dll outside _native/ rejected).
  3. Signatures (verify_manifest_signature) verify against config/trusted_keys *.pub files (64-hex ed25519 keys, plus optional trusted_keys_dir); policy allow_unsigned (warn default, strict blocks): with no keys configured verification reports no trusted keys configured instead of silently passing.
  4. _zplugin_fingerprint (core/foundation/plugins/ui_registry.py:130, sha256 + size + mtime) consults the extraction cache — reinstalls of unchanged files cost nothing.
  5. Activation resolves dependencies, mounts bundled libs, loads the entry.

Updating: bump the manifest version, rebuild, redistribute — the fingerprint changes, the cache re-extracts, dependents re-resolve. Keep NAME stable across versions or configs orphan.

The repo ships an example artifact: plugins/mcp_pack-2.1.1.zplugin — inspect it (as an archive) to see a real manifest, native layout and versioning scheme.

Troubleshooting: refused unsigned → sign with a trusted key or add the key; missing dependency → install the named package first; stale behavior after rebuild → fingerprint unchanged (mtime granularity), touch or version-bump; native load failure → architecture mismatch (win .pyd/.dll vs linux .so).

Related: Plugin Manager (verification chain), User Plugins guide (what to pack), System Plugins catalog.

docs.title: BSP Map Import (BSPImport)
docs.text:
Source-engine map import: parses .bsp geometry and rebuilds it as entities with materials.

NAME VERSION SYSTEM BSPImport 2.0.0 False

Declared in plugins/user/bsp_import/plugin.py (BSPImportPlugin, DESCRIPTION = "Import Source Engine BSP maps into the scene (async)"), re-exported from plugins/user/bsp_import/__init__.py. Parser: plugins/user/bsp_import/parse.py (BSPFile). Settings dialog + texture baking: plugins/user/bsp_import/build.py (ImportSettingsDialog, _generate_texture_png, BSPImportWorker).

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
on_viewport_ready inserts Tools → Import BSP... → file dialog (BSP Files (*.bsp)) → ImportSettingsDialog.get_settings() → _import_sync(path, settings, engine, parent):

  1. BSPFile(path) parses lumps; logs BSP v{version}, {faces} faces, {verts} verts.
  2. extract_mesh_groups(settings, progress_cb) → groups {name, vertices, normals, uvs, indices, centroid}; groups with fewer than 3 indices are skipped.
  3. Optional texture baking (generate_textures, texture_size default 128) → assets/materials/bsp/<tex>.png; per-group .mat files ({name, shader_path: "", properties: {albedo_texture, use_albedo_tex: 1}}) unless one already exists.
  4. Scene build: root entity named after the file + one child per group (Transform at centroid, MeshFilter.mesh_name = f"bsp_{bsp}_{tex}", MeshRenderer.materials[0]["path"] = <.mat>), GL upload via mesh.build_gl(ctx, default_prog) when a viewport renderer exists.

Settings keys: merge_by_material (default True), generate_textures (True), texture_size (128), center_pivot (False), convert_coords (True), scale (1.0).

docs.title: Limitations (from the parser)
docs.text:
• Only files with VBSP magic are accepted (ValueError: Not a valid BSP file otherwise); header stores a 32-bit version and 64 lump entries.
  • Only these lumps are read: vertices (3), texdata (2), texinfo (6), faces (7), edges (12), surfedges (13), texdata string data (43) + table (44). Entities, lightmaps, visibility, physics hulls are not imported.
  • Edge width adapts to file version (32-bit indices when version >= 20 and indices validate, else 16-bit).
  • Textures are procedurally generated placeholder PNGs per material name (_generate_texture_png) — original embedded/WAD textures are not extracted.
  • Import is synchronous (_import_sync); the async BSPImportWorker path exists in build.py alongside the _on_import_finished assembler.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Editor path (no code): Tools -> Import BSP... -> pick de_dust2.bsp
#   -> keep merge_by_material + generate_textures -> Import.
# Result: entity "de_dust2" with one child per material group,
# materials under assets/materials/bsp/, hierarchy refreshed.
from plugins.user.bsp_import.parse import BSPFile
bsp = BSPFile("C:/maps/de_dust2.bsp")
print(bsp.version, len(bsp.faces), len(bsp.vertices))
groups = bsp.extract_mesh_groups({"merge_by_material": True}, lambda p, m: None)

docs.title: MCP Tools Bridge (ZarinMCP)
docs.text:
LLM bridge: a Model Context Protocol server inside the editor that exposes scene, components, assets, and viewport capture as tools, resources, templates, and prompts.

NAME VERSION SYSTEM ZarinMCP 2.1.0 False

Declared in plugins/zarin_mcp/__init__.py (ZarinMCPPlugin). Registers dock "ZarinMCP" (area right), menu item ZarinMCP → Open MCP Panel, and an MCP toolbar button.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• plugins/zarin_mcp/__init__.py — plugin, _discover_handlers() wiring.
  • plugins/zarin_mcp/registry.py — Registry: tool() / resource() / resource_template() / prompt() decorators.
  • plugins/zarin_mcp/mcp_server.py — McpServer(host="127.0.0.1", port=9100): SSE app at GET /sse + POST /messages/, activity log (recent_actions(), max 300 entries).
  • plugins/zarin_mcp/handlers/ — scenep/ (query + modify), compp/ (transform + crud), project.py, engine.py, assets.py, editor.py, console.py, resources.py, viewportp/ (camera + capture), util.py.
  • plugins/zarin_mcp/mcp_dock.py, main_thread.py (ensure_dispatcher() / run_on_main_thread() — engine calls from worker threads are marshalled to the Qt main thread via a QueuedConnection dispatcher).
  • plugins/mcp_pack-2.1.1.zplugin — packaged build of the bridge.
  • zarin_mcp_config.json + zarin_mcp_launcher.py — client-side config and stdio↔SSE bridge (repo root).

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Handler areas (one verified tool signature shown; the rest follow the same Registry.tool(name, description, inputSchema) pattern):

  • Scene query: scene_list_entities(include_components=False, filter_name="", limit=50, offset=0) — paginated, filter_name is a case-insensitive substring match.
  • Scene modify (scenep/modify.py), component transform get/set (compp/transform.py), component add/remove/inspect (compp/crud.py), project, engine (play/stop/time), assets, editor selection, console, viewport camera + frame capture (viewportp/).

Resources (handlers/resources.py, 9 total):

URI Content scene://entities all entities with component data scene://hierarchy entity tree project://info root, loaded scene, entity count engine://status play_mode, fps, frame_count, time_scale editor://selection selected entities console://log last 100 log entries project://scenes *.scene files prefab://list *.zpep files asset://overview mesh/texture/audio/script counts

Templates (2): scene://entity/{entity_id}, scene://component/{component_type}. Prompts (2): analyze_scene(detail="basic"), project_overview(). Counts match the client config description: 67 tools, 9 resources, 2 templates, 2 prompts.

docs.title: Config + launcher
docs.text:
zarin_mcp_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "zarin-engine": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["zarin_mcp_launcher.py"],
      "cwd": ".",
      "description": "Zarin Engine — connects to open editor via SSE bridge (67 tools, 9 resources, 2 templates, 2 prompts). Start the editor first."
    }
  }
}

zarin_mcp_launcher.py bridges MCP stdio to http://{ZARIN_MCP_HOST}:{ZARIN_MCP_PORT}/sse (defaults 127.0.0.1:9100), forwarding both directions with 3 connection attempts.

docs.title: Call example
docs.text:
// tools/call over the MCP session:
{ "name": "scene_list_entities",
  "arguments": { "filter_name": "Player", "limit": 50, "offset": 0 } }
// -> { "entities": [{ "id": "...", "name": "Player", "active": true, ... }], ... }
// resource read:
{ "uri": "engine://status" }
// -> { "play_mode": false, "fps": 60.0, "frame_count": 1234, "time_scale": 1.0, ... }

Start the editor first — the launcher only bridges; the SSE server runs inside the editor process (_server.start_sse() on initialize).

docs.title: Tracker Music (TrackerMusicPlugin)
docs.text:
Tracker-module music: MOD/XM/S3M/IT playback rendered to WAV by the plugin's own software synthesis engine in rend/, plus a pattern editor dock.

NAME VERSION SYSTEM TrackerMusicPlugin 1.0.0 False

Declared in plugins/tracker_music_plugin/__init__.py (packaging manifest plugins/tracker_music_plugin/manifest.json, entry: tracker_music_plugin/__init__.py). Registers the TrackerAudioSource component, dock "Tracker Editor" (area bottom, tab Audio), menu Edit → Open Tracker Editor, toolbar button Tracker, and file openers for .mod .xm .s3m .it.

docs.title: Files (the rend/ engine — not nodmod)
docs.text:
• plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/engine.py — TrackerSoftwareRenderer(_SeqMixin, _FxMixin, _MixMixin), METER_BLOCK_SEC = 0.1.
  • plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/engine_seq.py — sequencer mixin: sample_rate = 44100, voices, n_channels, channel_gains, master_gain, set_channel_db(ch, db), get_meter_data().
  • plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/engine_mix.py — numpy voice mixer (_mix_one, _render_voice_numpy).
  • plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/engine_fx.py — instrument/sample helpers (_sample_for_instrument, _sample_volume, _sample_wave, _sample_loop).
  • plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/defs.py — constants _NTSC_SR = 8287.0, _AMIGA_CLOCK = 3546894.6, _RENDER_VERSION = 3, _MOD_PERIODS, _NOTE_NAMES, plus _note_to_midi() and _parse_effect().
  • plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/service.py — TrackerRenderService(cache_dir, sample_rate=44100), load_module(path), render_to_wav_file(pcm, path, sample_rate), find_external_renderer().
  • plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/voice.py — _Voice.
  • plugins/tracker_music_plugin/tracker_audio_source.py — TrackerAudioSource(AudioSource) component + patch_audio_source_play().
  • Optional Cython mixer: fastmix.pyx / fastmix.c, loaded via import_extension (core/foundation/plugin_cython.py), built by ensure_extensions.

Note: module parsing is delegated to the vendored plugins/tracker_music_plugin/libs/nodmod (load_song); all synthesis is the rend/ engine above.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
TrackerRenderService.render_wav(module_path, quality="software") → cached .wav path (key includes file hash, sample rate, _RENDER_VERSION) or None. quality="external" tries openmpt123/ffmpeg first, then falls back to the software renderer (TrackerSoftwareRenderer(sample_rate).render(song) → stereo 16-bit WAV).

TrackerAudioSource fields: clip_path (module file), render_quality ("software" / "external"), readonly song_length_sec, channels_count (filled from song.get_song_info()). Supported extensions (TRACKER_EXTS): .mod .xm .s3m .it .669 .mtm .stm .ult. play() renders the module to WAV and plays it through AudioSource, restoring the original clip_path afterwards. The plugin also patches stock AudioSource.play (ComponentPatcher.wrap_method, before/after) so a plain AudioSource with a tracker clip_path renders automatically too.

docs.title: Playing a track — example
docs.text:
class Jukebox:
    module: str = "assets/music/level1.xm"

    def on_start(self):
        src = self._entity.get_component_by_name("TrackerAudioSource")
        if src is None:
            return
        src.clip_path = self.module
        src.render_quality = "software"  # or "external" for openmpt123/ffmpeg
        src.play()
        Logger.info(f"Playing: {src.channels_count} ch, {src.song_length_sec:.1f} s")

Steps: add TrackerAudioSource to an entity → set Module to the .xm/.mod file → press Play (or call play()). Open Edit → Open Tracker Editor (or double-click a module file) to inspect patterns via song.get_song_info().

docs.title: Physics Tooling Plugins
docs.text:
Four plugins around the physics core: simulation, debug visualisation, editor drag, and mesh editing.

NAME VERSION SYSTEM PhysicsPlugin 0.4.0 True PhysicsVisualisation 1.1.0 True PhysicsDragPlugin 0.1.0 False MeshEditorPlugin 1.0.0 False

Declared in plugins/physics_plug/plugin.py, plugins/physviz/plugin.py, plugins/physics_drag_plugin.py, plugins/mesh_editor_plugin.py.

docs.title: What each does
docs.text:
PhysicsPlugin (0.4.0, SYSTEM) — the simulation itself (DESCRIPTION = "Physics system with shared-memory parallel simulation."). simulation_mode from project config: multi_threaded (default, PhysicsProcess shared-memory worker), single (in-process solver), per_layer_process. Solver resolved via physics_solvers.registry (normalize, get_module_class, is_available, fallback to DEFAULT_SOLVER). Key API: physics_scene property, ensure_single_mode() -> bool, hooks on_scene_loaded / on_scene_unloaded / on_project_opened. Note: CharacterController only works in-process — without it the controller logs Use single-threaded physics mode (simulation_mode='single') for characters.

PhysicsVisualisation (1.1.0, SYSTEM) — debug arrows through the Gizmos system (tag from physviz/draw.py): velocity / acceleration / moment vectors, contacts, joints, colliders. Settings (all live-patchable via configure(patch)): enabled, show_velocity/acceleration/moment/contacts/joints/colliders, only_selected, show_labels, show_editor/show_runtime, velocity_scale (0.3), acceleration_scale (0.05), moment_scale (0.05), max_length (2.5), min_magnitude (0.1), smooth (0.35), accel_spike (200.0), moment_spike (400.0), label_cap (48), contact_normal_length (0.6). Panel: dock "Physics Visualisation" (area right), menu Tools → Physics Visualisation, 50 ms QTimer refresh in editor, step(dt) redraw in play.

PhysicsDragPlugin (0.1.0, editor tool) — Ctrl+Shift+LeftClick drags simulated bodies in play mode. Installs an event filter on the viewport (on_viewport_ready); on press it casts physics_scene.ray_cast(origin, direction, 1000.0) and accepts only entities with a non-kinematic Rigidbody with mass > 0; move updates update_drag_constraint(id, target) (plane-projected via viewport.screen_to_plane), release calls remove_drag_constraint(id). Scene handle is refreshed from PhysicsPlugin.physics_scene on initialize / on_scene_loaded / on_play_start.

MeshEditorPlugin (1.0.0, ProBuilder-style) — one menu item Mesh Editor → Open Mesh Editor (shortcut Ctrl+Shift+M) opening the main window's _mesh_editor for the first selected entity.

docs.title: Dragging a body — example
docs.text:
# 1. Press Play (drag works only when engine.play_mode is True).
# 2. Hold Ctrl+Shift, left-click a dynamic Rigidbody in the viewport.
# 3. Move the mouse: the hit body follows on the grab plane
#    (debug line body -> anchor while dragging).
# 4. Release the mouse button: constraint removed, body keeps velocity.
#
# Script-side equivalent of what the filter does:
ps = engine.plugin_manager.get("PhysicsPlugin").physics_scene
origin, direction = viewport.screen_to_ray(x, y)
hit = ps.ray_cast(origin, direction, 1000.0)   # {"entity_id", "body_id", "position"}
cid = ps.create_drag_constraint(hit["body_id"], Vec3(*hit["position"]))
ps.update_drag_constraint(cid, new_target)
ps.remove_drag_constraint(cid)

docs.title: Example — chart plus world-space button
docs.text:
# Plotter (editor): select any entity, open the Plotter dock,
# Y-picker -> Transform -> position.x, press "Track", press Play.
# The chart samples the property every refresh_interval ms.

# QtQuick world button (script side, on an entity with QuickButton):
def on_start(self):

    btn.text = "Launch"

docs.title: VR Session Setup (VRPlugin)
docs.text:
Stereo VR integration: OpenXR session, XR rig entities, and the editor control dock.

NAME VERSION SYSTEM VRPlugin 1.0.0 True

Declared in plugins/vr_plugin/plug/plugin.py (VRPluginBase, DESCRIPTION = "VR display integration with OpenXR"). Factory get_plugin() lives in plugins/vr_plugin/plug/__init__.py.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• plugins/vr_plugin/plug/plugin.py — VRPluginBase: dock registration ("VR Control", area bottom), toggle_vr(), spawn_xr_rig(engine), ensure_vr_entities() / remove_vr_entities(), hooks on_scene_loaded / on_viewport_ready.
  • plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_rig.py — XRRig, XRTrackedPoseDriver, XRController, XRHand, XRCull.
  • plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_locomotion.py — XRSmoothMoveProvider, XRSnapTurnProvider, XRTeleportationProvider.
  • plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_haptics.py — XRHaptics.
  • plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_ar.py — ARSession, ARCameraBackground, ARPlaneManager, ARRaycastManager, ARAnchorManager, ARPointCloudManager.
  • plugins/vr_plugin/components/xrinter/ — XRInteractionManager, XRRayInteractor, XRDirectInteractor, XRPokeInteractor, XRGrabInteractable.
  • plugins/vr_plugin/vr_dock.py — VRControlWidget editor panel.
  • plugins/vr_plugin/core/ — runtime: session.py / session2.py (OpenXR session), state.py / state2.py (state, is_available()), swapchain.py (eye framebuffers), controllers.py (controller state, haptics).

docs.title: API
docs.text:
XRRig defaults (xr_rig.py): move_speed = 5.0, turn_speed = 80.0, vert_speed = 2.5, acceleration = 12.0, damping = 8.0, ipd = 0.063, tracking_origin_mode = "Floor", enable_locomotion = True. XRTrackedPoseDriver.pose_source is one of Head, CenterEye, LeftEye, RightEye, LeftHand, RightHand (default Head). XRController(controller_hand) is "Left" / "Right" with SendHapticImpulse(amplitude, duration, frequency) / CancelHaptic().

Core functions (core/__init__.py, state.py): is_available(), is_active(), session_running(), get_ipd() / set_ipd() / reset_ipd(), reset_hmd_origin(), is_eye_view() / set_eye_view() / toggle_eye_view(), get_controllers(), get_hmd_pos_offset(). Eye defaults: textures 1440x1600, vertical FOV 90 deg, horizontal FOV 100 deg.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Yes — an OpenXR runtime is required. is_available() returns _XR_AVAILABLE, which is True only when import xr succeeds (core/state.py). The dock's Initialize VR button stays disabled (setEnabled(avail)) until then, and session.initialize(ctx) refuses to start without it. Without a working OpenXR runtime on the machine, VR stays Off and the scene runs on the desktop camera.

docs.title: Session setup example
docs.text:
# 1. Open the "VR Control" dock (bottom area) and press "Initialize VR".
#    Status flips Off -> Initializing... -> Active (333 ms refresh timer).
# 2. Spawn the rig from code (same call the dock's "Spawn XR Rig" button makes):
rig = plugin.spawn_xr_rig(engine)
# Creates: XRRig (+ XRRig, XRInteractionManager, move/snap/teleport providers)
#   + XRHMD (tracked pose driver, eye height 1.6 m)
#   + XRControllerLeft / XRControllerRight (pose driver + XRController + XRHand)
# 3. Tune in the dock: IPD slider 10..200 mm (default 63 -> 0.063 m),
#    "Reset HMD Origin", "View: Eye/Desktop" toggle.
from plugins.vr_plugin import core as vr_core
vr_core.set_ipd(0.063)
vr_core.set_eye_view(True)   # Eye stereo vs Desktop mirror

When the session is active, on_scene_loaded auto-spawns the rig; when VR is off, rig entities are removed from the scene.

• Transform: Transform — translate(Vec3), rotate(Vec3 degrees), position/rotation/scale, parent-chain.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
• Entity — scene object with UUID, name, parent/children, tags, layer, active toggle. Behavior comes only from components.
  • Component — data + lifecycle hooks (on_awake/on_start/on_update/on_fixed_update/on_destroy/on_enable/on_disable) auto-discovered via ComponentRegistry.
  • ScriptComponent — the component that hosts a user .py behavior: script_path + script_fields + hot_reload.
  • Behavior class — first class in the script file declaring a lifecycle/collision/gizmo member or _inspector_buttons; no base class, constructed with no arguments.
  • Inspector field — annotated class attribute rendered as a widget; values persist per instance in the scene.
  • Play — run mode: scripts load, on_awake/on_start fire, per-frame updates run. Gizmo methods also run outside Play.
  • Hot-reload — mtime-triggered instance recreation during Play preserving Inspector values.
  • Fixed update — physics-clock callback with stable dt (0.02 default); render dt is already time-scaled.
  • Prefab (.zpep) — saved entity subtree with stable GUIDs; instances remap GUIDs and keep overrides.
  • Cython companion — sibling .pyx auto-built into cache/cython on first import, rebuilt when newer.
  • Time scale — multiplier applied to render dt; fixed-step dt stays constant.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
• Script does nothing on Play? The Script field is empty or points at a moved file (script_path is project-root-relative). Re-pick it; the Check action reports file:line errors.
  • Vec3.rotate missing? Correct — rotation lives on Transform.rotate(Vec3 degrees). Vec3 offers dot/cross/length/normalized/lerp, not rotate.
  • core.math3d import fails? Import from core.maths.math3d. The Check button suggests exactly this.
  • Edit during Play lost state? Expected: __init__ state resets on reload by design; keep tunable state in Inspector fields and rebuild caches in on_awake/on_start.
  • Ball falls through the floor? Missing collider, Is Trigger without contact handling, or Is Kinematic where solver motion is expected.
  • No sound? clip_path empty/unresolvable, AudioListener missing from the camera entity, or play() called with no AudioSystem in a headless context.
  • First Play is slow with .pyx? One-time native compile into cache/cython; later runs reuse it. The Check button validates .pyx without a C compiler.

docs.text: Panel light: AreaLight (core/components/lighting/lightp/shadows.py:79-185) with nit brightness, rect/disk shape and multi-sample shadows. Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Surface brightness in nits (cd/m²): monitor 200, office panel 500, overcast sky 2000, softbox 10000. Same nits on a bigger panel lights more (shadows.py:92). Gizmo draws the rect frame, optional disk ring and double-sided back frame (shadows.py:118-161).

docs.title: Camera
docs.text: Scene camera: Camera component (core/components/rendering/cameras/camera.py) with perspective/orthographic projection, depth ordering and native/custom render size. Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: View matrix is Mat4.look_at(position, position + forward, up); projection is Mat4.perspective(fov, aspect, near, far) or orthographic with half_w = ortho_size * aspect (camera.py:56-69). Gizmo draws the frustum from near/far corners (camera.py:100-143). Base clamps and render-size logic live in CameraBase (camera_base.py).

docs.text: Forward OpenGL renderer: Renderer facade in core/renderer/renderer.py draws the scene into the viewport FBO in opaque then transparent phases. Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: ZarinEngine uses a forward renderer built on moderngl. Entry context is created in main.py: QSurfaceFormat, OpenGL 4.6 Core profile, depth buffer 24, swap interval from rendering.vsync (0 off / 1 on). Renderer composes mixins: config, programs, voxel, object-fx, framebuffers, water, uniforms, skinned, collector, geometry cache, outline, gizmo, icon, cubemap, post, scene (core/renderer/renderer.py:56). Render modes are RenderMode.SHADED / SHADED_WIREFRAME / FLAT (core/renderer/types.py). Default caps: _max_lights = 8, ambient [0.26, 0.28, 0.34], selection outline [0.8, 0.5, 0.1, 1.0] thickness 0.03 (core/renderer/renderer.py:90-114).

docs.title: Properties

See Pipeline, Camera, Gizmos. ## Usage in Code

renderer.render_scene(scene, view_mat, proj_mat, cam_pos, w, h)

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text: Forward pipeline in SceneRendererMixin.render_scene: collect snapshot → shadow maps → opaque phase → transparent phase → environment (sky/water/clouds) → editor overlays. Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: render_scene(scene, view_mat, proj_mat, cam_pos, viewport_w, viewport_h, ...) (core/renderer/scenev/mixin.py:24) applies _render_scale to get render size, collects a _RenderSnapshot (lights, dir_light, sky/cloud/water components, renderable entries), renders shadow maps via ShadowRenderer, then calls _scenev_render_forward_phases(opaque, transparent, ...) (core/renderer/scenev/forward.py:19). Transparent phase enables SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA blending with depth_mask = False. Specialized passes: WaterPassMixin, VoxelPassMixin, SkinnedPassMixin, cubemap pass for dynamic reflections, GizmoPassMixin/IconPassMixin/OutlinePassMixin for the editor.

docs.text:

Stats overlay reads _draw_calls, _opaque_draws, _trans_draws, _triangles_drawn. ## Usage in Code 
renderer.render_scene(scene, cam.get_view_matrix(),
                      cam.get_projection_matrix(aspect),
                      cam_pos, 1280, 720)

docs.title: PostFX Stack
docs.text:
Post-effects run in component order after the main scene pass. Each effect is a GraphicsEffect component with an enable toggle and its own Inspector fields. One page per effect:

  • Bloom

  • Color Grading
  • Depth of Field

  • Dithering
  • Edge Detection
  • Film Grain
  • Fog

  • Kuwahara
  • Lens Distortion
  • Lens Flares
  • Motion Blur

  • Quantize
  • Radial Blur
  • Scanlines
  • Sharpen
  • Sobel
  • SSAO
  • SSR
  • SVGF
  • Vignette
  • Watercolor

Recipes: clean 3D (FXAA, Color Grading, Vignette), cinematic (Bloom, Depth of Field, Film Grain, Color Grading), retro (Pixelate, Scanlines, Dithering), horror (Fog, Vignette, Chromatic Aberration, Sharpen).

docs.text: surface_type: Ocean (infinite, ocean_size) or Pond (pond_size). Eight default Gerstner-ish waves[i] = {direction, amplitude, wavelength, speed, steepness} (component.py:14-23). Interaction + sim blocks drive shore ripples (sim_damping / sim_propagation / sim_saturation / sim_disp_scale / sim_normal_scale).

docs.title: Dissolve
docs.text: Noise-gradient burn-off. Fragments past amount (biased by directional gradient × noise_strength + noise field × noise_scale) are discarded; a band of width edge_width glows with edge_color × edge_emission. Optional time animation drives amount 0→1 (ping-pong or loop). Class DissolveEffect in core/components/rendering/effects/dissolve_effect.py. ObjectFx pass (core/renderer/object_fx_pass.py): enabled DissolveEffect components are collected per entity (_find_object_effect) and bound in the FX program before the mesh draw.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Inspector Field Type Range Default Amount amount SLIDER 0.0 – 1.0 0.0 Noise Strength noise_strength SLIDER 0.0 – 1.0 1.0 Noise Scale noise_scale FLOAT 0.1 – 20.0 4.0 Gradient Direction direction VEC3 -1.0 – 1.0 (0.0, 1.0, 0.0) Invert invert BOOL — False Edge Width edge_width SLIDER 0.0 – 0.5 0.05 Edge Color edge_color COLOR — [1.0, 0.4, 0.05] Edge Emission edge_emission SLIDER 0.0 – 5.0 2.5 Animate animate BOOL — False Speed speed FLOAT 0.0 – 5.0 0.5 Ping Pong ping_pong BOOL — False

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Editor: select the mesh entity, Add Component > DissolveEffect, tick enabled, animate the amount fields from a script.

Code:

from core.components.rendering.effects.dissolve_effect import DissolveEffect
fx = DissolveEffect()
entity.add_component(fx)
fx.amount = 0.5
fx.edge_width = 0.08
fx.animate = True
fx.enabled = True
# per-frame: fx.amount = min(1.0, fx.amount + dt * 0.5)

docs.title: Polygon Disintegration
docs.text: Triangle-ejection shatter. Per-cell hash (cell_size/noise_scale/stagger/thr_scale) gates ejection by amount; ejected tris fly along direction + outward normal with speed±variance, scatter/jitter, drag, gravity, spin/twist; fade shrinks alpha; surviving fringe glows with edge_width/color/emission. Optional animate/ping_pong drives amount. Class PolygonDisintegrationEffect in core/components/rendering/effects/polygon_disintegration_effect.py. ObjectFx pass with GEOMETRY-shader path: fx_geometry_shader path ejects whole triangles (see spike_growth u_spike_* geometry precedent); double_sided controls culling in _render_object_effects.

docs.title: Spike Growth
docs.text: Geometry-shader spikes. Each triangle extrudes up to 4× (max 12 verts) along normals; length × amount sets height, radius shrinks the base, noise/cell vary per-spike length, twist rotates, emission/color + rim shade the spikes. ObjectFx geometry-shader extrusion (layout triangles → triangle_strip max_vertices = 12): vertices push along normals by length × amount with cell noise.

docs.title: Tree Wind
docs.text: Vegetation wind for trees. Normalized wind_direction × wind_strength × wind_influence bends trunks/branches at wind_speed; leaves add high-frequency flutter (leaf_flutter_speed/amount); turbulence_scale/amount adds gust noise. Disabled fast-path writes _WindInfluence = 0. Class TreeWindEffect in core/components/rendering/effects/tree_wind_effect.py. ObjectFx pass but with Tree material path: fx_geometry_shader() loads Tree.gshader (core/renderer/meshd.read_shader); _Wind* uniforms target the Tree/vegetation shader, not ObjectFx.shader.

docs.title: Voxel Raymarch
docs.text: Mesh→volume raymarch. Host mesh is voxelized on CPU into a 3D texture (dims clamped to 192 max), then a fullscreen pass raymarches (max_steps) with Beer-Lambert-ish alpha × opacity × amount, shaded by color/emission/rim and light_dir. Blends with SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA over the scene color target. Class VoxelRaymarchEffect in core/components/rendering/effects/voxelp/effect.py. NOTE: despite living under effects/, this is a GraphicsEffect (fullscreen raymarch into a 3D occupancy texture), not an ObjectEffect. Requires a MeshFilter on the same entity to build the grid; disabled/fast-pathed when amount/opacity ≤ 0.001.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Inspector Field Type Range Default Amount amount SLIDER 0.0 – 1.0 1.0 Voxel Size voxel_size FLOAT — 0.3 Voxel Color color COLOR — [0.4, 1.0, 0.6] Glow emission FLOAT — 0.6 Rim Power rim FLOAT — 2.5 Opacity opacity SLIDER 0.0 – 1.0 1.0 Max Steps max_steps INT 32 – 1024 256 Light Dir light_dir VEC3 — (0.4, 0.8, 0.3)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Editor: select the mesh entity, Add Component > VoxelRaymarchEffect, tick enabled, animate the amount fields from a script.

Code:

from core.components.rendering.effects.voxelp.effect import VoxelRaymarchEffect
fx = VoxelRaymarchEffect()
entity.add_component(fx)
fx.voxel_size = 0.2
fx.max_steps = 128
fx.opacity = 0.9
fx.enabled = True
# per-frame: fx.amount = min(1.0, fx.amount + dt * 0.5)

docs.title: Voxelize
docs.text: Mesh→cubes breakup. CPU voxelizer (voxel_cpu.compute_voxel_instances) bins the mesh into voxel_size grid (world_grid toggles world vs local snap, jitter offsets); cubes shaded with color/emission/rim; amount cross-fades; cell is the shading cell; optional animate/ping_pong. Class VoxelizeEffect in core/components/rendering/effects/voxelize_effect.py. ObjectFx pass + instanced cubes path: _render_voxel_instances() in object_fx_pass.py draws voxel cubes when enabled and amount > 0; show_base_mesh toggles the original mesh draw.

docs.title: Light Units
docs.text:
Physical units per light type — lux for directional, lumens for point/spot, nits for area — the in-code reference tables, legacy multipliers, and a setup guide.

Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Base class Light (core/components/lighting/lightp/light.py:25-90) stores color, intensity (0–200000), and cast_shadows. Units depend on the concrete type: DirectionalLight reads lux, PointLight/SpotLight read lumens, AreaLight reads nits. Internal conversion factors are LUX_TO_RADIANCE = 1e-5, CANDELA_TO_RADIANCE = 1e-2, AREA_TO_RADIANCE = 1e-2 (light.py:33-35).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: name type default description DirectionalLight.intensity float, lux 100000.0 Illuminance in lux (light.py:198,205). PointLight.intensity float, lumens 1000.0 Total flux in lumens (light.py:241,248). SpotLight.intensity float, lumens in cone 1000.0 Same lumens concentrated by the cone angle (light.py:317,327). AreaLight.intensity float, nits 100.0 Surface brightness in cd/m² (shadows.py:92,106). Light.color color3 [1,1,1] Light color (light.py:72,78). Light.cast_shadows bool True Shadow-map contribution (light.py:74,80).

docs.title: Reference tables (verbatim keys, light.py:40-64)
docs.text: LUX_REFERENCE: direct_sun 100000.0, full_daylight 15000.0, overcast_day 5000.0, sunrise_sunset 400.0, office 500.0, twilight 10.0, full_moon 0.2. LUMEN_REFERENCE: candle 12.57, decorative_led 100.0, desk_lamp 300.0, room_ceiling 800.0, bulb_100w 1600.0, street_light 15000.0, stadium_floodlight 100000.0. NIT_REFERENCE: monitor_sdr 200.0, office_panel 500.0, overcast_sky 2000.0, clear_sky 5000.0, led_softbox 10000.0.

docs.title: Setup guide
docs.text:
• Sun: DirectionalLight, intensity = 100000.0 (direct sun). Overcast day 5000, sunrise 400.
  • Bulb/lamp: PointLight, intensity = 1000.0 (≈100 W bulb is 1600 lm; desk lamp 300 lm). Set range to the room size.
  • Flashlight/spot: SpotLight, intensity = 1000.0; narrow cones look brighter because the same lumens are concentrated.
  • Softbox/panel: AreaLight, intensity = 100.0 default; office panel ≈ 500 nits, LED softbox ≈ 10000 nits. Bigger panels emit more total light at equal nits.
  • Fill lights: switch cast_shadows off.

docs.title: Legacy migration
docs.text: Scenes with light_version < 2 are auto-rescaled (light.py:36-38,166-167): LEGACY_DIRECTIONAL_MULT = 100000.0, LEGACY_POINT_MULT = 2000.0 (also applied to spot), LEGACY_AREA_MULT = 100.0. New scenes serialize light_version: 2 (light.py:134).

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
from core.components.lighting.lightp.light import DirectionalLight
sun = entity.get_component(DirectionalLight)
sun.color = [1.0, 0.95, 0.9]
sun.intensity = 100000.0
sun.cast_shadows = True

docs.title: Material Library
docs.text:
Every shipped material asset under assets/materials/ (currently a single .mat file), the .mat JSON field table from core/assets/matp/materials.py, and a verbatim example.

Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Material assets are .mat JSON files (Material { name, shader_path, properties }), loaded by Material (core/assets/matp/materials.py:14-169) and cached by MaterialManager (core/renderer/mats/manager.py:54-80). shader_path = "default" maps to the built-in PBR; any other path is resolved against the project root first, then engine core/shaders/ (materials.py:26-46). Missing files warn once and fall back to default (manager.py:63-71). No .zpem files ship under assets/ at time of writing.

docs.text:
field type default description name string "" Material name (materials.py:14-24). shader_path string "default" .shader path or "default" for built-in PBR (materials.py:48-52,110-118). Non-.shader extensions are rejected when loading shader properties. properties object {} Shader uniforms (manager.py:89-96). Missing keys are back-filled from the shader's Properties defaults (materials.py:63-66).

Shader resolution order for a non-default path (materials.py:26-46): absolute path if it exists → <project_root>/<path> → <engine_root>/<path> → <engine_root>/core/shaders/<path> → basename lookup inside materials/, internal/, compute/, include/, legacy/.

docs.title: PostFX Stack Order
docs.text:
The exact frame order — snapshot → shadow pass → opaque/transparent forward phases → additive effects → screen-effect chain → tonemap hook — how to order effects, and how the tonemapping hook works.

Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
One frame in SceneRendererMixin.render_scene (core/renderer/scenev/mixin.py:24) runs in this order:

  1. Snapshot — _collect_snapshot(scene, ...) (mixin.py:54) gathers lights, sky, renderable entries, sprites, videos, SVGs, particles into a _RenderSnapshot.
  2. Shadow pass — _scenev_render_shadow_pass(...) (mixin.py:144) renders CSM/point/spot/area shadow maps.
  3. Skybox + forward phases — sky render (mixin.py:158), then _scenev_partition_and_sort splits opaque vs transparent (mixin.py:204) and _scenev_render_forward_phases draws opaque first, transparent second (core/renderer/scenev/forward.py:19-34).
  4. Additive effects — every GraphicsEffect with render_type != "screen" renders directly into the scene FBO (output.py:269-281).
  5. Screen-effect chain — render_type == "screen" effects run ping-pong between _se_fbo_a / _se_fbo_b in registry order (output.py:285-324).
  6. Tonemap hook — _present_composite (post_pass.py:28-44) presents the composite texture.

docs.title: How to order effects
docs.text:
• Execution order inside each group (additive, screen) is GraphicsEffect._registry order — i.e. component creation/enable order (graphics_effect.py:16,39-54). There is no numeric priority field; reorder by re-adding components or toggling enabled/entity.active.
  • render_type is a class attribute (graphics_effect.py:18): most postfx (bloom excluded) use "screen"; Bloom and lens-flare style effects use "additive" and run before the screen chain.
  • Skipped effects cost nothing: should_skip() (graphics_effect.py:28-37) drops disabled/inactive entities and any effect whose _intensity_prop is <= 0.001 (plus _skip_rate frame skipping).

docs.title: Tonemapping hook
docs.text:
PostPassMixin._has_tonemap_effect (post_pass.py:18-25):

def _has_tonemap_effect(self):
    if not GraphicsEffect._registry:
        return False
    from core.components.rendering.postfx.color_grading import ColorGrading
    for e in GraphicsEffect._registry:
        if isinstance(e, ColorGrading) and e.enabled and e.entity and e.entity.active:
            return True
    return False

_present_composite (post_pass.py:28-44): if a live ColorGrading effect exists (or the tonemap program is missing), the plain copy program is used — tonemapping is then owned by ColorGrading in the screen chain. Otherwise the built-in tonemap program runs with u_exposure from self._exposure.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: name type default description GraphicsEffect.render_type "additive" / "screen" "additive" Which group the effect runs in (graphics_effect.py:18). GraphicsEffect._intensity_prop string "" Auto-skip knob; effect skipped when <= 0.001 (graphics_effect.py:32-36). GraphicsEffect._skip_rate int 0 Render every N+1-th frame when > 0 (graphics_effect.py:29-31). renderer._exposure float 0.0 Exposure fed to u_exposure only on the built-in tonemap path (renderer.py:172, post_pass.py:41).

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
fx.enabled = True           # include in the chain
fx.render_type              # "screen" -> ping-pong chain, "additive" -> scene FBO
GraphicsEffect._registry    # order == execution order within each group

docs.title: Raytracing Setup
docs.text:
Raytracing.compute kernel contract, component knobs, hard limits, and performance guidance.

Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The path-tracer is a #version 430 core compute kernel (local_size 8×8, core/shaders/compute/Raytracing.compute:13-15) driven by the RaytraceRenderer component split across core/components/rendering/renderers/raytrace/ (component.py, dispatch.py, denoise.py).

docs.title: Kernel properties (verbatim, Raytracing.compute:3-11)
docs.text:
Properties
{
    _MaxBounces("Max Bounces", Int) = 1
    _SamplesPerPixel("Samples Per Pixel", Int) = 1
    _ResolutionScale("Resolution Scale", Float) = 1.0
    _Accumulate("Accumulate Frames", Int) = 0
    _HeatmapMode("Heatmap Mode", Int) = 0
    _HeatmapScale("Heatmap Scale", Float) = 40.0
}

Hard GLSL limits (Raytracing.compute:17-18): #define MAX_INSTANCES 256, #define MAX_LIGHTS 8. Extra instances/lights are dropped during scene upload (denoise.py:85,217-243).

docs.title: Component knobs (raytrace/component.py:31-49)
docs.text:
field range default description _resolution_scale 0.1–1.0 0.5 Trace resolution factor; dispatch size max(1, size × scale) (dispatch.py:17-18). _max_bounces 1–16 1 → u_max_bounces. _samples_per_pixel 1–16 1 → u_samples_per_pixel. _accumulate bool False → u_accumulate; progressive refine (dispatch.py:126). _show_overlay bool True Composite overlay presentation. _heatmap_mode 0–2 0 → u_heatmap_mode (off/cost diagnostic). _heatmap_scale 1–256 40.0 → u_heatmap_scale.

Buffers bound at dispatch: BVH nodes (0), vertices (1), indices (2), materials (3), instances (4), lights (5), plus rgba32f output/emissive images and a 32-layer albedo texture array (_MAX_ALBEDO_LAYERS = 32, component.py:17, dispatch.py:79).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• OpenGL 4.3+ compute (SSBO + image load/store, #version 430 core).
  • Scene caps: 256 instances, 8 lights, 32 albedo layers — components beyond the cap are ignored with no error besides the drop.
  • Rays/frame accounting: rw × rh × spp × (bounces + 1) (dispatch.py:271, surfaced as _rt_rays_per_frame).

docs.title: Performance notes
docs.text: Cost scales linearly with pixels (× resolution_scale²), spp, and bounces+1. Start at 0.5 scale / 1 bounce / 1 spp, enable _accumulate for stills, and use _heatmap_mode to find hot spots before raising quality.

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
rt._resolution_scale = 0.5
rt._max_bounces = 1
rt._samples_per_pixel = 1
rt._accumulate = False

docs.title: Shadows Tuning
docs.text:
Resolution/distance/cascade defaults per light type, bias constants, and performance notes — all from code.

Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Shadow settings have two layers: the DirectionalShadow scene component (authored values) and renderer fallbacks (core/renderer/renderer.py:125-131) used when no component is present. The shadow backend is ShadowRenderer (core/renderer/shadows/renderer.py:23-30).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
setting authored default (DirectionalShadow) renderer fallback code Directional resolution 4096 2048 directional_shadow.py:45, renderer.py:125 Shadow distance 50.0 m 50.0 m directional_shadow.py:46, renderer.py:126 Cascades 4 4 directional_shadow.py:48, renderer.py:127 Cascade splits (4) [0.05, 0.13, 0.3] computed log/linear blend (lam = 0.9) directional_shadow.py:18, csm.py:69-75 Point resolution — 512 renderer.py:129 Area resolution — 512 renderer.py:130 Spot resolution — 1024 renderer.py:131 u_shadow_bias — 0.0015 shadows/uniforms.py:213 u_shadow_normal_bias — 0.02 shadows/uniforms.py:214 area_shadow_bias 0.005 (per AreaLight) 0.005 light.py:90, shadows/area.py:71-73

Cascade tile resolutions for a 4-cascade map derive from the base: [base, max(512, base//2), max(512, base//2), max(256, base//4)] (shadows/uniforms.py:33), with a static atlas layout of [2048, 1024, 1024, 512] in the renderer (shadows/renderer.py:70).

docs.title: Tuning guide
docs.text:
• Directional: resolution slider 256–4096 step 256, distance 1–500 m, cascades 1–4 (directional_shadow.py:33-40). 4096 + 4 cascades is the authored default; drop to 2048/2 cascades for low-end.
  • Splits: defaults per count are {2: [0.5], 3: [0.2, 0.6], 4: [0.05, 0.13, 0.3]} (directional_shadow.py:18, mirrored in editor/cascade_split_widget.py:15). Push splits outward to cover far ground, inward for close-up detail.
  • Point/spot/area: fixed at 512/1024/512 in the renderer; disable cast_shadows on fill lights instead of lowering globally.
  • Acne vs peter-panning: raise u_shadow_bias/u_shadow_normal_bias against acne; raise area_shadow_bias (0–0.1, step 0.001) per area light (shadows.py:100).

docs.title: Performance notes
docs.text: Shadow cost scales with cascade count × tile resolution plus one 512² cube-ish pass per point light and one 1024² pass per spot. ShadowRenderer clamps cascades to 1–4 (shadows/renderer.py:25). Outline queue rendering is capped at 512 entries (output.py:397).

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
from core.components.rendering.environment.directional_shadow import DirectionalShadow
ds = DirectionalShadow()
ds._shadow_resolution = 4096
ds._shadow_distance = 50.0
ds._set_cascade_count(4)

docs.title: Splat Pipeline
docs.text:
Gaussian splat ingest → GPU upload → sorted rasterization: supported formats, SH degree, opacity cutoff, GL requirements, and the _splat_sort sorter.

Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: GaussianSplatRenderer (core/components/rendering/renderers/gaussian_splat_renderer.py:12-35) points at a splat file and tunes evaluation. The GPU backend is _SplatResourcesMixin (core/renderer/splat/resources.py:330-388); sorting uses the optional Cython core._splat_sort module (core/renderer/splat/sort.py:31-34, built in core/build_cython.py:127).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: name type default description ply_path resource path "" Splat file; picker filter Splats (*.ply *.sog *.ssog) (gaussian_splat_renderer.py:23-24). sh_degree int slider 0–3 3 Spherical-harmonics degree uploaded as u_sh_degree (gaussian_splat_renderer.py:25-26, resources.py:385-386). opacity_threshold float 0–1 0.005 Opacity cutoff uploaded as u_opacity_threshold (gaussian_splat_renderer.py:27-28, resources.py:387-388).

docs.title: Formats and import
docs.text: _is_sog_style (resources.py:306-313) treats these as directory/archive-style splats: .sog, .ssog, .zip, paths ending in /meta.json or /lod-meta.json, or basenames meta.json / lod-meta.json. Everything else goes through _load_splat_file (resources.py:316-327): the first 4 lines are sniffed — binary PLY takes the fast path (_load_splat_fast), otherwise the generic loader (_load_splat_generic). Relative ply_path values resolve against the project root with an assets/ fallback (post_pass.py:47-61).

docs.title: GPU requirements and sorting
docs.text:
• Shader init failure logs GaussianSplatRenderer shader init failed (needs OpenGL 4.3+): ... and disables the program/VAO (resources.py:342-345). SSBO storage buffers are used (_ensure_buffers, _bind_gpu_draw binding points 0–1).
  • Per-frame uniforms: u_model, u_view, u_proj, u_viewport, u_camera_pos, u_sh_degree, u_opacity_threshold (resources.py:369-388).
  • Sorting uses splat_cull_depth, compact_keep, radix_sort_into, remap_order from core._splat_sort when compiled, with a NumPy fallback (splat/sort.py:31-34,168).

docs.title: Usage in Code
docs.text:
from core.components.rendering.renderers.gaussian_splat_renderer import GaussianSplatRenderer
gs = GaussianSplatRenderer()
gs.ply_path = "assets/splats/scan.ply"
gs.sh_degree = 3
gs.opacity_threshold = 0.005
entity.add_component(gs)

docs.title: Voxel Pipeline
docs.text:
Object voxelization (VoxelizeEffect), the voxel_pass instancing backend with its hard caps, and the screen-space VoxelRaymarchEffect.

Home · Section index

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Two components cover voxels: VoxelizeEffect (an ObjectEffect that voxelizes the host mesh) and VoxelRaymarchEffect (a GraphicsEffect that raymarches a 3D occupancy texture). Instanced voxel cubes are drawn by VoxelPassMixin (core/renderer/voxel_pass.py:18-25).

docs.title: VoxelizeEffect (core/components/rendering/effects/voxelize_effect.py:18-52)
docs.text:
name type default description amount slider 0–1 0.5 Blend between base mesh and voxels. show_base_mesh bool True Keep drawing the original mesh. world_grid bool False Snap voxels to a world grid instead of object space. voxel_size float 0.3 Target voxel size; also cell = 0.3. scale vec3 [1,1,1] Per-voxel cube scale. jitter float 0.0 Cell jitter seed factor. emission float 2.5 Voxel glow. color color3 [0.4, 1.0, 0.6] Voxel tint. rim float 2.5 Rim power. double_sided bool True Two-sided voxel cubes. animate / speed_anim / ping_pong bool / float / bool False / 0.5 / False Auto-animate amount 0→1.

Voxel cells are computed on CPU by compute_voxel_instances and cached per (mesh, size, grid, jitter) key (voxelize_effect.py:59-72).

docs.title: voxel_pass caps (core/renderer/voxel_pass.py:22-25)
docs.text:
constant value meaning _VOX_MAX_DIM 128 Max grid dimension; larger extents rescale the cell (voxel_pass.py:304-309). _VOX_MAX_INSTANCES 2200000 Instance clamp: need_inst = min(total, _VOX_MAX_INSTANCES) (voxel_pass.py:164).

The instanced vertex shader (_VOXEL_INST_VERT, #version 330 core) packs i_cell.xyz (center) + i_cell.w (cull flag) with u_vox_size/u_vox_scale.

docs.title: VoxelRaymarchEffect (core/components/rendering/effects/voxelp/effect.py:22-59)
docs.text:
A GraphicsEffect (render_type = "additive", _intensity_prop = "amount", multi-instance allowed) rendering a fullscreen raymarch over a texture3d occupancy grid built from the host MeshFilter.

name type default description amount slider 0–1 1.0 Effect intensity (auto-skipped at <= 0.001). voxel_size float 0.3 Grid cell size. color color3 [0.4, 1.0, 0.6] Voxel color. emission float 0.6 Glow. rim float 2.5 Rim power. opacity slider 0–1 1.0 Output opacity. max_steps int 32–1024 256 Raymarch steps. light_dir vec3 [0.4, 0.8, 0.3] March lighting direction.

Grid build cap: max_dim = 192 — if ceil(extent / cell) exceeds it, the cell is enlarged to max(extent) / 192 (effect.py:164-167).

from core.components.rendering.effects.voxelize_effect import VoxelizeEffect
vx = VoxelizeEffect()
vx.amount = 0.5
vx.voxel_size = 0.3
entity.add_component(vx)

docs.title: Audio Scripting
docs.text: Triggering and tuning sounds from gameplay code. Component: AudioSource (get_component_by_name("AudioSource")).

docs.title: Fields (all live-tunable)
docs.text: Field Default Notes clip_path "" Audio resource; empty ⇒ play() is a no-op. volume 1.0 0–1. Multiplied by fade volume each frame. pitch 1.0 −3…3. loop False Re-plays from on_update when the voice ends. play_on_awake False Auto-play() in on_start when a clip is set. spatial_blend 1.0 0 = 2D, 1 = 3D. zone_shape SPHERE AudioZoneShape enum. volume_rolloff [[0, 1], [1, 0]] Linear falloff curve points. min_distance / max_distance 1.0 / 50.0 3D attenuation range. box_inner_size / box_outer_size (2,2,2) / (10,10,10) Box-zone extents (Vec3). offset 0.0 Start offset in seconds. fade_in_time / fade_out_time 0.0 Automatic fades around play()/stop().

docs.title: Methods and lifecycle
docs.text:
Signature Behavior src.play() Starts the voice; returns silently if no clip or already playing. Applies fade_in_time when > 0. src.stop() If fade_out_time > 0, fades out first, then stops; otherwise stops immediately. Fires on_stopped. src.is_playing: bool Read-only property. src.fade_in(duration) / src.fade_out(duration) Manual fade envelopes. AudioSource.linear_preset() / AudioSource.logarithmic_preset() Rolloff curve factories. src.on_finished / src.on_stopped Optional zero-arg callables.

Critical auto-start rule: on_enable plays whenever clip_path is set and nothing is playing — independent of play_on_awake. Toggling an entity active with a clip restarts its sound. on_disable/on_destroy stop the voice immediately.

docs.title: Footsteps + gunshot example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
class Footsteps:
    step_gap: float = 0.35
    shot_clip: str = "assets/audio/shot.wav"

    def on_start(self):
        self.step_src = self._entity.get_component_by_name("AudioSource")
        self.timer = 0.0
        self.moving = False

    def on_update(self, dt):
        self.moving = Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W) or Input.GetKey(KeyCode.A) \
            or Input.GetKey(KeyCode.S) or Input.GetKey(KeyCode.D)
        if self.step_src is None:
            return
        if self.moving:
            self.timer += dt
            if self.timer >= float(self.step_gap):
                self.timer = 0.0
                # restart the step sound even if the previous step still rings:
                self.step_src.stop()
                self.step_src.play()
        else:
            self.timer = float(self.step_gap)  # next step is immediate

        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.MOUSE_LEFT):
            self.play_one_shot(self.shot_clip, volume=0.9)

    def play_one_shot(self, clip, volume=1.0):
        scene = self._entity._scene
        e = scene.create_entity("OneShot")
        from core.components.transform.tr import Transform
        e.add_component(Transform())
        from core.ecs import ComponentRegistry
        cls = ComponentRegistry.get("AudioSource")
        voice = cls()
        voice.clip_path = clip
        voice.volume = float(volume)
        voice.spatial_blend = 0.0
        e.add_component(voice)
        voice.play()
        self._cleanup = getattr(self, "_cleanup", {})
        self._cleanup[e.id] = 2.0

    def on_fixed_update(self, dt):
        for eid in list(getattr(self, "_cleanup", {}).keys()):
            self._cleanup[eid] -= dt
            if self._cleanup[eid] <= 0.0:
                scene = self._entity._scene
                if scene.get_entity(eid) is not None:
                    scene.remove_entity(eid)
                del self._cleanup[eid]

Notes on the snippet: stop() before play() re-triggers a looping/off voice; the one-shot helper creates a bare entity + Transform + AudioSource purely from verified APIs and cleans it up after 2 s. ComponentRegistry.get("AudioSource") returns the registered class.

Per-clip volume/pitch from the Inspector: expose volume: float / pitch: float script fields and assign them to the source in on_start — the source fields are plain attributes.

docs.title: Cython in Scripts
docs.text:
Heavy computations move to a Cython module next to the plain script — no manual build steps, no polluted script folders.

Setup:

  1. Project → Create → Cython Script creates fast_sum.pyx with a working template.
  2. A plain script in the same folder writes import fast_sum.
  3. Before import, the engine prepares the script folder on the module search path, then on first import compiles the extension into cache/cython automatically. On Windows the bundled MinGW toolchain is discovered by the engine itself.
import move_fast


class Mover:
    speed: float = 5.0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        step = move_fast.clamp_step(self.speed * dt, 0.0, 1.0)
        t = self._entity.transform
        if t:
            t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, step))

cpdef double clamp_step(double value, double lo, double hi):
    if value < lo:
        return lo
    if value > hi:
        return hi
    return value

Rules and mechanics:

  • The module name is top-level: import foo where foo.pyx sits next to the script. Names must be unique within the project. A neighboring foo.pxd declaration file is tracked for rebuilds too.
  • Rebuilds are automatic when the .pyx (or .pxd) is newer than the cached build. Artifacts live in cache/cython under build/<dirhash16>/<fingerprint12> (directory hash + 12-hex source fingerprint over .pyx, neighboring .pxd, Cython version and toolchain); only the last 3 builds per script folder are kept. The script folder stays clean. Editing .pyx during Play triggers a script hot-reload as usual.
  • The Check button validates .pyx without a C compiler (Cython parsing and typing only). The full native build happens lazily on first import.
  • If no compiler is found, the console shows an actionable error and the script keeps working on the previous working build — iteration never hard-blocks on toolchain setup.
  • Keep the Python/Cython boundary typed (cpdef, typed locals) and batch calls: one call processing an array beats per-element calls across the boundary.

When to reach for it: per-frame math over many elements (crowds, particles logic, procedural deformation), tight loops the profiler attributes to a script, and numeric kernels. Game flow, input and orchestration stay in plain Python.

Troubleshooting: stale results → touch the .pyx (mtime drives rebuilds); import errors → module name collision within the project, rename uniquely; slow first Play → that is the one-time compile, later runs reuse cache/cython.

docs.text: Where errors go, how to check a script before Play, and what the runtime hides from you.

docs.title: The Check button (Script Editor)
docs.text:
Toolbar button Check (Run → Check Script menu duplicates it):

Location Behavior editor/panels/script_editor_panel/wid/widget.py:196-197 QAction("Check"), tooltip "Check script for errors" → _check_current(). editor/panels/script_editor_panel/wid/tabs_host.py:135-157 _check_current(): reads the live diagnostics of the current tab and shows a message box: No errors or warnings found. on clean; error [line N]: message (first 15) + warning [line N]: message (first 15) otherwise. Status label shows ✖ E ⚠ W / ⚠ W / ✓ clean.

This is editor-side static analysis. The runtime adds a second net below.

docs.title: Runtime error net (ScriptComponent)
docs.text:
core/components/scripting/scriptc/hotreload.py:99-149 — _collect_script_errors(path) returns file:line: strings:

Format Meaning path:0: cannot read file: ... File unreadable. path:lineno:offset: SyntaxError: msg ast.parse failed. path:lineno: No module named 'core.X' (did you mean 'core.maths.math3d' ...) Bad core.* import; note the hint — the math module is core.maths.math3d, not core.math3d. path:lineno: cannot import name 'Y' from 'core.X' Wrong symbol from a valid module. path:lineno: ExcType: msg Top-level execution error (traceback line extracted).

With errors present, the class is not loaded (_py_instance = None, fields cleared) and the message is logged once per file revision via Logger.error.

Callback exceptions (_call_py, hotreload.py:253-260):

try:
    meth(*args)
except Exception as e:
    Logger.error(f"Script {canonical} error '{self.script_path}': {e}")

Only str(e) is logged — no traceback, no line number. When a Play-mode error names the method but not the line, reproduce it under the Check button or wrap the suspect block yourself (see below). Hot-reload failures additionally keep the previous working version (hotreload.py:292-301): failed reload restores old class/instance/methods and retries on the next mtime change.

docs.title: Logger levels
docs.text:
core/foundation/logger.py — LogLevel: DEBUG = 0, INFO = 1, WARNING = 2, ERROR = 3:

Call Behavior Logger.debug(msg) / info / warning Emitted when _min_level allows; stored + broadcast to listeners (the editor console panel is one). Logger.error(msg, exc=None) Includes a formatted traceback only when exc is passed. Logger.get_entries() / Logger.clear() / add_listener(fn) History inspection and subscription.

Logger is injected into every behavior script automatically.

docs.title: Diagnostics example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
A script that makes runtime failures locatable despite the str(e)-only logging:

import traceback


class Diagnosable:
    verbose: bool = True

    def on_start(self):
        Logger.info(f"Diagnosable on {self._entity.name} (id={self._entity.id})")
        self.body = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody")
        if self.body is None and self.verbose:
            Logger.warning("Diagnosable: no Rigidbody; physics branch disabled")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        try:
            self._tick(dt)
        except Exception as e:
            # full traceback with file:line, since _call_py logs only str(e):
            Logger.error(f"Diagnosable._tick failed: {traceback.format_exc()}")

    def _tick(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.G):
            raise RuntimeError("repro case: press-G handler")

Checklist when a script silently does nothing: entity active? component enabled? script_path resolves (Inspector shows Missing: otherwise)? class detected (first dir()-order class with a lifecycle/collision/gizmo member)? axis defined (else GetAxis is 0.0)? play() called with empty clip_path?

docs.title: Entity API
docs.text: Everything a gameplay script can do with entities and their components: creating, finding, reading, adding, removing, duplicating, parenting, tagging. For the callback side (when each method runs) see lifecycle.md; for field widgets see inspector-fields.md.

docs.title: Lookup: scene → entity
docs.text:
Signature Behavior Scene.create_entity(name="Entity", prefab_guid=None) -> Entity Creates a bare entity: no components, not even Transform. Marks scene dirty. Scene.add_entity(e) Registers an externally built Entity (wires indices, update sets, spatial state). Scene.remove_entity(eid) Removes the entity and all its children recursively. Calls on_destroy on components. Scene.get_entity(eid) -> Entity \| None By id string. Scene.get_entity_by_name(name) -> Entity \| None First entity with this name (names are not unique). Scene.get_all_entities() -> list[Entity] Cached flat list. Scene.get_root_entities() -> list[Entity] Entities with parent is None (cached, invalidated on parenting). Scene.get_entities_with_component(cls) -> list[Entity] Indexed query, subclass-aware. Scene.duplicate_entity(entity, new_name="") -> Entity Deep copy of the entity and its whole subtree with fresh UUIDs; Armature bone ids rebound. scene.mark_dirty() / scene.mark_clean() / scene.dirty Manual dirty flag (serialization and editor save indicators).

Inside a script the scene is always at hand: self._entity._scene (assigned by the engine before on_awake).

docs.title: Lookup: entity → component
docs.text: Signature Behavior entity.add_component(comp, key=None) -> Component Attaches; calls comp.on_awake(). Key defaults to TypeName, or TypeName.<8 hex> when the class allows multiples. entity.get_component(cls) -> Component \| None Exact type first, then issubclass fallback. Returns the first match. entity.get_components(cls) -> list All matches (exact or subclass). entity.get_component_by_name(name) -> Component \| None Resolution order: registered type name → exact component key → "Name." prefix (multi-instance) → ComponentRegistry subclass fallback. entity.has_component(cls) -> bool Exact or subclass presence. entity.get_all_components() -> list Every attached component. entity.get_component_in_children(cls) Depth-first search through children. entity.remove_component(cls) Removes first match, calls on_destroy. entity.remove_all_components(cls) Removes every match. entity.remove_component_by_key(key) Removes the exact keyed instance (use for multi-instance components).

docs.title: Hierarchy, tags, flags
docs.text:
Member Behavior entity.set_parent(parent, preserve_world=True) Re-parents; with True (default) the world matrix is preserved via a world_matrix round-trip. Pass None to unparent. Depth caches are invalidated for the whole subtree. entity.parent / entity.children Read-only hierarchy links. entity.transform First component named Transform (cached), or None on bare entities. entity.active: bool Toggling deactivates the entity: update sets shrink, spatial entry drops, and on_disable/on_enable fire on every enabled component. comp.enabled: bool Per-component switch with the same update-set wiring. entity.tags: set[str] Free-form tag set (entity.tags.add("enemy")). Serialized as a list. entity.layer: int Integer layer, default 0. entity.prefab_guid / entity.prefab_source_id Prefab linkage; None on plain entities. entity.is_prefab_instance: bool True when prefab_guid is set. entity.embed_resources / entity.locked / entity.system Serialization/editor flags.

duplicate_entity details: every node in the copied subtree gets a new uuid4; children of copied nodes are re-linked inside the copy; a copied node whose original parent was outside the copied subtree is attached to that original parent; new_name renames the copy root. Armature bone_entity_ids are remapped through the old→new id map.

docs.title: Spawner example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
Uses only verified calls: bare create_entity, manual Transform, set_parent, tags, get_root_entities.

from core.components.transform.tr import Transform
from core.maths.math3d import Vec3


class Spawner:
    spawn_name: str = "Pickup"
    count: int = 5
    spacing: float = 2.0

    def on_start(self):
        self.scene = self._entity._scene
        self.spawned = []
        for i in range(int(self.count)):
            e = self.scene.create_entity(f"{self.spawn_name}_{i}")
            t = Transform()
            t.local_position = Vec3(float(i) * float(self.spacing), 0.0, 0.0)
            e.add_component(t)
            e.tags.add("pickup")
            e.set_parent(self._entity, preserve_world=False)
            self.spawned.append(e.id)

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE):
            e = self.scene.create_entity(self.spawn_name)
            e.add_component(Transform())
            e.tags.add("pickup")

    def alive_roots(self):
        return [e.name for e in self.scene.get_root_entities()]

Inspector fields for this script: spawn_name (string), count (int), spacing (float) — plain annotated attributes.

Duplicating at runtime (fresh UUIDs guaranteed by the engine):

class Cloner:
    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.C):
            scene = self._entity._scene
            copy = scene.duplicate_entity(self._entity, new_name="Clone")
            copy.set_parent(None, preserve_world=True)

Finding components defensively (multi-instance safe):

class Reader:
    def on_start(self):
        e = self._entity
        tr = e.get_component_by_name("Transform")
        all_scripts = e.get_components(
            __import__("core.ecs", fromlist=["ComponentRegistry"]).ComponentRegistry.get("ScriptComponent")
        ) if e.has_component(
            __import__("core.ecs", fromlist=["ComponentRegistry"]).ComponentRegistry.get("ScriptComponent")
        ) else []
        Logger.info(f"transform={tr is not None} scripts={len(all_scripts)}")

Simpler idiom for the common case — cache in on_start, never per frame:

class CacheDemo:
    def on_start(self):
        self.body = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody")
        self.audio = self._entity.get_component_by_name("AudioSource")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if self.body is not None and Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W):
            self.body.add_force(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 10.0))

docs.title: Script Examples
docs.text:
Copy-paste behaviors. All run as-is: create a Python Script asset, replace its content, attach to an entity, press Play.

Rotator — spins around Y using the frame delta:

from core.maths.math3d import Vec3


class Rotator:
    speed: float = 90.0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        t = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Transform")
        if t:
            t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, self.speed * dt, 0.0))

Mover — constant forward motion with an Inspector slider:

from typing import Annotated
from core.maths.math3d import Vec3


class Mover:
    speed: Annotated[float, Range(0.0, 20.0)] = 5.0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        t = self._entity.transform
        if t:
            t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, self.speed * dt))

Keyboard driver — WASD movement plus sprint on Shift:

from core.maths.math3d import Vec3


class Driver:
    speed: float = 6.0
    sprint: float = 10.0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        v = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W):
            v = v + Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.S):
            v = v + Vec3(0.0, 0.0, -1.0)
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.A):
            v = v + Vec3(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.D):
            v = v + Vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        rate = self.sprint if (Input.GetKey(KeyCode.LEFT_SHIFT) or Input.GetKey(KeyCode.RIGHT_SHIFT)) else self.speed
        t = self._entity.transform
        if t and v.length() > 0.0:
            t.translate(v.normalized() * rate * dt)

Patrol — waypoint ping-pong with an enum mode and a cached Transform:

from enum import Enum
from core.maths.math3d import Vec3


class PatrolMode(Enum):
    PINGPONG = 0
    LOOP = 1


class Patrol:
    mode: PatrolMode = PatrolMode.PINGPONG
    speed: float = 3.0
    distance: float = 8.0

    def on_awake(self):
        self.t = self._entity.transform
        self.home = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        self.dir = 1.0
        if self.t:
            self.home = self.t.position

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if not self.t:
            return
        step = self.speed * self.dir * dt
        self.t.translate(Vec3(step, 0.0, 0.0))
        walked = self.t.position.x - self.home.x
        if self.mode == PatrolMode.LOOP:
            if walked > self.distance or walked < 0.0:
                self.t.position = Vec3(self.home.x, self.t.position.y, self.t.position.z)
        else:
            if walked > self.distance or walked < 0.0:
                self.dir = -self.dir

Follower — chase an Entity picked in the Inspector:

from core.maths.math3d import Vec3


class Follower:
    target: 'Entity' = None
    speed: float = 4.0
    stop_at: float = 1.5

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if not self.target:
            return
        t = self._entity.transform
        goal = self.target.transform
        if not t or not goal:
            return
        delta = goal.position - t.position
        dist = delta.length()
        if dist > self.stop_at:
            t.translate(delta.normalized() * self.speed * dt)

Hit counter — collision callbacks with impact force and an Inspector button:

class HitCounter:
    hits: int = 0
    last_force: float = 0.0
    _inspector_buttons = [("reset", "Reset")]

    def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force):
        self.hits = self.hits + 1
        self.last_force = force

    def reset(self):
        self.hits = 0
        self.last_force = 0.0

Physics kick — impulse on key press for an entity with Rigidbody:

from core.maths.math3d import Vec3


class Kicker:
    impulse: float = 5.0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE):
            rb = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody")
            if rb:
                rb.add_impulse(Vec3(0.0, self.impulse, 0.0))

Countdown spawner — timed logic with enable/disable safety:

class Spawner:
    interval: float = 2.0
    active: bool = True

    def on_awake(self):
        self.clock = 0.0
        self.count = 0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if not self.active:
            return
        self.clock = self.clock + dt
        if self.clock >= self.interval:
            self.clock = 0.0
            self.count = self.count + 1
            Logger.info("spawn tick")

    def on_disable(self):
        self.clock = 0.0

docs.text: Driving UI from gameplay code: buttons, labels, canvas, and the GuiApi builders. Component names for lookup: "ButtonComponent", "LabelComponent", etc.

docs.title: Widget components
docs.text:
Every widget component shares the base fields (all serialized, all Inspector-editable):

Field Default Notes widget_text "Button" / "Label" / … Synced to the live Qt widget via setText/text(). widget_width / widget_height per-type (e.g. 120×36 button, 100×30 label) Logical size, zoom-scaled to screen. _anchor 0 Anchor preset id. _visible True Visibility flag. _bg_color / _text_color / _border_color None RGB lists, stylesheet-driven. _font_size / _font_bold / _opacity 14.0 / False / 1.0 Appearance.

Live-widget access:

Member Behavior comp._widget_ref The live QWidget (e.g. Button(QPushButton)), or None before creation/destroyed after. comp.sync_to_widget() Pushes component state (geometry, text, style) to the live widget. comp.update_from_widget() Pulls geometry/text back (editor drag path). Button.clicked Native Qt QPushButton.clicked signal — connect your slot. Also textChanged/valueChanged/toggled on other widgets auto-sync edits back.

Widget position comes from the entity's Transform.local_position (x/y); size from widget_width/widget_height.

docs.title: Counter-HUD example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
A label showing the score plus a button that increments it — Qt signals wired from a behavior script:

class CounterHud:
    start_score: int = 0

    def on_start(self):
        scene = self._entity._scene
        self.score = int(self.start_score)
        self.label = scene.get_entity_by_name("ScoreLabel")
        btn_entity = scene.get_entity_by_name("ScoreButton")
        self._refresh()
        if btn_entity is not None:
            btn = btn_entity.get_component_by_name("ButtonComponent")
            w = btn._widget_ref if btn is not None else None
            if w is not None:
                try:
                    w.clicked.disconnect()
                except Exception:
                    pass
                w.clicked.connect(self._on_click)

    def _on_click(self):
        self.score += 1
        self._refresh()

    def _refresh(self):
        if self.label is None:
            return
        comp = self.label.get_component_by_name("LabelComponent")
        if comp is None:
            return
        comp.widget_text = f"Score: {self.score}"
        comp.sync_to_widget()

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.R):
            self.score = 0
            self._refresh()

Inspector fields: start_score (int). Setup: two entities named ScoreLabel (LabelComponent) and ScoreButton (ButtonComponent) anywhere in the scene.

Building UI purely from code with GuiApi:

class MenuBuilder:
    def on_start(self):
        from core.gui.api import GuiApi
        api = GuiApi.get("default")
        if api is None:
            Logger.warning("MenuBuilder: no default GuiApi")
            return
        title = api.label(x=300, y=40, w=200, h=40, text="PAUSED")
        btn = api.button(x=300, y=120, w=200, h=48, text="Resume")
        btn.clicked.connect(self._on_resume)
        self._built = [title, btn]

    def _on_resume(self):
        Logger.info("Resume pressed")

    def on_destroy(self):
        from core.gui.api import GuiApi
        api = GuiApi.get("default")
        if api is not None:
            api.clear()

Saving a layout to disk and restoring it:

api.save("assets/ui/hud.json")   # GuiCanvas.save_to_file under the hood
api.load("assets/ui/hud.json")   # GuiCanvas.load_from_file under the hood
