docs.title: Hot Reload
docs.text:
A script file can be edited while Play is running. The change is picked up on the next frame: the instance is recreated, Inspector values are preserved, and on_awake / on_start run again. Instance state from __init__ is reset, like a recompilation in Unity.

Reload pipeline:

  1. The engine compares the file modification time before each on_update / on_fixed_update. A newer mtime starts a reload.
  2. The file is re-validated (same checks as the Check button). On errors a single consolidated console message Script '...' has N error(s): is written per file version, and the previous working instance keeps running.
  3. On success the module re-executes with the injected API, the behavior class is re-resolved, and a fresh instance is constructed.
  4. Inspector field values are re-applied onto the new instance, then on_awake and on_start run again.

What survives: Inspector-tuned values, the component wiring, the entity hierarchy. What resets: anything assigned in __init__ or built up in callbacks (timers, caches, spawned handles) — rebuild it in on_awake/on_start if the behavior must continue seamlessly.

The Check button validates without Play in three stages: syntax parse with file:line positions, core.* import resolution (including the hint to use core.maths.math3d instead of core.math3d), and a full trial execution catching runtime import errors such as circular imports.

Control: the hot_reload flag on ScriptComponent (default True). Set False to freeze the instance for the session — useful when debugging native-side state or comparing against a fixed baseline.

Workflow tips: keep Play running and iterate on feel (speeds, curves, timings) with an external editor; the tuned Inspector values persist across reloads, so save the scene when the feel is right. For structural refactors (renamed fields, new buttons) expect one clean reload cycle and re-check the Inspector.

Troubleshooting: changes ignored → the file did not save (mtime unchanged) or hot_reload is off; old behavior persists with errors → fix the reported file:line entries, the last working build stays live meanwhile; fields reset → the annotation was renamed, the old stored value has no target.

docs.title: Input and Math API
docs.text:
These names are injected into every user script module automatically, so importing them is optional. An explicit import with the same name in the script takes priority over the injection.

Injected names: Input, KeyCode, Vec2, Vec3, Vec4, Curve, Range, Logger.

Keyboard and mouse:

  • Input.GetKey(code) — held this frame; Input.GetKeyDown(code) — pressed this frame; Input.GetKeyUp(code) — released this frame. Codes come from KeyCode (KeyCode.W, KeyCode.SPACE, KeyCode.LEFT_SHIFT / KeyCode.RIGHT_SHIFT, arrows, digits and more).
  • Input.GetMouseButton(i), GetMouseButtonDown(i), GetMouseButtonUp(i) — button index state.
  • Input.GetButton(name), GetButtonDown(name), GetButtonUp(name) — named action buttons.
  • Input.GetAxis(name), Input.GetAxisRaw(name) — smoothed vs raw axes such as "Horizontal".
  • Input.mousePosition — cursor in screen space; Input.deltaTime — scaled frame time; Input.cursorLocked / Input.cursorVisible — pointer capture state.

Math:

  • Vec2, Vec3, Vec4 — full vector math (add, scale, dot, cross, length, normalized, lerp) backed by numpy.float64; the GPU downgrade to float32 happens only on upload.
  • Quat, Mat4 — import from core.maths.math3d for rotations and matrices (slerp, look_at, perspective helpers live there with numba acceleration).
  • Curve — keyframed response curves edited in the Inspector and evaluated at runtime for falloff, easing and throttle shapes.
  • Range — slider metadata for Inspector fields (see Inspector Fields).
  • Logger — Logger.info/warning/error with timestamps; errors include tracebacks and reach the console panel.

Frame-rate independence: always multiply motion by dt (or use Input.deltaTime); fixed-step logic belongs in on_fixed_update with its stable step.

class Player:
    speed: float = 6.0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        step = self.speed * dt
        t = self._entity.transform
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W):
            t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, step))
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.S):
            t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, -step))
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE):
            Logger.info("jump pressed")

class Looker:
    sensitivity: float = 2.0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        x = Input.GetAxis("Horizontal")
        t = self._entity.transform
        if t and x != 0.0:
            t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, x * self.sensitivity * dt, 0.0))

Cursor pattern for fly cameras: lock on right-mouse hold, release on up — drive Input.cursorLocked from the mouse-button callbacks in on_update.

Axes such as "Horizontal" exist only after bindings are loaded (Input.LoadProjectBindings at startup) or an explicit Input.DefineAxis("Horizontal", positive=[KeyCode.D], negative=[KeyCode.A]). An undefined axis name makes GetAxis / GetAxisRaw return 0.0, so the Looker above stays still until the axis is defined — define it in project setup before relying on it (see Input overview).

docs.title: Input Reference
docs.text: Complete, code-backed reference for keyboard, mouse, buttons, axes, and cursor. Shorter narrative version: input-math-api.md. Injected names: Input, KeyCode, Cursor (no import needed); InputAxis/InputButton for manual setup.

docs.title: Polling
docs.text: Signature Behavior Input.GetKey(key) -> bool Held right now. Returns False when input is disabled. Input.GetKeyDown(key) -> bool Pressed this frame (edge from the frame accumulator). Input.GetKeyUp(key) -> bool Released this frame. Input.GetMouseButton(button) / GetMouseButtonDown / GetMouseButtonUp button is an index: internal code is KeyCode.MOUSE_LEFT + button, so 0 = left, 1 = right, 2 = middle. Input.GetButton(name) / GetButtonDown / GetButtonUp Named InputButton (keys + alt keys); unknown name ⇒ False. Input.GetAxis(name) -> float Smoothed value in [−1, 1]; unknown or undefined name ⇒ 0.0. Negated when the axis is inverted. Input.GetAxisRaw(name) -> float Unsmoothed −1/0/1 (or mouse delta for mouse axes); unknown ⇒ 0.0. Input.mousePosition / mouseDelta / mouseScrollDelta (x, y) tuples; deltas reset at frame end. Input.anyKey / anyKeyDown Held-anything / pressed-this-frame. Input.deltaTime Clamped frame dt (0…0.1 s). Input.inputEnabled + Input.set_input_enabled(v) Master gate: polling returns False/0.0 while off.

docs.title: Axes and buttons (setup is mandatory)
docs.text:
An axis that was never defined reads as 0.0 — always. Define before use:

Signature Behavior Input.DefineAxis(name, positive, negative, alt_positive=None, alt_negative=None, gravity=3.0, dead=0.001, sensitivity=1.0, snap=False, invert=False) Registers a smoothed axis. Value ramps toward ±1 at sensitivity/s and falls back at gravity/s. Input.DefineMouseAxis(name) Registers a mouse-delta axis (e.g. "Mouse X"); GetAxis returns delta × sensitivity with optional inversion. Input.DefineButton(name, keys, alt_keys=None) Registers a named button over key-code lists. Input.LoadProjectBindings(project_path=None) Loads axes/buttons/mouse axes, sensitivity, inversion, and control scheme from the project config; clears existing maps first. Input.set_mouse_sensitivity(v) / set_invert_mouse_x/y(v) / set_control_scheme("fps"\|"tps") Runtime tuning. Input.OnEvent(name, cb) / Input.OffEvent(name, cb) Frame/key/mouse/scroll events: any_key_down/up, key_down/up, mouse_down/up, mouse_move, scroll, frame_begin/end. Input.Reset() Clears held/down/up/mouse/scroll state.

docs.title: Cursor (confirmed API only)
docs.text:
Member Behavior Input.cursorLocked / Input.set_cursor_locked(v) Pointer-capture flag (plain boolean, engine-bridged). Input.cursorVisible / Input.set_cursor_visible(v) Cursor visibility flag. Cursor.visible (get/set) Alias of Input.cursorVisible. Cursor.lockState (get/set) "locked" ⇔ (cursorLocked=True, cursorVisible=False); anything else unlocks + shows. CursorLockMode.LOCKED/NONE/CONFINED constants.

No gamepad/joystick polling exists in core/input/inpsys (keyboard + mouse + abstract axes/buttons only). Anything beyond the table above is not confirmed — do not document gamepad calls.

docs.title: InputManager wrapper example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
One place that guarantees every axis the game uses exists, then thin readers:

class InputSetup:
    def on_awake(self):
        Input.DefineAxis("Horizontal", [KeyCode.D], [KeyCode.A])
        Input.DefineAxis("Vertical", [KeyCode.W], [KeyCode.S])
        Input.DefineAxis("Strafe", [KeyCode.E], [KeyCode.Q], sensitivity=2.0)
        Input.DefineButton("Jump", [KeyCode.SPACE])
        Input.DefineButton("Fire", [KeyCode.MOUSE_LEFT])
        Input.DefineMouseAxis("Mouse X")
        Input.DefineMouseAxis("Mouse Y")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        # fly-camera cursor pattern (verified flags only):
        if Input.GetMouseButtonDown(1):
            Input.set_cursor_locked(True)
            Input.set_cursor_visible(False)
        if Input.GetMouseButtonUp(1):
            Input.set_cursor_locked(False)
            Input.set_cursor_visible(True)

Reader side (any other script, no setup needed):

class ShooterInput:
    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetButtonDown("Jump"):
            Logger.info("jump!")
        if Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0):   # == MOUSE_LEFT
            Logger.info(f"fire at {Input.mousePosition}")
        yaw = Input.GetAxis("Mouse X")
        if yaw != 0.0:
            self._entity.transform.rotate(Vec3(0.0, yaw * 120.0 * dt, 0.0))

docs.title: Inspector Fields and Range
docs.text:
Annotated class attributes automatically appear in the Inspector, and their values are stored in the scene (.zpes). Class-level defaults become the initial values; per-instance edits override them without touching the .py file. Private names starting with _ are skipped, except the special _inspector_buttons.

from enum import Enum
from typing import Annotated
from core.maths.math3d import Vec3
from core.foundation.curve import Curve


class Mode(Enum):
    IDLE = 0
    PATROL = 1


class Enemy:
    speed: Annotated[float, Range(0.0, 10.0)] = 5.0
    health: int = 100
    title: str = "grunt"
    active: bool = True
    offset: Vec3 = Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)
    mode: Mode = Mode.PATROL
    falloff: Curve = Curve()
    target: 'Entity' = None
    _inspector_buttons = [("explode", "Explode")]

    def explode(self):
        self.health = 0
Annotation Inspector widget Stored as float Number field float int Integer field int bool Checkbox bool str Text field string Annotated[float, Range(min, max[, step])] Float slider, default step 0.01 float clamped to range Annotated[int, Range(min, max)] Integer slider, default step 1 int clamped to range Vec2 / Vec3 / Vec4 Vector fields float components Enum subclass Dropdown of member names enum value 'Entity' Entity picker UUID; the live object is passed to the script Curve Curve editor keyframe set

Details:

  • Range is Range(min_value=0.0, max_value=1.0, step=None). A plain [min, max] or (min, max[, step]) sequence in Annotated metadata works identically.
  • Entity picker stores the target UUID in the scene and resolves the live object before each call — safe across renames, unlike name-based lookup.
  • Resource-typed fields (mesh, material, texture, audio, prefab, scene, physics material) reuse the built-in picker dialogs and their file filters: models *.obj *.fbx *.stl *.gltf *.glb *.usdz *.dae *.3ds *.blend, materials *.zpem *.mat, images *.png *.jpg *.jpeg *.bmp *.tga *.tif *.tiff *.webp *.hdr *.exr *.dds *.svg, audio *.wav *.mp3 *.ogg *.flac *.aiff *.m4a, scripts *.py, prefabs *.zpep, scenes *.zpes, animation clips and controllers, physics materials *.zphysmat.
  • _inspector_buttons = [(method_name, label), ...] renders buttons that invoke the method on the live Play instance (or the editor instance outside Play) — handy for test triggers like explode, reset or spawn.
  • The component header shows an immutable Script field with the file display name: click reveals the file in the Project panel, the ... button opens the built-in script editor. Changing the file rebuilds the field list; values for surviving names are kept.
  • Hot-reload re-applies Inspector values onto the recreated instance, so tuning survives code edits.

Guidance: expose designers' knobs (speeds, counts, toggles) as fields, keep internal caches (self._cache, cooldowns) as plain un-annotated attributes set in on_awake.

docs.title: Lifecycle Callbacks
docs.text:
Every callback is optional. Define only what the behavior needs; the engine caches per-method lookups and skips missing ones without cost.

Method Short alias Signature When it runs on_awake awake () Once when Play starts, before on_start; use for caches and peer lookups on_start start () Once when Play starts; use for initial state and first actions on_update update (dt) Every rendered frame in scene order; dt already scaled by time scale on_fixed_update fixed_update (dt) Every physics step with stable dt (0.02 default); forces and movement here on_enable enable () When the entity becomes active (entity.active = True) on_disable disable () When the entity becomes inactive; stop loops and sounds here on_collision_enter — (other_id) or (other_id, force) Contact starts on_collision_stay — (other_id) or (other_id, force) Contact continues on_collision_exit — (other_id) or (other_id, force) Contact ends on_destroy destroy () Component removed or scene unloaded; release resources here gizmo_lines — () -> list Editor gizmo lines, runs outside Play too gizmo_meshes — () -> list Editor gizmo meshes, runs outside Play too

Call order at Play start: on_awake for every scripted component, then on_start for every scripted component. Do not assume sibling start order — fetch peers lazily or in on_update guards.

dt semantics: render dt stretches with slow motion and pause (time scale 0 freezes updates); fixed dt stays constant so physics and its scripts stay deterministic.

Collision dispatch: the solver reports contacts to the physics layer, which maps solver bodies to entity ids and invokes callbacks. Arity is measured once from the signature — two parameters receive (other_id: str, force: float), one parameter receives just other_id. Resolve the other entity inside the callback only if needed; id comparison is cheaper.

Enable/disable: toggling entity.active fires on_disable/on_enable on all components of that entity, scripts included. Disabling mid-Play pauses that behavior without destroying its instance state.

Destroy cases: removing the ScriptComponent in the editor, deleting the entity, unloading the scene, or stopping Play. Hot-reload recreates the instance but preserves Inspector field values and re-runs on_awake/on_start.

Exceptions: any error in any callback is caught and logged as Script ... error ... with only str(e) (no traceback — use the Check button for static diagnostics), naming the script and method. The frame, the physics step and the remaining components continue.

class Fighter:
    health: int = 100

    def on_awake(self):
        self.hits = 0
        self.body = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody")

    def on_start(self):
        self.alive = True

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if self.health <= 0 and self.alive:
            self.alive = False
            self._entity.active = False

    def on_fixed_update(self, dt):
        if self.body and self.health <= 0:
            self.body.velocity = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

    def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force):
        self.hits = self.hits + 1
        self.health = self.health - int(force)

    def on_destroy(self):
        self.hits = 0
        self.body = None

docs.title: Network Scripting
docs.text: Multiplayer from gameplay code: RPCs, message subscriptions, prefab spawn/despawn, authority, and send rates.

docs.title: Concepts (as the code defines them)
docs.text:
• NetworkManager component: transport control + spawn/despawn + RPC send. Singleton via NetworkManager.get().
  • NetworkIdentity: per-entity net_id/owner_id/prefab_id + AuthorityMode: SERVER, OWNER, SHARED.
  • Sync components: NetworkTransform (authority SERVER/OWNER, send_rate default 20.0), NetworkVariables (authority + send_rate default 10.0), plus NetworkRigidbody/NetworkAnimator (same send_rate pattern). NetworkManager itself has tick_rate (default 20.0), not send_rate.
  • RPC handler lookup on the receiving entity: method decorated with @server_rpc/@client_rpc/@target_rpc called as fn(args_dict) → else handle_rpc(method, args, sender) → else rpc_<method>(**args).
  • Plugin bus: NetworkPlugin.on_message(msg_type, handler) receives NetworkMessage(msg_type, payload, sender_id); "*" subscribes to everything.

docs.title: NetworkManager API
docs.text:
Signature Behavior NetworkManager.get() -> NetworkManager \| None Cached _instance, else scans the active scene for the component. mgr.host(port=None, max_players=None) -> bool Hosts on 0.0.0.0; resets net-id tables, registers existing identities. mgr.connect(address=None, port=None, name="Player") -> bool Connects as client; clears net tables. mgr.disconnect() Drops transport, clears tables. mgr.is_server / is_client / is_connected / local_id / peer_count Transport-backed read-only properties. mgr.send_rpc(net_id, method, args=None, target=None) Broadcast when server (or no target); send_to(target) when server + target set; plain send from a client. Payload: {net_id, method, args, t}. mgr.spawn_entity(entity, owner_id=None) -> int Server: assigns net id, stamps identity, broadcasts NET_SPAWN. Client: sends NET_SPAWN_REQUEST, returns -1. mgr.spawn_prefab(prefab_path, pos=None, rot=None, owner_id=None) Server: Prefab.load for .zpep paths, sets Transform from pos (Vec3/list) and rot (Quat/list), stamps prefab_id, broadcasts. Client: forwards a spawn request to the server. Returns the entity (server) or None (client). mgr.despawn(net_id) / mgr.despawn_entity(entity) Server broadcasts NET_DESPAWN then removes; client forwards and returns. Non-owner clients cannot despawn others' entities.

Identity helpers: ident.is_spawned (net_id >= 0), ident.is_owner, ident.has_authority (SHARED ⇒ always; OWNER ⇒ is_owner; SERVER ⇒ transport is_server), transfer_ownership(new_owner) (server only), request_ownership() (client→server).

NetworkVariables: set_var(name, value) (marks dirty, sends on change), get_var(name, default), set_vars(dict), has_var, remove_var, all_vars(); sync_on_change + send_rate gate the on_update flush.

docs.title: Score-sync example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
Server-authoritative score: clients request a bump via RPC, the server updates a NetworkVariables entry that replicates to everyone:

from core.network.rpc import server_rpc


class ScoreSync:
    score_key: str = "score"

    def on_start(self):
        from core.components.network.netmgr.manager import NetworkManager
        self.mgr = NetworkManager.get()
        ident = self._entity.get_component_by_name("NetworkIdentity")
        self.net_id = ident.net_id if ident is not None else -1
        self.vars = self._entity.get_component_by_name("NetworkVariables")
        # subscribe to a lightweight bus message as well:
        try:
            from core.engine.eng import Engine
            plug = Engine.instance().plugin_manager.get_plugin("NetworkPlugin")
            if plug is not None:
                plug.on_message("score_flash", self._on_flash)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.P):
            if self.mgr is not None and self.net_id >= 0:
                self.mgr.send_rpc(self.net_id, "add_point", {"by": 1})

    @server_rpc
    def add_point(self, args):
        if self.vars is None:
            return
        cur = int(self.vars.get_var(self.score_key, 0))
        self.vars.set_var(self.score_key, cur + int(args.get("by", 1)))

    def _on_flash(self, msg):
        Logger.info(f"flash from {msg.sender_id}: {msg.payload}")

    def current_score(self):
        return int(self.vars.get_var(self.score_key, 0)) if self.vars is not None else 0

Setup: entity carries NetworkIdentity (authority SERVER) + NetworkVariables + this script. send_rpc routes by role automatically; @server_rpc executes on the server copy via invoke_rpc.

Spawning a networked prefab from gameplay:

class NetSpawner:
    prefab_path: str = "assets/prefabs/player.zpep"

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.N) and self.mgr.is_server:
            ent = self.mgr.spawn_prefab(self.prefab_path, pos=Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0))
            Logger.info(f"spawned: {ent.name if ent else None}")

docs.title: Scripting Overview
docs.text:
Entity behaviors in ZarinEngine are plain .py files with a behavior class. No base class, no registration boilerplate, no build step — the file itself is the asset.

End-to-end flow:

  1. Project → Create → Python Script creates the file inside the project folder. Keep scripts next to the content that uses them; sibling imports (including Cython modules) resolve from the script folder automatically.
  2. Select an entity, Inspector → Add Component → Scripts, pick the file in the Script field. Annotated class attributes instantly become Inspector widgets.
  3. Tune values in the Inspector — they are stored in the scene (.zpes), not in the .py file, so one script drives many tuned instances.
  4. Press Play. The engine loads the class, instantiates it with no arguments, assigns self._entity, and calls on_awake then on_start.

How it works inside:

  • The engine finds the first class in alphabetical attribute order (dir() order, not definition order) that declares at least one lifecycle callback, collision callback, gizmo method, or _inspector_buttons. Inheritance is not required; the constructor must take no arguments.
  • Short names are full aliases: update = on_update, start = on_start, and so on for awake, fixed_update, destroy, enable, disable. If both variants are defined, the on_* version wins.
  • One entity can hold several ScriptComponent instances (_allow_multiple = True): movement, health and visuals as separate scripts on one object.
  • An exception inside any callback never crashes the game: it is written to the console with the script and method name, and the frame continues with the next component.
  • script_path is stored relative to the project root, so scenes and scripts move between machines cleanly.

Execution context:

  • on_update(dt) runs in scene order every rendered frame with dt already multiplied by the time scale; on_fixed_update(dt) runs on the physics clock with a stable step (0.02 default).
  • Collision callbacks arrive from the physics dispatch, not the ECS loop, with the other entity id and optionally the impact force.
  • Gizmo methods (gizmo_lines, gizmo_meshes) execute in the editor even outside Play for custom handles and debug drawing.

Performance guidance: scripts are Python and run per frame — keep on_update lean, cache component lookups in on_start instead of fetching by name every frame, and move number-crunching into Cython modules (see Cython in Scripts).

Subpages:

  • Lifecycle Callbacks — every method, signature and call order.
  • Inspector Fields and Range — annotations to widgets, Entity pickers, buttons.
  • Input and Math API — injected names, keys, axes, vectors, curves.
  • Hot Reload — editing scripts during Play.
  • Cython in Scripts — compiled helpers with zero manual builds.
  • ScriptComponent — paths, flags, class resolution, Check.
  • Script Examples — copy-paste behaviors.

docs.title: Physics Scripting
docs.text: Applying forces and reading velocity from gameplay code, plus the exact collision-callback contract.

docs.title: Rigidbody (3D)
docs.text: Member Behavior rb.velocity: Vec3 Read/write; writing sets _velocity_dirty so the solver picks it up. rb.angular_velocity: Vec3 Same dirty-flag mechanism. rb.add_force(force: Vec3, world_space=True) Accumulates into _force_accum, consumed by the solver step. rb.add_torque(torque: Vec3) Accumulates into _torque_accum. rb.add_impulse(impulse: Vec3) Instant velocity += impulse / mass; ignored when mass <= 0 or is_kinematic. rb.mass / rb.drag / rb.angular_drag 1.0 / 0.0 / 0.05 defaults. rb.use_gravity / rb.is_kinematic Gravity toggle; kinematic bodies ignore impulses. rb.freeze_pos_x/y/z, rb.freeze_rot_x/y/z Per-axis locks (serialized as freeze_pos/freeze_rot arrays).

docs.title: Rigidbody2D
docs.text: Member Behavior rb.velocity: Vec2 / rb.angular_velocity: float Same dirty-flag write path. rb.add_force(force: Vec2) 2D force accumulator. rb.add_torque(torque: float) Scalar torque accumulator. rb.add_impulse(impulse: Vec2) Instant velocity kick, same mass/kinematic guard. rb.gravity_scale (default 1.0) 2D-only gravity multiplier. rb.freeze_rotation: bool 2D rotation lock.

docs.title: Collision callbacks (exact contract)
docs.text:
Define either arity; the engine measures the parameter count once at load (2 if nargs >= 2 else 1) and dispatches accordingly:

def on_collision_enter(self, other_id): ...          # arity 1
def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force): ...   # arity 2
def on_collision_stay(self, other_id): ...           # or (self, other_id, force)
def on_collision_exit(self, other_id): ...           # or (self, other_id, force)

other_id is the entity id string of the other body; force is the solver contact force float (ev.get("force", 0.0)). Callbacks come from the physics event layer, not the ECS update loop, and each contact fires on both entities' scripts. Resolve the entity only when needed — id comparison is cheaper:

def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force):
    if force > 50.0:
        Logger.warning(f"Hard hit by {other_id}: {force}")

docs.title: Jump + recoil example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
Forces in on_fixed_update (stable step), input polling in on_update:

class Jumper:
    jump_impulse: float = 8.0
    move_force: float = 30.0

    def on_start(self):
        self.body = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody")
        self.want_jump = False

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE):
            self.want_jump = True

    def on_fixed_update(self, dt):
        if self.body is None:
            return
        fx = Input.GetAxis("Horizontal") * float(self.move_force)
        if fx != 0.0:
            self.body.add_force(Vec3(fx, 0.0, 0.0))
        if self.want_jump:
            self.want_jump = False
            v = self.body.velocity
            self.body.velocity = Vec3(v.x, 0.0, v.z)  # reset fall speed
            self.body.add_impulse(Vec3(0.0, float(self.jump_impulse), 0.0))

    def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force):
        if force > 40.0:
            # recoil: kick away from the impact, scaled by mass for free
            v = self.body.velocity if self.body is not None else Vec3.zero()
            if self.body is not None:
                self.body.velocity = Vec3(-v.x * 0.5, v.y, -v.z * 0.5)

Inspector fields: jump_impulse, move_force (floats). Requires a Rigidbody on the same entity and a defined "Horizontal" axis (see input-reference.md; undefined ⇒ 0.0, so the body just won't strafe).

2D variant (gravity-aware hop):

class Hopper2D:
    jump_impulse: float = 6.0

    def on_start(self):
        self.body = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody2D")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE) and self.body is not None:
            self.body.velocity = Vec2(self.body.velocity.x, 0.0)
            self.body.add_impulse(Vec2(0.0, float(self.jump_impulse)))

docs.title: Scripting Pitfalls
docs.text: Symptom → cause → fix. Every item is grounded in the implementation cited at the end.

docs.title: 1. Vec3(...).rotate(...) → AttributeError
docs.text:
Symptom: rotating a vector crashes. Cause: Vec3 has cross/dot/length/normalized/lerp/... but no rotate. Fix: rotate the transform, or rotate the vector with a quaternion:

# wrong: v.rotate(...)
# right (object turns, degrees):
self._entity.transform.rotate(Vec3(0.0, 90.0 * dt, 0.0))
# right (vector turns, radians via axis-angle):
from core.maths.math3d import Quat
q = Quat.from_axis_angle(Vec3.up(), 1.5708)
v2 = q.rotate_vec3(v)

docs.title: 2. Wrong class runs (or nothing runs)
docs.text: Symptom: the engine instantiates an unexpected class from your file. Cause: discovery scans dir(module) — alphabetical, not definition order — and picks the first class with any lifecycle/collision/gizmo member or _inspector_buttons. Fix: one behavior class per file, or name the behavior so it sorts first; helper classes must not define on_update/start/etc.

docs.title: 3. GetAxis("Horizontal") is always 0.0
docs.text:
Symptom: axis input dead while keys work. Cause: undefined axes read as 0.0 by contract. Fix: define before use (or ship project bindings):

Input.DefineAxis("Horizontal", [KeyCode.D], [KeyCode.A])
Input.DefineAxis("Vertical", [KeyCode.W], [KeyCode.S])

docs.title: 4. Sound starts although play_on_awake is off
docs.text:
Symptom: enabling an entity starts its clip. Cause: AudioSource.on_enable plays whenever clip_path is set and idle — independent of play_on_awake. Fix: clear clip_path until you mean it, or stop() in on_enable for ambience managers:

def on_enable(self):
    src = self._entity.get_component_by_name("AudioSource")
    if src is not None and not self.want_sound:
        src.stop()

docs.title: 5. Cursor won't lock / mouse axis dead
docs.text:
Symptom: cursorLocked set but nothing changes, or GetAxis("Mouse X") is 0.0. Cause: the flags are plain engine-bridged booleans (set both lock and visibility), and mouse axes need DefineMouseAxis. Fix:

Input.set_cursor_locked(True)
Input.set_cursor_visible(False)
Input.DefineMouseAxis("Mouse X")

There is no gamepad API in core/input/inpsys — keyboard, mouse, and abstract axes/buttons only.

docs.title: 6. Cython import fails / stale compiled code
docs.text:
Symptom: import fast_math (companion fast_math.pyx) fails or ignores edits. Cause: the companion builds synchronously on first import via the in-process pyximport hook; a missing cython package only warns once and the import then fails. Edits are picked up because the reloader snapshots extension mtimes and rebuilds on change. Fix: keep the .pyx next to the .py, ensure cython is installed, touch nothing else:

# myscript.py + fast_math.pyx in the SAME folder:
import fast_math  # resolved from the script folder automatically

docs.title: 7. Spawned entity is invisible / has no position
docs.text:
Symptom: create_entity object can't be placed. Cause: new entities are bare — no Transform. Fix: always add one (setting transform on a None crashes):

from core.components.transform.tr import Transform
e = scene.create_entity("Prop")
e.add_component(Transform())   # before touching e.transform

docs.title: 8. on_fixed_update order surprises
docs.text: Symptom: two scripts race (e.g. writer vs reader). Cause: updates run through cached scene-order lists; cross-entity order is an implementation detail, not a contract. Fix: don't rely on sibling order — write in on_fixed_update, read with a one-frame lag or resolve lazily, and never assume who runs first.

docs.title: 9. Inspector edits vanish / types wrong
docs.text:
Symptom: field shows but value resets, or a Vec3 arrives as a list. Cause: two stores — _field_values (source of truth, serialized as script_fields) vs live instance attributes (re-applied every frame from _field_values, lists converted to Vec2/3/4 only when the annotation matches). Fix: use get_field_value/set_field_value from tooling, keep annotations exact (x: Vec3, not x = [0,0,0]), and on disk expect script_fields, not _field_values:

comp.set_field_value("speed", 7.5)
speed = comp.get_field_value("speed")

docs.title: 10. Angles in radians do nothing useful
docs.text:
Symptom: rotate(Vec3(0, 0.05, 0)) barely turns. Cause: Transform.rotate takes degrees (radians→degrees conversion lives inside). Fix: pass degrees, convert at the boundary:

t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, 45.0 * dt, 0.0))   # 45 deg/sec, not 45 rad/sec

docs.title: 11. GetMouseButton(1000) never fires
docs.text: Symptom: mouse checks with KeyCode.MOUSE_LEFT fail. Cause: GetMouseButton(button) adds the index to MOUSE_LEFT — pass 0, not 1000. Fix: Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0) for left. (Input.GetKey(KeyCode.MOUSE_LEFT) is the code-based alternative.)

docs.title: 12. Errors name the method but not the line
docs.text: Symptom: console shows Script on_update error 'x.py': ... with no location. Cause: _call_py logs only str(e). Fix: develop with the Check button (error [line N] diagnostics) and wrap risky per-frame code with traceback.format_exc() logging (see debugging.md).

docs.title: Prefab Scripting
docs.text: Building, saving, and spawning prefabs from code, plus the five override types for instances.

docs.title: Prefab object
docs.text:
Signature Behavior Prefab(name="Prefab", guid=None, base_guid=None, menu_path=None) New prefab container; guid auto-uuid4 unless given. base_guid set ⇒ variant. Prefab.create_via_code(name, build=None, menu_path=None, guid=None) -> Prefab Builds roots_data from a build(prefab) callable returning a list of entity dicts. prefab.capture(entities) Serializes entities into roots_data: stores source_id, drops live parent links, nests children recursively, strips prefab_guid. prefab.save(path) Writes {guid, name, roots, base_guid?, menu_path?} JSON; relativizes resource paths to the project root. Logs Prefab saved: path. Prefab.load(path) -> Prefab \| None Reads the file back (also accepts legacy entity/entities shapes). Logs on failure, returns None. prefab.instantiate(scene, registry, parent=None) -> list[Entity] Deep-copies roots, assigns fresh UUIDs to every node, deserializes, stamps _prefab_guid/_prefab_source_id, scene.add_entity, parents to parent. Returns root entities. prefab.instantiate_plain(scene, registry, parent=None) -> list[Entity] Same as instantiate, then Prefab.unpack on each root — plain copies with no prefab link. Prefab.unpack(entity_root) Clears _prefab_guid/_prefab_source_id on the root and all descendants (static, in place). Prefab.create_variant(base_prefab, name, guid=None) -> Prefab Variant sharing base data with its own guid + base_guid.

Import: from core.ecs.prefabp import Prefab (also exports PrefabOverrideType, PrefabLibrary).

docs.title: The five override types
docs.text:
PrefabOverrideType values plus the functions that compute/apply them (defined in overrides.py, attached as Prefab.* statics):

Type value Meaning modified_property Name/active/tags/layer or one Component.property differs from the prefab source. Root Transform local_position/local_rotation are excluded (placement is per-instance by design). added_component Instance has a component the prefab lacks. removed_component Prefab has a component the instance lost. added_child Extra child entity under the instance. removed_child Prefab child missing from the instance. Signature Behavior Prefab.compute_overrides(entity) -> list[dict] Diff of one instance vs its resolved prefab source (variant chains resolved). [] for non-instances. Prefab.compute_all_overrides(entities) -> list[dict] Recursive over children; thread-pooled for >4 entities. Prefab.has_overrides(entities) -> bool len(compute_all_overrides(...)) > 0. Prefab.apply_overrides(entity_root) Writes the instance diff back into the .zpep file and invalidates the library cache. Prefab.revert_instance(root_entity, registry) Restores names, flags, components, and children from prefab source data (removes added children, re-creates missing ones with fresh ids).

Each override dict carries entity_id, entity_name, source_id, type, plus property/old_value/new_value (or component_type/child_source_id variants).

docs.title: Enemy factory example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
Spawns prefab instances at runtime with per-instance placement (placement never counts as an override):

from core.ecs import ComponentRegistry
from core.ecs.prefabp import Prefab
from core.maths.math3d import Vec3


class EnemyFactory:
    prefab_path: str = "assets/prefabs/enemy.zpep"
    spawn_gap: float = 3.0

    def on_start(self):
        self.scene = self._entity._scene
        self.prefab = Prefab.load(self.prefab_path)
        if self.prefab is None:
            Logger.error(f"EnemyFactory: cannot load {self.prefab_path}")
        self.spawned = 0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if self.prefab is None:
            return
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.E):
            roots = self.prefab.instantiate(
                self.scene, ComponentRegistry, parent=self._entity
            )
            for root in roots:
                root.name = f"Enemy_{self.spawned}"
                if root.transform is not None:
                    root.transform.local_position = Vec3(
                        float(self.spawned) * float(self.spawn_gap), 0.0, 0.0
                    )
            self.spawned += 1
            Logger.info(f"Spawned Enemy_{self.spawned - 1}")

    def report_overrides(self):
        for root in self.scene.get_root_entities():
            if root.is_prefab_instance:
                ovs = Prefab.compute_overrides(root)
                if ovs:
                    Logger.info(f"{root.name}: {len(ovs)} override(s)")

Capturing a prefab from a live hierarchy (editor tooling / bootstrap):

from core.ecs.prefabp import Prefab

prefab = Prefab("Enemy")
prefab.capture([template_root_entity])   # template_root + descendants
prefab.save("assets/prefabs/enemy.zpep")

# spawn a linked instance later:
roots = Prefab.load("assets/prefabs/enemy.zpep").instantiate(scene, ComponentRegistry)

# ...or a plain, unlinked copy:
plain = Prefab.load("assets/prefabs/enemy.zpep").instantiate_plain(scene, ComponentRegistry)

docs.title: Scene API
docs.text: Creating, saving, and loading scenes from code. Entity-level operations live in entity-api.md; prefab spawning lives in prefab-scripting.md.

docs.title: Key fact first
docs.text:
Scene.create_entity() returns a bare entity with no components. If the entity must be visible or placed in the world, add a Transform yourself:

from core.components.transform.tr import Transform

e = scene.create_entity("Prop")
e.add_component(Transform())

docs.title: Engine save/load (sync)
docs.text:
These live on the engine scenes mixin and block until done:

Signature Behavior engine.load_scene(path) -> Scene \| None Reads JSON, extracts embedded resources, resolves project-relative paths, deserializes, sets scene.path and scene.name (from file basename), marks clean, notifies plugins. Returns None on failure. engine.save_scene(path=None) -> None Serializes, embeds resources, relativizes paths, rotates backups (path.bak, path.bak2), writes atomically (path.build → rename), marks clean. Defaults to scene.path. engine.save_scene_object(scene, path=None) -> bool Same as save_scene but for an explicit scene object; returns success. engine.load_scene_from_data(data) -> Scene \| None Installs an already-deserialized dict as the active scene (network sync path).

docs.title: Engine save/load (async)
docs.text:
Non-blocking variants for editor and loading screens; the callback runs on the GUI thread:

Signature Behavior engine.load_scene_async(path, data=None, on_done=None) Worker thread reads/parses/deserializes, then swaps on the GUI thread and calls on_done(scene). Shows scene:load progress with throttled updates. engine.save_scene_async(path=None, on_done=None) Snapshots via scene.serialize(), persists on a worker thread, then marks clean and calls on_done(ok).

on_done is any callable: on_done(scene) for loads, on_done(ok: bool) for saves.

docs.title: Scene serialize/restore
docs.text: Signature Behavior Scene.serialize() -> dict {"name": ..., "entities": {eid: entity_dict}} plus embed_all / compress_resources flags when set. Scenes over 64 entities serialize in a thread pool. Scene.deserialize(data, registry) -> Scene Rebuilds entities, re-links parents from stored parent ids, re-registers indices/update sets, clears dirty. scene.mark_dirty() / scene.mark_clean() Dirty flag + render version bump on dirty. scene.path / scene.name / scene.dirty File path, display name, unsaved-changes flag.

docs.title: Level-loader example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
A menu script that loads levels asynchronously without freezing, using only verified signatures:

class LevelLoader:
    level_path: str = "assets/scenes/level_02.zpes"

    def on_start(self):
        from core.engine.eng import Engine
        self.engine = Engine.instance()
        self.loading = False

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.F5) and not self.loading:
            self.loading = True
            Logger.info(f"Loading {self.level_path} ...")
            self.engine.load_scene_async(
                self.level_path,
                on_done=self._on_loaded,
            )

    def _on_loaded(self, scene):
        self.loading = False
        if scene is None:
            Logger.error(f"Failed to load {self.level_path}")
            return
        Logger.info(f"Loaded scene: {scene.name} ({len(scene.get_all_entities())} entities)")

    def on_update_save(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.F6):
            self.engine.save_scene_async(on_done=lambda ok: Logger.info(f"Saved: {ok}"))

Sync save with explicit path (editor tooling / bootstrap code, not per-frame):

from core.engine.eng import Engine

engine = Engine.instance()
engine.save_scene("assets/scenes/checkpoint.zpes")
scene = engine.load_scene("assets/scenes/checkpoint.zpes")
assert scene is not None and not scene.dirty

Round-tripping a scene snapshot in memory (verified serialize/deserialize pair):

from core.ecs import Scene, ComponentRegistry

snapshot = scene.serialize()
clone = Scene.deserialize(snapshot, ComponentRegistry)
assert len(clone.get_all_entities()) == len(scene.get_all_entities())

docs.title: ScriptComponent
docs.text:
ScriptComponent is the engine side of user scripts: it loads the .py file, builds Inspector fields from the class, forwards lifecycle calls, stores field values in the scene, and validates on demand.

Component facts:

  • script_path is stored relative to the project root, so scenes are portable. A relative path that does not resolve directly is retried against the project root; absolute paths resolve as-is.
  • hot_reload defaults to True.
  • Several ScriptComponent instances may live on one entity (_allow_multiple = True).
  • The Inspector header shows the file display name (base name without extension) with a reveal action and an editor button; a second header lists the discovered script variables.

Class resolution, in order:

  1. Modification-time short-circuit: unchanged mtime reuses the cached class with zero work.
  2. Import preparation: the script folder joins the module search so sibling .py and compiled Cython modules resolve.
  3. Error collection: syntax parse, core.* import checks, trial execution. On errors one consolidated Script '...' has N error(s): message is logged per file version, the old instance is dropped, and no fields render until the file is fixed.
  4. Module execution with the injected API (Input, KeyCode, Vec2/3/4, Curve, Range, Logger).
  5. Class pick: the first class in alphabetical attribute order (dir() order, not definition order) that declares at least one lifecycle callback, collision callback, gizmo method, or _inspector_buttons. Instantiated with no arguments; self._entity is assigned before every call.
  6. Method caching: bound methods per canonical name with fast flags for on_update / on_fixed_update; collision arities measured once via signature inspection; field hints cached until the file changes.

Serialization: script_path and the script_fields dict persist in .zpes, so tuned instances survive reloads, prefabs and version control. hot_reload (default True) is a runtime-only flag and is not serialized.

The Check action runs step 3 on demand and reports file:line: message rows — including the core.maths.math3d vs core.math3d hint and circular-import failures — so broken scripts are diagnosed without pressing Play.

Multiple instances on one entity each keep an independent module state, instance and field set; they reload independently. Cross-script communication goes through the entity (get_component by sibling script is resolved via its component, or shared state on the entity).

docs.title: Script Templates
docs.text: Six complete, runnable starters. Each lists its Inspector fields. Conventions used throughout: KeyCode.SPACE (not Space), Transform.rotate/translate, injected Input/Vec3/Logger, Inspector state via plain annotated attributes (script_fields on disk). dt is already time-scaled in on_update.

docs.title: 1. Mover (WASD + Space hop)
docs.text:
Fields: speed: float = 6.0, jump: float = 8.0. Needs Rigidbody for the hop; movement is kinematic via translate(world_space=True).

class Mover:
    speed: float = 6.0
    jump: float = 8.0

    def on_start(self):
        self.body = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        t = self._entity.transform
        step = float(self.speed) * float(dt)
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W):
            t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, -step), world_space=True)
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.S):
            t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, step), world_space=True)
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.A):
            t.translate(Vec3(-step, 0.0, 0.0), world_space=True)
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.D):
            t.translate(Vec3(step, 0.0, 0.0), world_space=True)
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE) and self.body is not None:
            self.body.add_impulse(Vec3(0.0, float(self.jump), 0.0))

docs.title: 2. Follower (damped chase + face target)
docs.text:
Fields: damping: float = 5.0, height: float = 2.0.

class Follower:
    damping: float = 5.0
    height: float = 2.0

    def on_start(self):
        self.target = self._entity._scene.get_entity_by_name("Player")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if self.target is None or self.target.transform is None:
            return
        t = self._entity.transform
        goal = self.target.transform.position + Vec3(0.0, float(self.height), 0.0)
        k = min(1.0, float(self.damping) * float(dt))
        t.position = t.position.lerp(goal, k)
        t.look_at(self.target.transform.position)

docs.title: 3. Orbiter (circle a pivot, degrees!)
docs.text:
Fields: radius: float = 8.0, angular_speed: float = 30.0 (degrees/second), height: float = 3.0.

class Orbiter:
    radius: float = 8.0
    angular_speed: float = 30.0
    height: float = 3.0

    def on_start(self):
        import math
        self.math = math
        self.angle = 0.0
        self.pivot = self._entity._scene.get_entity_by_name("Player")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        self.angle += float(self.angular_speed) * float(dt)
        a = self.math.radians(self.angle)
        cx, cz = 0.0, 0.0
        if self.pivot is not None and self.pivot.transform is not None:
            p = self.pivot.transform.position
            cx, cz = p.x, p.z
        t = self._entity.transform
        t.position = Vec3(
            cx + float(self.radius) * self.math.cos(a),
            float(self.height),
            cz + float(self.radius) * self.math.sin(a),
        )
        t.look_at(self.pivot.transform.position if self.pivot is not None else Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))

docs.title: 4. Timer / Respawner (dt accumulation — the only timer there is)
docs.text:
Fields: delay: float = 3.0. No coroutines exist; this is the sanctioned shape.

class TimerRespawner:
    delay: float = 3.0

    def on_start(self):
        self.left = 0.0
        self.home = self._entity.transform.position

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if not self._entity.active:
            self.left -= dt
            if self.left <= 0.0:
                self._entity.transform.position = self.home
                self._entity.active = True

    def kill(self):
        self._entity.active = False
        self.left = float(self.delay)

docs.title: 5. Counter HUD (label + button, Qt signal)
docs.text:
Fields: start_score: int = 0. Needs ScoreLabel (LabelComponent) and ScoreButton (ButtonComponent) entities.

class CounterHud:
    start_score: int = 0

    def on_start(self):
        scene = self._entity._scene
        self.score = int(self.start_score)
        self.label = scene.get_entity_by_name("ScoreLabel")
        btn_entity = scene.get_entity_by_name("ScoreButton")
        self._refresh()
        if btn_entity is not None:
            btn = btn_entity.get_component_by_name("ButtonComponent")
            w = btn._widget_ref if btn is not None else None
            if w is not None:
                try:
                    w.clicked.disconnect()
                except Exception:
                    pass
                w.clicked.connect(self._on_click)

    def _on_click(self):
        self.score += 1
        self._refresh()

    def _refresh(self):
        if self.label is None:
            return
        comp = self.label.get_component_by_name("LabelComponent")
        if comp is None:
            return
        comp.widget_text = f"Score: {self.score}"
        comp.sync_to_widget()

docs.title: 6. ClickSpawner (mouse → entity)
docs.text:
Fields: spawn_name: str = "Pickup", spawn_offset: Vec3 = Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0). Note: Vec3 default field serializes as [x, y, z] and round-trips through _apply_fields_to_instance.

from core.components.transform.tr import Transform


class ClickSpawner:
    spawn_name: str = "Pickup"
    spawn_offset: Vec3 = Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)

    def on_start(self):
        self.scene = self._entity._scene

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0):  # index 0 == MOUSE_LEFT
            e = self.scene.create_entity(str(self.spawn_name))
            t = Transform()
            base = self._entity.transform.position
            off = self.spawn_offset
            if isinstance(off, (list, tuple)):
                off = Vec3(float(off[0]), float(off[1]), float(off[2]))
            t.local_position = Vec3(base.x + off.x, base.y + off.y, base.z + off.z)
            e.add_component(t)
            Logger.info(f"Spawned {e.name} at {t.local_position.to_list()}")

The isinstance guard covers the deserialized-list form of Vec3 fields before the engine converts them (see pitfalls.md: _field_values vs instance attributes).

docs.title: Timers and Delayed Actions
docs.text: Honest summary first: the scripting runtime has no coroutines, no Invoke, no InvokeRepeating, no StartCoroutine, no scheduler. The dispatcher (_call_py) only invokes lifecycle methods; nothing in core/components/scripting, core/ecs, or core/input implements delayed calls (the only invoke_rpc in the codebase is the network RPC path, and the only coroutines are asyncio internals of network transports). The single code-backed timing path is accumulating dt in on_update/on_fixed_update.

docs.title: The pattern
docs.text:
def on_start(self):
    self.timer = 0.0

def on_update(self, dt):
    self.timer += dt
    if self.timer >= self.delay:
        self.timer = 0.0   # or self.timer -= self.delay to avoid drift
        self.fire()

Use on_update for UI/countdown pacing and on_fixed_update for physics-adjacent timing. Pause behavior: render dt is already time-scaled (0 while paused), so on_update timers freeze with the game for free.

docs.title: Cooldown example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
class CooldownShot:
    cooldown: float = 0.5

    def on_start(self):
        self.ready_in = 0.0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if self.ready_in > 0.0:
            self.ready_in -= dt
        if Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0) and self.ready_in <= 0.0:
            self.ready_in = float(self.cooldown)
            Logger.info("bang")

docs.title: Wave spawner example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
from core.components.transform.tr import Transform
from core.maths.math3d import Vec3


class WaveSpawner:
    wave_gap: float = 10.0
    per_wave: int = 4

    def on_start(self):
        self.scene = self._entity._scene
        self.clock = 0.0
        self.wave = 0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        self.clock += dt
        if self.clock >= float(self.wave_gap):
            self.clock -= float(self.wave_gap)
            self.wave += 1
            for i in range(int(self.per_wave)):
                e = self.scene.create_entity(f"Wave{self.wave}_{i}")
                t = Transform()
                t.local_position = Vec3(float(i) * 2.0, 0.0, float(self.wave) * 5.0)
                e.add_component(t)
            Logger.info(f"Wave {self.wave} spawned")

Repeating-pulse variant without drift (timer -= interval keeps long-run cadence even under hitches).

docs.title: Transform Scripting
docs.text: Moving, rotating, and aiming entities from gameplay code. Import path: from core.components.transform.tr import Transform. Vectors: injected Vec3 (no import needed inside behavior scripts).

docs.title: Accessors
docs.text: Member Type / units Notes transform.local_position Vec3, world units Position relative to parent. Assign a Vec3 (or list/tuple/ndarray). transform.local_rotation Quat Local rotation quaternion. transform.local_euler_angles Vec3, degrees Human-friendly rotation; converts via Quat.from_euler/to_euler. transform.local_scale Vec3 Local scale, default (1, 1, 1). transform.position Vec3, world units World position; the setter back-solves local position through the parent inverse. transform.world_matrix Mat4 Full world matrix; settable (goes through the deferred world-target path). transform.forward Vec3 (normalized) −Z of the world matrix. transform.right Vec3 (normalized) +X of the world matrix. transform.up Vec3 (normalized) +Y of the world matrix. transform.set_local_position_xyz(x, y, z) — In-place write, no temp Vec3. transform.set_local_scale_xyz(x, y, z) — In-place write.

docs.title: Motion methods
docs.text:
Signature Behavior transform.translate(delta: Vec3, world_space=False) False (default): adds to local position. True: adds to world position (parent-aware). transform.rotate(euler: Vec3) Multiplies local rotation by a quaternion built from Euler angles in degrees (radians conversion happens inside). transform.look_at(target: Vec3, up=None) Points local −Z…​ forward (-Z convention) at target via (target − position).normalized() + Quat.look_rotation; default up is Vec3.up().

Every mutation marks the transform dirty and flags _physics_dirty, so colliders and render matrices follow on the next flush.

docs.title: Follower example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
class Follower:
    damping: float = 5.0
    height: float = 2.0

    def on_start(self):
        from core.ecs import Entity  # noqa: F401  (annotation only)
        self.target = self._entity._scene.get_entity_by_name("Player")

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if self.target is None:
            return
        t = self._entity.transform
        goal = self.target.transform.position + Vec3(0.0, self.height, 0.0)
        cur = t.position
        k = min(1.0, float(self.damping) * float(dt))
        t.position = cur.lerp(goal, k)
        t.look_at(self.target.transform.position)

Inspector fields: damping (float), height (float). The target is resolved by name to keep the snippet dependency-free; an Entity-typed inspector field works too (see inspector-fields.md).

docs.title: Orbit-camera example (full, runnable)
docs.text:
Demonstrates rotate with degrees, translate in world space, and the −Z forward:

class OrbitCamera:
    radius: float = 8.0
    angular_speed: float = 30.0  # degrees per second
    height: float = 3.0

    def on_start(self):
        self.angle = 0.0
        self.pivot = self._entity._scene.get_entity_by_name("Player")
        self.t = self._entity.transform

    def on_update(self, dt):
        self.angle += float(self.angular_speed) * float(dt)
        import math
        a = math.radians(self.angle)
        cx, cz = 0.0, 0.0
        if self.pivot is not None:
            p = self.pivot.transform.position
            cx, cz = p.x, p.z
        self.t.position = Vec3(
            cx + self.radius * math.cos(a),
            self.height,
            cz + self.radius * math.sin(a),
        )
        look = self.pivot.transform.position if self.pivot is not None else Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        self.t.look_at(look)
        # self.t.forward is now (look - position).normalized()

Keyboard yaw variant showing rotate units explicitly:

class YawControl:
    turn_speed: float = 90.0  # degrees per second

    def on_update(self, dt):
        t = self._entity.transform
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.LEFT):
            t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, self.turn_speed * dt, 0.0))   # degrees!
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.RIGHT):
            t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, -self.turn_speed * dt, 0.0))
        if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W):
            t.translate(t.forward * 5.0 * dt, world_space=True)

docs.title: Honest Scripting Limitations
docs.text: What the engine does not give you — each item verified against the source, with the supported alternative.

docs.title: 1. No Vec3.rotate
docs.text:
Vec3 (core/pyx/_math_vec.pyx) exposes dot, cross, length, length_sq, normalized, to_list, zero, one, up, forward, right — there is no rotate method. Rotating a free vector is Quat.rotate_vec3(v) (same file). Rotating an object is Transform.rotate(euler: Vec3) taking euler degrees (core/components/transform/tr/matrix.py:355).

t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, 90.0 * dt, 0.0))  # yaw 90 deg/sec, NOT t.rotate(vector)

docs.title: 2. _call_py logs errors without a traceback
docs.text:
core/components/scripting/scriptc/hotreload.py:253-260:

def _call_py(self, canonical, *args):
    ...
    try:
        meth(*args)
    except Exception as e:
        Logger.error(f"Script {canonical} error '{self.script_path}': {e}")

Only str(e) is logged — no traceback, no line number. When a callback silently stops working, wrap suspect blocks yourself and log with traceback.format_exc(), or reproduce the logic outside Play mode.

docs.title: 3. Named axes return 0.0 until you DefineAxis
docs.text:
Input.GetAxis(name) (core/input/inpsys/gamepad.py) returns 0.0 for any name missing from cls._state._axes — and mouse axes only after DefineMouseAxis. There are no pre-registered Horizontal/Vertical axes: call Input.DefineAxis("Horizontal", positive=[...], negative=[...], ...) (key codes from KeyCode) before first use, once (e.g. in on_awake).

def on_awake(self):
    Input.DefineAxis("Horizontal", [KeyCode.D], [KeyCode.A])
    Input.DefineAxis("Vertical", [KeyCode.W], [KeyCode.S])

def on_update(self, dt):
    x = Input.GetAxis("Horizontal")  # 0.0 unless defined above

docs.title: 4. AudioSource.on_enable auto-starts playback
docs.text:
core/components/audio/source/component.py:82-84:

def on_enable(self):
    if self.clip_path and not self._playing:
        self.play()

Any disable→enable toggle restarts the clip (in addition to play_on_awake in on_start). on_disable/on_destroy stop the voice. Workaround: keep clip_path empty until you explicitly play(), or gate enables behind your own flag.

docs.title: 5. A neighbouring .pyx triggers a blocking build
docs.text: Hot-reload watches Cython neighbours (ext_sources_changed, unload_ext_modules in hotreload.py); a stale .pyx is rebuilt synchronously by ensure_extensions(plugin_dir, background=False) with a per-file timeout (core/foundation/plugin_cython.py), and loaded via import_extension(package, module, fallback_dir) from the adjacent .pyd/.so. Keep script-side .pyx files small, or ship the prebuilt extension so frames never stall on a compile.

docs.title: 6. Threads: never touch Qt / GL / scene objects from workers
docs.text:
Docks are QTimer-driven widgets and the viewport renders GL on the main Qt thread (vr_dock.py, physviz/plugin.py, plotter_plugin/panel.py). The codebase's own crossing pattern is a QueuedConnection dispatcher — plugins/zarin_mcp/main_thread.py:

def run_on_main_thread(fn, timeout_ms=60000): ...

Compute on worker threads, then marshal all engine/scene/Qt calls through main-thread dispatch. There is no thread-safe scene API.

docs.title: Scripting Patterns Cookbook
docs.text: Copy-paste patterns built only on verified engine APIs: Scene.create_entity / remove_entity / get_entity / get_entity_by_name / get_all_entities (core/ecs/scene.py), Entity.get_component_by_name / set_parent (core/ecs/entity.py), Transform.translate(Vec3) / rotate(Vec3 euler degrees) (core/components/transform/tr/matrix.py), Engine.instance().time_scale (core/engine/eng/loop.py), GuiApi widgets + GuiCanvas (core/gui/api.py), stdlib json.

docs.title: 1. Script-to-script communication through the entity
docs.text:
Scripts see each other via the shared Entity (self._entity is assigned by the script component, core/components/scripting/scriptc/fields.py). No imports of the other script needed.

class Health:
    hp: float = 100.0

    def damage(self, amount):
        self.hp = max(0.0, self.hp - float(amount))
        if self.hp <= 0.0:
            Logger.info(f"{self._entity.name} died")


class DamageDealer:
    amount: float = 10.0
    target_name: str = "Enemy"   # entity NAME, resolved through the scene

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.F):
            scene = self._entity._scene
            target = scene.get_entity_by_name(self.target_name)
            if target is None:
                return
            hp = target.get_component_by_name("Health")  # script components resolve by class name
            if hp is not None and hasattr(hp, "_py_instance") and hp._py_instance is not None:
                hp._py_instance.damage(self.amount)

Same-entity variant: self._entity.get_component_by_name("Health").

docs.title: 2. Timers by accumulating dt
docs.text:
on_update(dt) receives the scaled frame delta; accumulate it — pausing via time_scale then freezes timers for free.

class Blinker:
    interval: float = 1.0
    duration: float = 5.0

    def on_start(self):
        self._t = 0.0
        self._life = 0.0
        self._on = True

    def on_update(self, dt):
        self._t += dt
        self._life += dt
        if self._t >= self.interval:
            self._t = 0.0
            self._on = not self._on
            mr = self._entity.get_component_by_name("MeshRenderer")
            if mr is not None:
                mr.enabled = self._on
        if self._life >= self.duration:
            self._entity._scene.remove_entity(self._entity.id)

docs.title: 3. Object pooling
docs.text:
Pre-create with scene.create_entity(name), park the idle ones far away, recycle by repositioning. Uses only create_entity / get_entity / local_position.

class BulletPool:
    size: int = 20
    speed: float = 20.0

    def on_start(self):
        from core.maths.math3d import Vec3  # injected anyway; import is harmless
        scene = self._entity._scene
        self._free = []
        self._busy = {}  # entity id -> travelled
        for i in range(self.size):
            e = scene.create_entity(f"PooledBullet_{i}")
            e.transform.local_position = Vec3(0.0, -9999.0, 0.0)
            self._free.append(e.id)

    def fire(self, origin):
        if not self._free:
            return
        scene = self._entity._scene
        e = scene.get_entity(self._free.pop(0))
        e.transform.local_position = Vec3(origin.x, origin.y, origin.z)
        self._busy[e.id] = 0.0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        scene = self._entity._scene
        for eid in list(self._busy):
            e = scene.get_entity(eid)
            step = self.speed * dt
            e.transform.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, step))
            self._busy[eid] += step
            if self._busy[eid] > 100.0:  # recycle
                e.transform.local_position = Vec3(0.0, -9999.0, 0.0)
                del self._busy[eid]
                self._free.append(eid)

docs.title: 4. Save / load via JSON (GUI file picker optional)
docs.text:
Persistence is plain json + Transform.local_position / local_rotation. GuiApi.input() (core/gui/api.py) can supply the filename widget on a GuiCanvas.

import json
import os

class SavePoint:
    slot: str = "assets/saves/slot1.json"

    def _data(self):
        scene = self._entity._scene
        out = {}
        for e in scene.get_all_entities():
            t = e.get_component_by_name("Transform")
            if t is not None:
                out[e.name] = {
                    "pos": t.local_position.to_list(),
                    "rot": t.local_rotation.to_list(),
                }
        return out

    def save(self):
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.slot), exist_ok=True)
        with open(self.slot, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(self._data(), f, indent=2)

    def load(self):
        from core.maths.math3d import Vec3, Quat
        with open(self.slot, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        scene = self._entity._scene
        for name, rec in data.items():
            e = scene.get_entity_by_name(name)
            if e is None:
                continue
            t = e.get_component_by_name("Transform")
            if t is not None:
                p, r = rec["pos"], rec["rot"]
                t.local_position = Vec3(p[0], p[1], p[2])
                t.local_rotation = Quat(r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3])

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.F5):
            self.save()
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.F9):
            self.load()

docs.title: 5. Pause via time_scale
docs.text:
Engine.time_scale (loop.py) clamps at 0.0; the loop multiplies the frame delta (dt = raw_dt * self._time_scale), so 0.0 freezes on_update(dt) and physics while input polling continues.

class PauseToggle:
    def on_update(self, dt):
        from core.engine.eng import Engine
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.P):
            eng = Engine.instance()
            eng.time_scale = 0.0 if eng.time_scale > 0.001 else 1.0
            Logger.info(f"time_scale={eng.time_scale}")

docs.title: Tutorials Overview
docs.text:
Three hands-on guides. Read them in order; each builds on the previous one.

Prerequisites (same for all tutorials):

  1. Install dependencies (pip install -r requirements.txt) and open the editor (python main.py). No project setup is required.
  2. Learn the four UI stops used everywhere: Hierarchy panel (scene tree) → Inspector → Add Component (the Add Component dialog) → Inspector field editing → Play to run.
  3. Scripts are created with Project → Create → Python Script (.py) and attached with Inspector → Add Component → Scripts, picking the file in the Script field. Values typed in the Inspector are stored in the scene (.zpes), not in the .py file.

Guides:

  • Rotator and Mover Scripts — spinning and WASD movement with Transform.rotate / translate, Input/KeyCode, Inspector-tuned speed. Start here.
  • Physics Scene — Rigidbody + BoxCollider ground and ball, forces in on_fixed_update, on_collision_enter counting hits.
  • GUI Menu, Prefabs, Audio, Build — ButtonComponent/LabelComponent menu, .zpep reuse, AudioSource.play() on keypress, running python player.py Scene.zpes, standalone build with python build_nuitka.py.

Conventions: self._entity is the owning entity (assigned by the engine before every call); get_component_by_name("...") fetches a sibling component by its registered name ("Transform", "Rigidbody", "AudioSource", "LabelComponent"); rotation input is a Vec3 of degrees applied by Transform.rotate, which is the only rotate in the scripting path — Vec3 itself has no rotate method, only dot, cross, length, normalized, lerp and friends.

docs.title: Tutorial: First Plugin
docs.text:
A working editor plugin in 5 steps: subclass PluginBase, export get_plugin(), react to play/scene hooks, install under plugins/user/. API from core/foundation/plugins/base.py; the example below mirrors plugins/example_plugin.py and the plugins/user/bsp_import/ package layout.

Available hooks: initialize(engine), shutdown(), step(dt) / pre_step(dt), on_viewport_ready(viewport), on_scene_loaded(scene) / on_scene_unloaded(scene), on_project_opened(), on_play_start() / on_play_stop(), on_main_window_ready(main_window). UI helpers: add_menu_item(menu, text, callback, shortcut, icon), add_toolbar_button(text, callback, icon, tooltip), register_dock(title, factory, area, tab_group, icon), register_file_opener(extensions, handler, label), register_component(cls). Config persists as JSON via get_config(key, default) / set_config(key, value).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the package. Folder plugins/user/hello_plugin/ with __init__.py (same layout as plugins/user/bsp_import/: package dir + __init__.py re-export; discovery picks up user-dir packages, warning on name override).
  2. Paste the code below into plugins/user/hello_plugin/__init__.py.
  3. Restart the editor (or reload plugins). The plugin's initialize runs: menu HelloPlugin → Say Hello (Ctrl+Shift+H) and a Hello toolbar button appear.
  4. Open any scene → on_scene_loaded logs the scene name. Press Play → on_play_start logs and resets the frame counter; move around; Stop → on_play_stop increments the persistent counter in config/plugins/HelloPlugin.json.
  5. Extend: add register_dock("Hello", factory, area="left") for a panel, or register_component(MyComp) (must inherit core.ecs.Component) to ship a component with the plugin.

docs.title: Full code — plugins/user/hello_plugin/__init__.py
docs.text:
from core.foundation.plugins import PluginBase
from core.foundation.logger import Logger


class HelloPlugin(PluginBase):
    NAME = "HelloPlugin"
    VERSION = "1.0.0"
    DESCRIPTION = "My first ZarinEngine plugin."
    SYSTEM = False  # user plugin, not engine system

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self._frame = 0

    def initialize(self, engine):
        super().initialize(engine)  # loads config/HelloPlugin.json
        self.add_menu_item("HelloPlugin", "Say Hello",
                           lambda: Logger.info("Hello from HelloPlugin!"),
                           "Ctrl+Shift+H")
        self.add_toolbar_button("Hello",
                                lambda: Logger.info("Hello from toolbar!"),
                                tooltip="Say hello")
        Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Initialized! Counter: {self.get_config('counter', 0)}")

    def on_scene_loaded(self, scene):
        Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Scene loaded: {scene.name}")

    def on_play_start(self):
        Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Play started!")
        self._frame = 0

    def on_play_stop(self):
        Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Play stopped after {self._frame} frames.")
        counter = self.get_config("counter", 0) + 1
        self.set_config("counter", counter)
        Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Run counter saved: {counter}")

    def shutdown(self):
        Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Shutdown.")
        super().shutdown()


def get_plugin():
    return HelloPlugin()

Rules the loader enforces: class attributes NAME / VERSION / DESCRIPTION / SYSTEM; module-level get_plugin() factory returning the instance; super().initialize(engine) first (loads config), super().shutdown() last (saves config, restores patches).

docs.title: Tutorial: First Shader
docs.text:
A custom material shader in 5 steps: .shader file (Properties + GLSL), .zpem material, assignment on MeshRenderer. Syntax from core/assets/matp/shader.py (_SHADER_PROP_RE, _parse_shader_default); material loading from core/assets/matp/materials.py (accepts .mat / .zpem, load_shader_properties requires the .shader extension); slots from core/components/rendering/renderers/mesh_renderer.py and mesh_filter.py.

Property line format: [Attr] _Name("Display Name", Type) = default. Types: Color / Vector → (1, 1, 1, 1); Float / Range(a, b) → number; Int → integer; 2D / Cube → "white" {}. Structure: Shader "Zarin/MyShader" { Properties { … } SubShader { Tags { … } Pass { GLSLPROGRAM … // @FRAGMENT … ENDGLSL } } } (see core/shaders/materials/Unlit.shader).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the shader. Project panel → Create → Shader, save as assets/shaders/pulse.shader, paste the code below. Keep GLSLPROGRAM / // @FRAGMENT / ENDGLSL markers — the extractor splits vertex/fragment there.
  2. Create the material. Create → Material, save as assets/materials/pulse.zpem, paste the JSON below (shader_path + properties; defaults fall back to the Properties block when omitted).
  3. Create the mesh holder. Entity Pulser → Add Component → MeshFilter (Source = <any .obj/.fbx>, e.g. a cube; Mesh = mesh) → Add Component → MeshRenderer.
  4. Assign. In MeshRenderer → Materials → [0] → Material pick assets/materials/pulse.zpem. The Inspector shows _PulseSpeed / _PulseColor from the shader's Properties block.
  5. Press Play. The fragment pulses between albedo and _PulseColor at _PulseSpeed Hz. A Shader path '…' not found, remapped warning means the shader_path is wrong — it resolves against the project root, then the engine root / core/shaders/.

docs.title: Full code — assets/shaders/pulse.shader
docs.text:
Shader "Zarin/Pulse"
{
    Properties
    {
        [MainColor] _BaseColor("Base Color", Color) = (1, 1, 1, 1)
        _PulseColor("Pulse Color", Color) = (1, 0.2, 0.4, 1)
        _PulseSpeed("Pulse Speed", Range(0, 8)) = 2.0
    }

    SubShader
    {
        Tags { "RenderType" = "Opaque" }

        Pass
        {
            GLSLPROGRAM
            #version 430 core
            layout(location = 0) in vec3 in_position;
            layout(location = 1) in vec3 in_normal;
            layout(location = 2) in vec2 in_uv;
            uniform mat4 u_model;
            uniform mat4 u_view;
            uniform mat4 u_proj;
            out vec2 v_uv;
            void main() {
                v_uv = in_uv;
                gl_Position = u_proj * u_view * u_model * vec4(in_position, 1.0);
            }

            // @FRAGMENT

            #version 330 core
            in vec2 v_uv;
            out vec4 frag_color;
            uniform vec4 _BaseColor;
            uniform vec4 _PulseColor;
            uniform float _PulseSpeed;
            uniform float u_time;
            void main() {
                float k = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(6.28318 * _PulseSpeed * u_time);
                frag_color = mix(_BaseColor, _PulseColor, k);
            }
            ENDGLSL
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Tutorial: FPS Controller
docs.text:
A playable first-person character in 6 steps: CharacterController component + linked camera, no custom movement code. Defaults below are the component's own (core/components/physics/character/move.py, jump_slope.py).

Key defaults: walk_speed = 260.0, run_speed = 440.0 (while Shift), crouch_speed = 130.0, jump_power = 300.0, jump_buffer_time = 0.1, coyote_time = 0.1, sensitivity = 5.0 / 5.0 / 5.0, cursor_lock_on_start = True, unlock_key = ESCAPE, camera_fov = 60.0, gravity = 800.0, capsule_radius = 0.5, capsule_height = 2.0, step_height = 0.3 (step offset), max_slope = 45.0 (slope limit), push_strength = 30.0.

Hard-wired keys (get_wish_dir / on_fixed_update): W/A/S/D move, Shift run, Space jump (buffered + coyote time), C crouch, Right mouse aim zoom (aim_fov = 45.0), wheel zoom when scroll_zoom. Mouse look is internal (sensitivity, invert_x/y, mouse_smoothing); there are no pre-made Horizontal/Vertical axes involved.

Requirement: the controller needs the in-process solver — set physics simulation_mode = 'single' (otherwise it logs physics world is not available in-process. Use single-threaded physics mode).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Project physics to single mode. In project config set physics.simulation_mode = 'single' (PhysicsPlugin._get_physics_settings reads the physics.* keys; ensure_single_mode() is the code fallback).
  2. Create the player. Hierarchy → add entity, rename Player. Add Component → CharacterController. Leave Capsule Radius 0.5 / Height 2.0 / Step Height 0.3 / Max Slope 45 for a standard humanoid.
  3. Create the camera. Add entity FPSCamera, add Camera component, drag it onto Player (make it a child). The controller detects the child itself (cam_tr._entity.parent is self._entity) and places it at eye height each frame; or set Camera field (camera_entity_id) to link a free camera.
  4. Ground. Add a large flat entity with a collider (static) at y = 0 so is_character_grounded has something to stand on.
  5. Attach the probe script below to Player for verification output.
  6. Press Play. WASD moves, mouse looks (cursor locked; Esc unlocks), Space jumps, C crouches, Shift sprints. Tune Walk Speed, Jump Power, Max Slope, Step Height live in the Inspector.

docs.title: Full code — fps_probe.py
docs.text:
class FpsProbe:
    def on_awake(self):
        self._cc = self._entity.get_component_by_name("CharacterController")
        self._was_grounded = None

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if self._cc is None:
            return
        grounded = self._cc.is_grounded
        if grounded != self._was_grounded:
            self._was_grounded = grounded
            Logger.info(f"grounded={grounded}")
        if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE) and not grounded:
            v = self._cc.velocity  # Vec3, set from solver each fixed update
            Logger.info(f"jump, speed={v.length():.1f}")

Notes: velocity, is_grounded, is_crouching, fixed_update_count are read-only properties (move.py); get_move_speed() / get_wish_dir() expose the current intent; set_ai_drive(dir, speed) drives the character without keys. resync_character() rebuilds the solver capsule after changing radius/height at runtime.
